title: The Bridge That Was Promised
summary: Across seventy years the Vermont landing of the Lake Champlain Bridge asks what was promised: a pier that would be told on, a brother who would be named, a plaque that would not comfort itself, a warning before the closure, and a sentence that outlives the steel.
endingImplications: If the promise is named as a sentence, the new span cannot launder the wound. If it is named as a span, the county gets to feel finished. Neither replaces Ellis's ending. Both tell that ending whether the shore was honest.

chainStages.title: The Pier and the Pencil
chainStages.summary: Bram Voss has penciled the Vermont pier where the 1929 bridge powders under a thumb. Cal asks Ellis not to make the landing the county's problem before the hay is in.
chainStages.discovery: At low water the chalk dusts off the Vermont abutment if you drag a thumb. Bram is already there with the pencil behind his ear. No one posts a notice.

steps.playerAction: At low water, stand on the Vermont abutment and read Bram's pencil ticks without taking them.
Listen to Cal count the cost in hay and fares before you answer.
Speak the testimony, or keep the season, in front of both brothers.

n_open.text: I didn't paint a picture on this pier. I marked where the concrete powders under the thumb. Press. If you call that a feeling, give me your thumb and then tell my brother why his season matters more than the dust.

choices.text: Press the thumb to the tick and say you will testify this week.
Keep the season. Do not put the ticks into a public sentence.

textVariants.text: Cal is looking at the hay wagons, not the crack. If the living come first, you already know which brother you are about to disappoint, and Bram can see it in how you won't press.

n_mid_br.bridge.testify.text: Then we become the cracked bridge. Fares drop. The cut complains. I will stand in the room with you, and I will not pretend I like you for it. Bram stays off that pier. That is the whole good I can see.

n_end_br.bridge.testify.text: Write it as dust, not as my fear. If they jacket it, I don't owe you a thanks. I owe the concrete a quieter week. The pencil stays in the crack so the next liar can find it.

n_mid_br.bridge.withhold.text: Hay comes in. I will hate the quiet of that more than I hate you, if you are wrong. Bram will go up on it himself when the state finally blinks. Don't tell me you didn't know the order of those two facts.

n_end_br.bridge.withhold.text: The soup is the same either way. I will feed the men who cross. If my older boy falls because this week stayed profitable, I will remember who chose the week. Eat or don't. The log will not say your courage.

branches.summary: Ellis testifies. The pier is jacketed. Bram's death-clock stays the long one.
Ellis keeps the landing's season. Bram dies on the unjacketed repair in 1965.
Ida enters the testimony when Cal cannot.
Ida keeps the season when Cal is gone.
Testimony proceeds from the pencil without Bram.
The season is kept over a dead brother's mark.

rewards.detail: Ellis can describe the 1952 pencil ticks as measurement, not mood.
Cal's landing log will open to this body's hands in a later season.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Rennet dies with the ticks unread in public. The pencil remains in the crack. Cal tells the story as unfinished, and Bram's death follows the withheld year.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: No testimony was given. The pier stays a landing problem. Bram's fall in 1965 is not yet a fact Ellis owned, but the unresolved flag treats the season as broken.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The testimony or the withholding is in the log. The jacket, or its absence, is the county's next fourteen years.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Cal is dead, Ida keeps the kitchen and the log and will not let Bram's pencil become a stranger's performance.

n_open.text: Cal isn't here to count the hay against the crack. I am. The soup rule stands. You can still tell the truth into the log, or you can still be a coward with clean hands. Don't use his absence as a third door.

choices.text: Tell Ida to put the ticks in the log in Cal's absence.
Tell her to keep the week and the soup, and leave the log thin.

n_end_br.bridge.testify.ida.text: Then I write it. I will not write your name as a hero. I will write the dust and the date. Bram can hate me for a week, which is better than the other week.

n_end_br.bridge.withhold.ida.text: Thin logs are how this landing stays fed. I know the price. I will not pretend you invented it. Go, before Bram asks me to be braver than I am.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Bram is already dead, Cal holds the pencil and the scene is grief, not a measurement lesson.

n_open.text: Bram marked it and then he wasn't here to argue. I still have the pencil. If you testify, you testify for a man who can't correct your adjectives. If you don't, the pier remains his unfinished sentence.

choices.text: Testify using only what the pencil still shows.
Leave the unfinished sentence in the crack.

n_end_br.bridge.testify.nobram.text: Then say dust and place. Don't say he was brave. The jacket can happen without a eulogy. I'll stand in the room.

n_end_br.bridge.withhold.nobram.text: Then we're both late. I'll keep the pencil and I won't thank you for the company. The season can have what it wants.

chainStages.endingImplications: Testimony jackets the pier and keeps Bram alive into later seasons. Withholding keeps the summer's crossings and kills him on the repair in 1965. The plaque year and the closure year read this choice.

chainStages.title: Say the Name Before Business
chainStages.summary: Ellis returns as Ada Smollet. Cal is not the young keeper who asked for a delay. If Bram fell, the first word allowed on the abutment is Bram's name. If the pier was jacketed, Cal refuses thanks and demands the exact scar.
chainStages.discovery: The 1966 toll shed is the same shed. Cal does not hail you. He waits to see whether the new face walks to the crack without being shown.

steps.playerAction: Walk to the Vermont crack before you say your name.
Let Cal set the first required sentence.
Leave only after a name, a measurement, or a refusal to pretend you remember.

n_fork.text: Fourteen years of tolls have worn the same bowl-chip in Ida's kitchen and a different man at the rail. Ada's face is irrelevant until it proves it can find the crack.

choices.text: There is no brother on the pier. Go to Cal before you say anything else.
The pier wears a jacket of newer concrete. Cal is not smiling about it.
The pier is unjacketed and Bram is still alive. Nothing was finished.

textVariants.text: The landing is the bond you claimed at creation. Cal sees you choose the crack the way kin do, and he hates the resemblance before he hates the face.

fell_b0.text: Don't introduce yourself. Bram fell off the repair in the gap, on the pier your silence kept unjacketed. Stand on the crack and say Bram Voss. After that you can be Ada or anyone. Before that you are a person wasting the year I have left to hate usefully.

fell_b1.text: I fed you once, or I fed the body before this one. The bowl is chipped in the same place. If his chair is empty, do not fill it with a schoolteacher's sympathy. Say the name or take the bowl outside and leave it.

fell_b2.text: I am not asking you to remember a past life. I am asking you to pay the sentence you owe this abutment. The state jacketed nothing. My brother paid. Your new mouth is not a fresh start. It is a tool. Use it or get off my wood.

choices.text: Say Bram Voss before any other word of business.
Refuse the test. Offer your name instead.

fell_name.text: Again. Bram Voss. That's enough for today. You don't get my thanks and you don't get the log. You get to have said it on the ground where he isn't. Come back when you can be useful without being forgiven.

fell_refuse_name.text: Then we have nothing. Ada Smollet can teach school and stay off my landing. I will not be a lesson in your second chance. Bram stays in my mouth because you wouldn't take him into yours.

jacket_b0.text: They jacketed it. I lost a season of fares and I kept a brother. Bram is alive and angry and not yours to collect. If you remember the pencil, say what the jacket covered, exactly, in inches of dust, or get off my abutment. I don't want your new face coming for thanks.

jacket_b1.text: I am alive. That is not a gift from a stranger. If you know where the ticks were, you stood here when I did, or someone coached you, and I don't care which. Don't make my not-dying into your credential.

jacket_b2.text: Fourteen years of being the man who forced a repair. People still blame the slow season on me. I would do it again and I will not be hugged for it. Say the measurement or admit you only have the story.

choices.text: Name the thumb-wide powder line the jacket covered, nothing sweeter.
Admit you have the story of the jacket and not the inches.

jacket_measure.text: That's the line. You can go. I won't drink with you. The pencil is still in Cal's drawer if the state ever calls the jacket a decoration. Don't you call it one.

jacket_story.text: Then you're a person who heard a kitchen. Kitchens talk. The pier doesn't. I'll keep the fares I lost and the brother I kept, and you can be Ada in the road like anybody. Don't come for a share.

open_b0.text: Somebody started this and died or left. The pencil's still in the crack. I have had fourteen years of almost. If you're here to finish it, finish it today. If you're here to be mysterious, the toll is a dollar and the mystery is extra, and I don't take the extra.

open_b1.text: I've been waiting on a testimony that never arrived. My thumb still finds the powder. I am not a symbol. I am a man who didn't fall yet. That's not the same as safe.

open_b2.text: Ada, or whoever is using that mouth: the hay is in this year. You don't get my old speech about waiting. You get one chance to put the dust on paper before I decide the landing no longer hosts this argument.

choices.text: Finish it. Put the 1952 ticks on paper now.
Leave the argument. Pay the toll and be Ada only.

open_finish.text: Late is a kind of true. I'll take late. Don't look at me like we embraced. Tell them the concrete powders. I'll stay off the top while they work.

open_drop.text: Then the landing is a landing. I'll stop waiting on a sentence. Bram can risk himself like a grown man. You can teach spelling. We won't be each other's proof.

branches.summary: The name is said on the abutment. Cal remains unforgiving and specific.
Ellis refuses the name. Cal closes the landing's confidence.
Ellis proves the memory as a measurement. Bram stays alive and ungrateful.
Ellis cannot prove the ticks. Cal keeps the credit and the cost inside the family.
The unresolved pier is testified in 1966. The mutex moves off unresolved.
Ellis drops the bridge argument. Cal stops waiting.
Ida extracts the hard word in Cal's absence.
Ellis refuses Ida. The landing's confidence stays shut.

rewards.detail: Cal's stance is grief or hardened credit, not a repeated hello.
The landing log gains a 1966 line that matches the life Cal actually had.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies on the abutment, Cal writes 'unfinished' and does not invent the sentence the new face failed to give.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The second meeting breaks. The plaque year will find Cal older and unreconciled.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Whatever Ada said, or refused to say, is the tone of every later Voss scene.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Cal dies before this season's meeting, Ida forces the same first sentence without his logistics. The second life still is not a greeting.

n_open.text: Cal is dead and the crack is not. I will not let a new face skip the hard word. If Bram is gone, you say him. If the jacket is on, you say what it covered. I don't do reunions. I do bowls and names.

choices.text: Say the name or the measurement, whichever the pier demands.
Refuse the word and leave the bowl.

n_end_ida_name.text: That's the word. You can eat. You cannot be comforted. Comfort is how people skip the next true thing.

n_end_ida_skip.text: Then go hungry off my landing. I have buried enough men to know a skipped name when I hear silence.

chainStages.endingImplications: This is Cal's second-life change. Later plaque and closure scenes inherit either a named dead brother or a jacketed pier and a man who spent fourteen years being right in public.

chainStages.title: The Plaque With the Wrong Names
chainStages.summary: Tolls have been gone since 1987. A plaque draft names a contractor and omits a painter who fell. Cal will not attend the unveiling unless the names are fixed. He keeps the log now because kindness failed.
chainStages.discovery: The plaque draft is tacked inside the toll shed that no longer takes tolls. You see it because you duck in out of the lake wind, not because a sign tells you to care.

steps.playerAction: Read the draft aloud, including the missing painter, before anyone makes a speech.
Hear Cal refuse the suit and the ceremony.
Change the draft, bless the comfort, or leave the plaque blank.

n_open.text: They took the tolls off and left the lying to a plaque. A contractor's name is in brass-to-be. The painter who fell is a blank. I will not stand in a suit while they forget him. Fix the names or unveil it to an empty rail. I am done being kind about records.

choices.text: Put the painter's name in and take the contractor off the honor line.
Leave the contractor. Call the blank a mercy.
Strike every name. Leave the plaque blank rather than half-true.

textVariants.text: You kept the season in 1952, and Bram fell off the unjacketed repair before Ada woke. Cal does not narrate it. He puts the plaque draft over the place in the log where Bram's name would have been a fare, not a eulogy. The blank is his brother. If you fix the names, you are late. If you comfort the plaque, you are insulting a fall you could have prevented.

You made them jacket the pier, and Bram lived long enough to be angry about it and then died of ordinary years. Cal will not let the plaque thank a stranger for that. The contractor's brass is already a lie. The painter is the smaller lie. He wants the draft to name the dust, not the mercy, because the mercy cost him a season of fares he has never stopped itemizing.
Names are the whole of your ideal, and Cal knows it. He slides the draft so the blank sits under your hand like a dare, not a courtesy.

n_mid_br.plaque.true.text: I'll copy it clean. Father won't come to the unveiling even then. He thinks ceremonies are how counties wash. The log will have the painter. That's the part I can promise.

n_end_br.plaque.true.text: Good. I still won't wear the suit. If they read it right, the lake can have the rest. Don't you add a sentence about brotherhood. One name. Then stop.

n_mid_br.plaque.comfort.text: Mercy is the word people use when they want the dead to be decorative. I kept this log after kindness failed. You just voted for decoration. Lena will do what the town says. I will not be in the picture.

n_end_br.plaque.comfort.text: I'll file it as written. I won't lie to him at supper and say you were brave. The comfort will look like a bridge from the road. Up close it will look like a gap.

n_mid_br.plaque.blank.text: A blank will make the selectboard furious and my father almost kind. Almost. He'll say a blank is honest and then he'll hate the honesty by Thursday. I can live with Thursday.

n_end_br.plaque.blank.text: Blank is the only sentence I trust this year. If someone later carves a truth, they can earn it. I won't donate my brother's ghost to their brass.

branches.summary: The plaque will name the painter. Cal refuses the ceremony and accepts the sentence.
The plaque keeps the comfortable names. Cal withdraws from the unveiling.
The plaque stays blank. Cal trusts the blank more than a partial honor.
Lena makes the plaque true without Cal.
Lena files a blank rather than counterfeit Cal.

rewards.detail: The plaque draft is settled as truth, comfort, or blank.
Cal in 1994 keeps records because kindness failed, not because he is gentle.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Hannah dies before the draft is touched, Lena files the town's comfort version and Cal does not attend.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: An unresolved plaque becomes whatever the selectboard can afford to engrave.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The chosen plaque-fact survives into the new span.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Cal is dead by this unveiling, Lena holds the draft and will not let the town call absence agreement.

n_open.text: Father is not here to refuse the suit. I am. The blank where the painter should be is still blank. Tell me if I am copying a truth, a comfort, or nothing. I will not guess his virtue for you.

choices.text: Tell Lena to put the painter in and strike the comfort.
Tell her to file a blank and not invent his wish.

n_end_br.plaque.lena_true.text: Then that's the copy. I'll read it without a crowd if I have to. A name doesn't need a suit.

n_end_br.plaque.lena_blank.text: Blank. I can defend a blank at town meeting. I can't defend a guess about a dead man's taste.

chainStages.endingImplications: The names on the eventual plaque are this choice. A blank, a comfort, or a painter. The 2022 reading of the new bridge starts from this sentence.

chainStages.title: The Summer Before the Closure
chainStages.summary: It is 2008. The piers are dusting in a way that matches Bram's old pencil. Ellis, in Chris Dobbs, can force a plain warning at the Vermont landing or protect the last busy summer that feeds the Route 17 stand.
chainStages.discovery: Noah has a hand on the rail and is not performing awe. Lena has the old log open to a page that is not today's. The concrete under the jacket, where the jacket has cracked, powders if you touch it.

steps.playerAction: Press the cracked jacket until it powders and show Lena, not a crowd.
Say whether the summer's traffic is worth a delayed sentence.
Leave a warning in the log or leave the log ordinary.

n_open.text: My father died on this abutment in 2004 looking at a span he opened anyway. If you know something about the piers, this is the dull year to say it. Dull years are the only ones that count. The stand up Route 17 will hate you if you spook August. I will hate you if you don't.

choices.text: Put a plain warning in the log: the piers are dusting again.
Keep August unfrightened. Leave the powder out of the log.

textVariants.text: The log still has the year you would not testify. Lena does not call you a killer. She shows you the cracked jacket and the blank where a warning should have been in 1952, and she says the dull year is the only year that ever counts. Pearl's stand will hate a spooked August. Lena will hate a second silence more, because the first one already took her uncle off this abutment.

The plaque at the landing already names the painter, because you refused the comfort version in 1994. Lena treats that as proof you can be dull in public. She wants the same dullness about the dust under the cracked jacket, not a speech about how honest the family has already been. Honesty in 1994 does not cash a check in 2008. The powder is new.
You spare kind lies, and August is full of them. Lena watches you almost choose the stand's feelings over the powder on your thumb.

n_mid_br.warn.2008.text: People say it's fine because they need it. I pump gas. I hear the need. I don't hear the concrete. If you write it, write it dull. Heroic warnings get ignored on purpose.

n_end_br.warn.2008.text: Dull it is. I'll take it to the meeting on this shore. I won't promise they close anything in time. I will promise they don't get to say nobody told them. Pearl can survive a spooked August. A drop can not.

n_mid_br.season.2008.text: Then you chose the stand and the wages and you also chose to be a person who knew. I won't tattle. I will write, in the margin only I read, that Chris Dobbs touched the dust and shut up. Margins have a history in this county.

n_end_br.season.2008.text: If it closes next year like a trick, I won't look at you for comfort. I'll look at the detour. Just so we're clear before the cones sell out.

branches.summary: The 2008 warning is logged. The closure, when it comes, is not a surprise.
The busy summer is protected. Lena keeps a private margin that Ellis knew.
Noah logs the warning without Lena.
Noah leaves the log ordinary and keeps the grudge.

rewards.detail: Either a public warning or a private margin records what Chris's hands found.
Ellis knows the 1952 disease is back in the concrete.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Chris dies at the rail, the powder is on the thumb of a corpse and Lena will not launder it into a guess.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: No 2008 sentence is logged. The closure arrives like weather.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Warning or protection is the frame for 2009 and for Ivy's later meaning of last.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Lena is dead, Noah holds the log and will not be romantic about a bridge he uses.

n_open.text: Mom's not here to split the difference between a stand and a pier. I will write what you say and I will not add adjectives. Dull or nothing. Those are the choices I inherited.

choices.text: Tell Noah to write that the piers powder, and stop.
Tell him to leave the page ordinary.

n_end_br.warn.noah.text: Written. If they ignore it, that's on them, and I will not add a sentence that makes the ignoring look like fate. If you wanted a speech, you picked the wrong Voss. The log has the dust. The stand can hate us in August. I can live with being hated by a pullout.

n_end_br.season.noah.text: Ordinary. I'll remember you chose it, and I don't have her mercy about remembering. The page stays a page a stranger could trust. The dust stays on your thumb and in my head. If the span drops, don't come to the pump and ask me what we knew.

chainStages.endingImplications: A warning in 2008 makes the 2009 closure a choice the county had. Silence makes it a betrayal. The creemee stand's last summer is the living cost of the warning.

chainStages.title: What the Promise Was
chainStages.summary: The new bridge is up. It is a different span on the same Vermont ground. Lena asks whether the promise was the object or the sentence. The plaque, if any, is already in the world from 1994, and the warning, if any, was 2008.
chainStages.discovery: You are Rowan, standing on the Vermont approach of the replacement span. Traffic works. Noah has the old log and the new plaque side by side on the hood of a truck. Nobody is lost. That is the problem.

steps.playerAction: Read the plaque and the log side by side without a speech.
Say which fact is the promise.
Leave the landing without anointing the new steel, or anoint it in one dull line.

n_open.text: It is a different bridge and the same ground. I will not pretend those are one fact. The closure happened. The new span opened. People want me to feel finished. Tell me if the promise was the span or the sentence. If you don't know, say you don't know. I am too old for your mystery.

choices.text: The promise was the sentence, not the steel.
The promise was that a span would be here, and it is.

textVariants.text: You warned them in the dull year, and the closure still came. Lena will not let the new span turn that warning into a prophecy you get to enjoy. The promise, if it was a sentence, was the sentence you wrote while the stand still had traffic. She wants you to say whether the steel overhead fulfills it or merely replaces the thing that failed after it was told.

You kept August unfrightened, and Lena's private margin says Chris Dobbs touched the dust and shut up. She has the margin on the hood next to the new plaque. She is not offering you a confession booth. She is asking whether a span that works is allowed to be the promise, after you already spent the warning on wages and cones.
You believe the record holds, so Lena puts the log on top of the plaque. She wants to see if your ideal survives a bridge that works.

n_mid_br.promise.sentence.text: Then the log is the bridge and this thing overhead is a tool. I can work a tool. I won't call it a kept vow. Mom wants the word exact. I'm giving you the practical version.

n_end_br.promise.sentence.text: Sentence. I'll write that in the back of the log where vows go to stay unperformed and honest. The steel can carry cars. It doesn't carry Bram, or my father, or you.

n_mid_br.promise.span.text: Then all the names were maintenance. I don't agree. I will still write what you said, because the landing's job is not to win the argument. It is to show what was claimed.

n_end_br.promise.span.text: Span's here. I'm not ungrateful to the engineers. I'm also not going to pretend the old pencil was about commuting. You picked commuting. Own it.

branches.summary: The promise is named as the sentence. The new span is demoted to a tool.
Ellis calls the new span the kept promise. The Vosses record the claim without sharing it.
Noah records the promise as the sentence.
Noah records the promise as the span.

rewards.detail: Ellis has said whether the promise was span or sentence.
Lena writes the claim in the back of the landing log.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies on the approach, Noah writes 'unfinished' and does not pick the prettier noun.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The new bridge stays a bridge. The promise stays unspoken.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The spoken noun, span or sentence, is what later tellings of this shore are allowed to repeat.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Lena is dead, Noah will not invent her noun. He asks once and then writes.

n_open.text: She's not here to be exact for both of us. I need the noun. Span or sentence. If you give me a paragraph I will keep the first noun and throw out the rest. That's the log I can stand.

choices.text: Tell Noah: sentence.
Tell Noah: span.

n_end_br.promise.noah_sentence.text: Sentence. Written. I won't frame it. The truck hood is not an altar.

n_end_br.promise.noah_span.text: Span. Written. Don't ask me to feel finished. I have to open tomorrow.

chainStages.endingImplications: The chain ends by deciding what was promised: a span, a true sentence, or nothing you are willing to anoint. This does not replace the county's ending. It tells the ending which bridge it means.

title: The Orchard Inheritance
summary: The south-block orchard is the silt Ivo sent onto Harrow ground. Maeve's second life is the fourteen years that choice built. Nell inherits trees or a fight. Asa asks whether grafting itself should end.
endingImplications: A stopped row lets the ending of the county be about a place that is finished. A continued row lets the ending admit that skill keeps the wound horticultural. Neither is absolution.

chainStages.title: The Stake in the South Block
chainStages.summary: An iron stake in the third row is not where the flood left the silt. Maeve wants the sentence. Samuel wants the trees without paper. Ellis either tells her Ivo moved it or drives it deeper.
chainStages.discovery: After a rain the south block shows a cleaner line of trunks than the silt would have planted. The stake is cold under your hand before Maeve speaks.

steps.playerAction: Find the stake in the third row and do not pull it yet.
Hear Maeve refuse the story that the creek did this alone.
Tell her the stake was moved, or drive it deeper and leave.

n_open.text: Don't tell me the creek did this by itself. Creeks don't carry iron stakes. Men do. If you are only Rennet the rodman, say so and hold still. If you know whose hand moved it after the silt, use a sentence, not a mood.

choices.text: Tell her Ivo moved the stake. The silt line is Harrow.
Drive the stake deeper and leave the county line looking honest.

textVariants.text: You are bound to this house, so she does not bother with the stranger's version. She puts your hand on the stake as if you already owe the row a confession.

n_mid_br.orchard.truth.text: Then we write it. Not a poem. The row, the year, the hand. Samuel will hate the paper and he will keep the trees. I can live with his hate. I cannot live with a county smile.

n_end_br.orchard.truth.text: All right. It's said. I'll graft under my name and not under a rumor. Don't come back to watch me be grateful. Gratitude is not a crop.

n_mid_br.orchard.hide.text: Good. Paper is how they take a row. You can be a coward for us if you want the nicer word. I won't thank you in front of her. I'll thank you by still having the trees next year.

n_end_br.orchard.hide.text: You just decided I will fight the county without a fact. Remember that when I don't know your next face. The gate is that way. Use it.

branches.summary: Maeve is told the truth. The south block will be named as hers.
The stake is hidden. Maeve is left to fight a lie.
Lottie records the truth in Maeve's absence.
The stake is hidden over Lottie's objection.

rewards.detail: Ellis knows the stake is a moved thing, not a flood relic.
Maeve's stance is either coworker-in-a-debt or enemy-at-the-gate, and it will not reset.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Rennet dies with the stake unsaid. Maeve keeps a rumor and no sentence.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The second life begins with Maeve unsure, not with a greeting.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Truth or concealment is the soil of every later Harrow scene.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Maeve is dead, Lottie still wants the number and will not let Samuel's fear of paper be the only vote.

n_open.text: Maeve isn't here to be fierce about it. I am here to count. The stake is in the wrong row. Tell me the hand that moved it or drive it down and be the kind of man this family already knows.

choices.text: Tell Lottie the hand was Ivo's.
Drive it deeper anyway.

n_end_br.orchard.truth.lottie.text: Then the book gets a row and a year. I'll fight Samuel for the paper. You don't get to call that love. You get to call it accurate.

n_end_br.orchard.hide.lottie.text: Then I have a number I won't write. That is its own lie. Don't ask me to bless it. Go off the row.

chainStages.endingImplications: Truth gives Maeve fourteen years of grafting under her own name. Hiding the stake gives her fourteen years of fighting the county. The second life is that life, not a new hello.

chainStages.title: The Row She Already Lived
chainStages.summary: Ada Smollet meets Maeve inside the life the stake already made. If the truth was told, Maeve asks which of June's trees comes out. If the stake was hidden, Maeve meets the office at the gate and will not let it in. If nothing was finished, she does not know this face.
chainStages.discovery: The south block in 1966 is either labeled in Maeve's hand on the end posts, or it is posted with a county notice she has torn and nailed back up, angry, more than once. You see the posts before you see her.

steps.playerAction: Read the end post before you announce yourself.
Let Maeve speak from the life she has been living, not from your memory of her.
Choose the tree, the trespass, or the first true sentence.

n_fork.text: Maeve is forty-two. The row has had fourteen seasons without your face. Ada's shoes are a schoolteacher's. The posts say whether that matters.

choices.text: Her name is on the end posts. Walk into the row. You are not a stranger here.
A county notice is nailed to the gate, torn, nailed again. Stop at the gate.
The posts are unlabeled. She is pruning and does not look up.

textVariants.text: You spare kind lies, and the row is full of them if the stake was hidden. Maeve watches your mouth soften and trusts it less.

truth_b0.text: You don't get to be a stranger on this row. I spent fourteen years grafting under my own name because someone finally said the silt was ours. Put the knife in the right hand or don't pick it up. June's tree is failing in the third row. It spoils the line. It is also the last thing my sister planted.

truth_b1.text: Mother talks like the row owes her a verdict. I talk like it owes taxes. If you take June's tree out, say so like a person who will still be here when the bill comes. If you keep it, don't call it sacred. Call it a cost.

truth_b2.text: I am not asking the creek. I am asking you, because you are the mouth that made this name legal, whatever face you're wearing. Take June out or keep her and live with a crooked row. Those are the only respects I have left.

choices.text: Take June's tree out. Say it is a cost, not a sacrament.
Keep June's tree and accept the crooked row.

truth_out.text: Then we do it before the sap rises far enough to make us feel holy. Nell will write the loss. I will not cry for you. I already cried in years you didn't attend.

truth_keep.text: Then the tax man and the fungus get a vote forever. I'll note it. Mother will pretend the note is a kindness. It isn't. It's a bill we agreed to.

hidden_b0.text: The county has been in my trees since the stake went quiet. I don't know your face. I know the office in a person's pocket. If you're Ada the teacher, teach somewhere else. If you're the office's new hands, you can read the notice from that side of the gate. You don't come in.

hidden_b1.text: I have counted this row for fourteen years of a fight I didn't choose. If you have the fact we were denied, say it now or stop pretending your silence was ever neutral. I am old. I am not confused about which one of those you are doing.

hidden_b2.text: Trespass, and I will have you walked out and I will be right. Tell the truth from the road, and I may open the latch. Stay charming, and I will remember the charm as another county tool.

choices.text: From the road, say Ivo moved the stake. Do not step in.
Leave the gate shut. Do not add a new charm to her war.

hidden_road.text: Late. Still a fact. I'll take the latch off tomorrow, not tonight. Don't look warmed. Lottie will write it. I will check her numbers because I don't trust relief.

hidden_leave.text: Good. Stay unknown. I have enough known enemies. Nell will inherit a lawsuit and a straight back. If your next face comes with a map, I will know the map before I know you.

unsure_b0.text: If you want apples, the stand is in Addison. If you want a row explained, I don't explain it to people who start with their names. State the tree or go back to the road. I have work that doesn't include your mystery.

unsure_b1.text: She says that to surveyors and to cousins and to God. I'm Nell. If you actually know why the third row is too straight, say it to me, because she will turn it into weather if you let her.

unsure_b2.text: Nell talks too much to strangers. You can still be one. Or you can tell me whose hand moved iron in my silt. I don't promise belief. I promise I will not help you perform it.

choices.text: Tell her Ivo moved it, and that you are late by a death.
Let her call it weather. Leave the row.

unsure_say.text: Late is not innocent. I'll graft under my name starting this week, and I'll spend the next years angry that the week wasn't earlier. Nell, write it. Don't decorate it.

unsure_weather.text: Then she'll call it weather until she dies, and I'll inherit the weather. Thanks for the help. The road is behind you.

branches.summary: June's tree comes out. The row is straight and poorer.
June's tree stays. The inheritance includes a crooked, living cost.
The hidden stake is confessed from the road. The fight turns into a document.
Ellis leaves Maeve's war intact and does not enter.
The unresolved stake is finally spoken. Maeve starts the work late.
Ellis lets the orchard stay unexplained. Nell inherits the weather.
Nell records the stake without Maeve.
Nell keeps the orchard question and Ellis leaves.

rewards.detail: Maeve's second-life stance is a worked life, not a swapped greeting.
The graft knife is either put in your hand or kept on her side of the gate.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies in the row, Maeve finishes the day's grafting alone and does not record a stranger's opinion.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: June's tree stays an argument Nell will have to finish without a sentence from this season.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The tree or the gate is settled enough for the cider year to inherit.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Maeve has died before 1966, which she has not by the default calendar, Nell already holds the knife and will not perform her mother's unfinished greeting.

n_open.text: Mother is not here to make this a test of reverence. I have the knife and the tax bill. If you know the stake, say the stake. If you don't, buy apples in Addison like a person.

choices.text: Tell Nell the stake was moved.
Buy nothing. Leave the bill and the knife with her.

n_end_nt.text: Then I write it without her blessing. That's finer. Blessings muddy the acres.

n_end_nl.text: Good. I have enough helpers who want a feeling. The row will outlast your visit.

chainStages.endingImplications: June's tree kept or removed becomes Nell's inheritance problem. A gate refused becomes Nell's lawsuit. An unrecognized Ada can still choose to speak.

chainStages.title: Cider and the Buyer
chainStages.summary: A broker wants the south block for houses. Maeve is fifty-six and tired. The press is running. Nell can inherit trees or a fight, and those are not the same will.
chainStages.discovery: The cider smell reaches the road before the offer does. Kit Downing's car is pointed at the south block as if the block were already a lot.

steps.playerAction: Stand at the press and read the offer before anyone summarizes it for you.
Hear Maeve separate a lawsuit from an orchard.
Tell Nell which will she is being handed.

n_open.text: Nell can inherit a lawsuit or an orchard. I am too tired to pretend those are the same will. Kit has a number. The number is not a home. Louis, or whoever you are, choose with me, not for me, and don't you dare say the creek would have wanted houses.

choices.text: Tell Nell the will is the trees, and send Kit off the row.
Say the fight has eaten them, and let the block be sold.

textVariants.text: Fourteen years ago you said the stake was moved, and Maeve has spent those years grafting under her own name. She does not thank you for arriving in time to watch a buyer. The silt is already a sentence in this yard. Kit's number is the new threat, not the old secret. Louis, she says, don't you spend the truth we already paid for on a softer noun.

You drove the stake down and left the county line looking honest. Maeve has been poor in her own trees for fourteen years and she still does not have the sentence. She looks at Kit's offer as if it might be the only way to stop bleeding for a lie you protected. If you sell, she says, you will not get to call the hidden stake a mercy twice.
The living come first for you, and the living in this yard are tired. Maeve sees you about to soothe Kit instead of her, and she puts the dipper down so you have to speak without a prop.

n_mid_br.orchard.keep.text: Then I take the taxes and the fungus and June's crookedness if it's still here. Kit can eat his number. Mother gets to be tired without being overruled by a lot line.

n_end_br.orchard.keep.text: I'll tell the buyer the block isn't a lot. I won't tell him you were noble. Noble is how sellers change their minds in August. If you change it, don't call me.

n_mid_br.orchard.sell.text: Then I inherit money and a hole. Don't dress it as mercy to her. She can hear mercy. It sounds like people leaving. Kit, write it so the silt line is at least named in the deed.

n_end_br.orchard.sell.text: Do it before I have to watch another season of being right and poor. I won't move into one of the houses. I'll die on the acre we keep for the sugarhouse, if you leave me that. Leave me that.

branches.summary: Nell keeps the trees. The south block is not sold.
The south block is sold. Maeve keeps the sugarhouse acre only if the deed says so.
Maeve keeps the block without Nell.
The sale proceeds only with the sugarhouse acre reserved.
Nell keeps the orchard after Maeve.
Nell sells with the silt named.

rewards.detail: Nell's inheritance is named as trees or as a sale.
Maeve's tiredness is on the record, not smoothed into dignity.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Louis dies at the press, Kit leaves the offer on the bench and Nell decides alone after the cider is racked.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The offer remains a rumor with a car pointed at the row.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Sale or keeping is the ground Asa walks into, and it is not reopened as a mood.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Nell is dead, Maeve will not let Kit narrate the daughter's absence into a sale.

n_open.text: Nell isn't here to be practical for me. I can still say no. I can still say yes and hate you. Don't use her death as the reason the houses are kind.

choices.text: Tell Maeve to keep the row and send Kit away.
Tell her the sale is allowed, and the sugarhouse acre stays.

n_end_br.orchard.keep.maeve.text: Then the row stays. I'll be tired on it. That's allowed. Kit can find another intervale to flatter.

n_end_br.orchard.sell.maeve.text: Write the acre in. If it isn't in, there is no sale. I will burn the offer before I lose the arch.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Maeve dies before the pressing, Nell refuses to let grief be the broker's lever.

n_open.text: She's dead and the offer got braver. I can smell that. Tell me if I'm keeping trees or selling a hole. Don't tell me what she would have wanted. I heard her when she could talk.

choices.text: Keep the trees.
Sell, and make him write the silt into the deed.

n_end_br.orchard.keep.nonmaeve.text: Trees. I'll pay the bill. Kit can leave before the cider turns.

n_end_br.orchard.sell.nonmaeve.text: He writes it or he doesn't buy it. I'm not handing him a blank pastoral.

chainStages.endingImplications: Sold land ends the graft. Kept land hands Nell the trees and the bill. Asa's later question about stopping depends on whether there is a row left.

chainStages.title: Two Maps in the Attic
chainStages.summary: Maeve died in 1991. Nell has two maps in the attic. One is a kindness. She asks which one Ellis is willing to be hated for, not which one is metaphysically true.
chainStages.discovery: The attic smell is cedar and old apples. Nell has the maps open on the floor because the table is too honest. You climbed because the hatch was already up.

steps.playerAction: Read both maps without saying which feels like Maeve.
Let Nell refuse the question of abstract truth.
Choose the map you will be hated for, and sign nothing you did not read.

n_open.text: There are two maps and one of them is a kindness. I am not asking you which is true. I am asking which one you are willing to be hated for. Mother is three years dead. The attic doesn't care which body you brought. I care which enemy you can stand to make.

choices.text: File the kind map. Accept the peace and the false row.
File the harsh map. Be hated at town meeting.

textVariants.text: Your flaw is signing unread. Nell sees your hand twitch toward the kinder map and puts a boot on it until you have said, aloud, what the legend means.

n_mid_br.maps.kind.text: Then town meeting stays dull and my son inherits a courtesy. I'll hate you a little and I'll sleep. Don't call it what Mother would have wanted. She wanted the fight on Tuesdays and the trees on Wednesdays.

n_end_br.maps.kind.text: I file the kind one. If Asa hates me for it, he can hate a person who chose sleep over a cleaner wound. I won't pretend the row matches the silt.

n_mid_br.maps.harsh.text: Then I'll stand next to you while they call it a haunting or a grudge. I prefer grudge. Grudges have acreage. Bring a coat. The meeting hall is mean in March.

n_end_br.maps.harsh.text: File the harsh one. I'll be hated in my own voice, not in Maeve's. If the bill comes, it comes to this body and the next one can inherit the receipt.

branches.summary: The kind map is filed. Peace is purchased with a false row.
The harsh map is filed. Nell and Ellis accept the grudge.
Asa files the kind map knowing it is false.
Asa files the harsh map and attends the meeting.

rewards.detail: One attic map becomes the filed map.
Ellis knows which enemies the filing makes.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Hannah dies in the attic, Nell files nothing that week and the kind map stays on top because it is lighter.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: Both maps remain in the attic, and Asa inherits the unfinished argument with the dust.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The filed map is what the intervale argues from.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Nell is dead, Asa at twenty-three will not let a stranger pick a parent's kindness for him without saying the cost.

n_open.text: Both maps. I was born in a dry year. Don't give me a flood feeling. Tell me which enemies you can stand, and I'll tell you if I'm willing to share them.

choices.text: Choose the kind map and name the falsehood.
Choose the harsh map and go to the meeting.

n_end_br.maps.asa_kind.text: Kind, and false. I'll file it and I won't thank you. Sleep is a reason. It's not a virtue.

n_end_br.maps.asa_harsh.text: Harsh. I'll go. If they laugh, they laugh at acreage, not at a ghost story. Sit where I can see you.

chainStages.endingImplications: The map Nell files is the one Asa will defend or abandon. A kindness map keeps peace and a false row. The harsh map costs the homestead at town meeting.

chainStages.title: Stop Grafting
chainStages.summary: Maeve and Nell are dead. Asa is good at grafting and asks Rowan, of all people, whether skill is a reason to keep putting lives into a row that already has too many.
chainStages.discovery: The knife is on the ladder, not offered. Asa is already in the third row. He does not call you over. The work is audible.

steps.playerAction: Watch one graft before you speak.
Answer his question about skill without flattering the row.
Leave the knife in his hand or take the day's wood down and stop.

n_open.text: I can graft. I am good at it. I am asking you, of all the mouths that have stood here, whether good at it is a reason to keep doing it to a row that already has too many lives in it. Don't say Maeve. I knew her answer. I am asking for mine.

choices.text: Tell him to stop. Skill is not a reason to continue the row.
Tell him the skill is a way of staying, and to keep the knife.

textVariants.text: June's tree is still in the row, spoiling the line, because someone in your will refused to take it out. Asa has pruned around it his whole working life. He is not asking you to eulogize it. He is asking whether a row that already keeps a dead girl's failure needs another generation of grafts on top of the failure.

The south block is houses now, except the acre the deed kept. Asa grafts on a remnant and is good at it, which embarrasses him. He wants to know if skill on a leftover is a reason, or if the sale already answered the question and the knife is just a habit with a sharp edge.
You think water has its level. Asa points at the silt line, still visible if you know to look, and waits to see if you will use the creek as an excuse to keep cutting.

n_mid_br.orchard.stop.text: Then the knife goes in the house. The trees that are here can finish their own lives. I will feel useless in March. Useless is not the same as wrong. I wanted someone who has worn too many hands to say it.

n_end_br.orchard.stop.text: Stop. Let the row be a place, not a device. If the silt wants a moral it can keep wanting. You don't owe it another scion.

n_mid_br.orchard.continue.text: Then I stay. I won't call it destiny. I'll call it Tuesdays. If the row is a device, it's my device now, and you don't get to be tragic about it from the ladder.

n_end_br.orchard.continue.text: Keep the knife. Do it as work. The moment it becomes a ceremony for the dead, put it down. I'll know if you don't. So will the wood.

branches.summary: Asa stops grafting. The orchard is allowed to be finite.
Asa keeps grafting as work, with a limit against ceremony.
The row stops without Asa.
The knife stays available as work, unsanctified.

rewards.detail: Asa either stops or continues as labor, not as myth.
Ellis has said whether the row should remain a device.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies on the ladder, Asa puts the knife in the house for the rest of the week and decides alone.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The grafting continues by habit, and no one this season said whether habit was a reason.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Stop or continue is visible in whether March has a knife on the ladder.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Asa is dead, Nina Abbott from the line farm will not graft and will not let the row be romanticized by a neighbor's absence.

n_open.text: Asa isn't here to be good at this. I mow the edge and I don't graft. Tell me if the row is a device you're still feeding. I won't feed it. I will tell you if you're being decorative.

choices.text: Say the row should stop being fed.
Say the work can continue if someone wants the Tuesdays.

n_end_br.orchard.stop.nina.text: Then leave the knife. I'll tell whoever inherits the ladder. I won't make it a speech at town meeting.

n_end_br.orchard.go.nina.text: Tuesdays aren't mine. If a Harrow cousin wants them, they can have the knife. I won't sanctify it.

chainStages.endingImplications: If Asa stops, the orchard ceases to be a machine for inheriting the wound. If he continues, the row outlives the household's plates as another way of keeping people. The ending of the county can use either fact.

title: The Choir of Unsent Letters
summary: A sack of letters people paid not to send moves from Sylvia's loft through law, a single tired voice, and a boy who cannot sing. The choir is either the singing or the keeping.
endingImplications: If the letters go public, the ending of the county has strangers holding unsent fear. If they stay kept, the ending has a family cupboard and no performance. Ash, if chosen earlier, means the ending cannot quote them.

chainStages.title: The Sack Above the Feed
chainStages.summary: Sylvia Keene keeps a sack of letters people paid her not to send after the flood. One is in Ivo's hand. She will not sing them. She asks Ellis to deliver one or bind the sack shut.
chainStages.discovery: The grange loft smells like paper and grain. Sylvia has the sack on the choir chair, not hidden. You climbed because the hatch was open and someone was humming without words.

steps.playerAction: Sit in the loft and let her show you the sack without taking a letter yet.
Read the address on Ivo's letter aloud, including who it is not allowed to reach.
Deliver that one by deciding it leaves the loft in a named hand, or bind the whole sack.

n_open.text: They paid me not to send these. That was the whole transaction. If you deliver Ivo's, you break a contract with a dead man's privacy. If you bind them, you obey people who were afraid of their own sentences. I will not sing either choice. Choose, and then help me tie or untie.

choices.text: Take Ivo's letter out. It will be delivered, not sung.
Bind the sack. Do not make an exception for Ivo.

textVariants.text: You cannot leave a thing half shut. Sylvia sees your hands on the sack's neck and says, before you pull, that finishing is also a kind of violence.

n_mid_br.letters.deliver.text: If one letter walks, the grange is a post office I didn't charter. Sylvia, if you let it go, it goes today, not after a rehearsal. I won't have a choir of leaks.

n_end_br.letters.deliver.text: Then it goes to Helen Perch's door and no farther, and you don't get to narrate his tenderness on the step. The rest stay tied. I will hate the exception and keep it.

n_mid_br.letters.bind.text: Then his sentence stays with the others, which is fairer and colder. Albert will be relieved. I am not relieved. I am consistent. Consistency is what they paid for.

n_end_br.letters.bind.text: Good. Grain below, paper above, both tied. If the roof goes I still choose grain. Today the roof is holding. Don't make me a villain for the order of my loves.

branches.summary: One letter is released to Helen. The sack stays bound around the rest.
The sack is bound. No exception is made for Ivo's hand.
Albert releases one letter without Sylvia's pitch.
Albert binds the sack as feed-loft order.

rewards.detail: Ellis knows the unsent sack is a paid contract, not a metaphor waiting in a loft.
The loft either has one letter missing or a knot that later hands must argue with.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rennet dies in the loft, Sylvia reties the sack herself and does not guess which letter the dead hands wanted.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The sack remains an argument for the next body, with no precedent either way.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Delivery or binding is the precedent the later choir inherits.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Sylvia is dead, Albert will not invent her musical reasons. He will choose feed's safety over a romance of paper.

n_open.text: Sylvia isn't here to make this holy. The sack is paper over feed. I can burn the ambiguity by binding it or by letting one letter out and pretending that's order. Tell me which mess you can stand.

choices.text: Let Ivo's letter out and bind the rest.
Bind all of it. No exceptions.

n_end_br.letters.albert_one.text: One exception. I'll walk it to Helen myself so it doesn't become your errand. The rest stay a sack. That's as much choir as I can bear.

n_end_br.letters.albert_bind.text: Tied. If someone calls that cowardice they can carry grain up these stairs and then lecture me.

chainStages.endingImplications: A delivered letter breaks a contract with the sender's fear. A bound sack obeys that fear. The later choir has either a precedent for opening or a precedent for keeping.

chainStages.title: Feed, Law, and Paper
chainStages.summary: The grange wants the loft for feed. Rain is in the forecast of the roof. Walter, now at the post corner, claims undeliverable paper as his by rule. The letters will be rained on, fed over, or seized.
chainStages.discovery: A bucket is already under the east eave. Walter's rule-card is tucked in the sack's string, which means he has been here and not taken it. Yet.

steps.playerAction: Look at the bucket and the rule-card before you take a side.
Hear Walter distinguish a séance with stamps from a delivery.
Leave the letters in the loft or let the post corner claim them.

n_open.text: Undeliverable is not a suggestion. If I start handing these to whoever feels addressed, the corner becomes a séance with stamps. Albert wants the floor for feed. I want the paper in a drawer that has a rule. You don't get to call either of us the villain without picking the rain.

choices.text: Keep them in the loft. Move the feed, not the paper.
Let Walter take them as dead mail under the rule.

textVariants.text: You want the record to hold, so Walter offers you the drawer as if it were a morality. He is watching whether you worship the drawer or the sentences inside it.

n_mid_br.letters.loft.text: Then I stack the grain in the lower bay and I pray the roof. I will resent you in wet weather. I will also not be the man who fed cows on somebody's unsent daughter.

n_end_br.letters.loft.text: The rule stays at the corner and fails here. I'll note that I was refused. Don't lose the sack to a picturesque leak and then come ask me for a miracle.

n_mid_br.letters.drawer.text: Then they are no longer mine to sing or to betray. A drawer is a kind of grave that still has office hours. I will miss the weight. I will not fight you for a sacrament I was paid not to perform.

n_end_br.letters.drawer.text: Drawer. Labeled. Not yours to browse. If a living addressee appears with a face I can document, we'll talk. Feelings are not documentation.

branches.summary: The letters stay a loft choir. The feed moves. Walter is refused.
The post corner takes custody. The letters become dead mail with a rule.
Sylvia keeps the loft without Walter.
Sylvia boxes the letters under Walter's rule.

rewards.detail: Ellis knows the difference between a choir's keeping and a post-corner drawer.
Custody of the unsent letters is either the loft or Walter's rule.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies between bucket and decision, Walter applies the rule because nobody stopped him.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: Custody stays ambiguous and the roof becomes the decider.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Loft or drawer is what Faye later is asked to sing from.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Walter is dead, Sylvia will not pretend the rule died with him. She still asks Ellis to choose rain or paper.

n_open.text: Walter isn't here to be the law. The card is. Albert is the grain. I am the tired pitch. Choose the loft or the idea of a drawer, and don't make me harmonize them.

choices.text: Keep the loft.
Honor the dead man's rule and box them.

n_end_br.letters.syl_loft.text: Loft. I'll move the bucket. I won't promise the roof. I never did.

n_end_br.letters.syl_rule.text: Boxed. I'll label it in his words, not mine. That is the only tribute he would have recognized.

chainStages.endingImplications: If the post corner takes the letters, they become dead mail. If the loft keeps them, they stay a choir's problem. The burn-or-sing year inherits that custody.

chainStages.title: One Voice, Tired
chainStages.summary: The choir is Faye alone. Sylvia is old and says burn them if the voice is tired, sing them if Faye agrees to be used. Faye will not be turned into a crowd.
chainStages.discovery: One chair is set. The others are stacked. Faye is humming a name and stops when the hatch opens, not as a performance, as a person caught working.

steps.playerAction: Listen to Faye stop, and do not ask her to continue for you.
Hear Sylvia's last instruction without smoothing it.
Burn, sing, or refuse to use Faye at all.

n_open.text: I can sing names. I cannot be the choir. If you need a crowd, you are in the wrong year. Sylvia says burn them if I'm tired and sing them if I agree to be used. I am tired. I have not agreed. Don't help her by looking mournful.

choices.text: Ask Faye to sing the roll, and accept if she says no.
Burn them as the mercy Sylvia named for a tired voice.

textVariants.text: One letter already left this loft in 1952, Ivo's, and Sylvia has never forgiven the exception or the relief. Faye knows the sack is no longer intact. She will not let you treat the rest as a choir just because one dead man's page already traveled. If you burn them, you are finishing a breach. If you sing them, you are hiring her voice to a decision someone else started.

The sack was bound and has stayed bound, which Sylvia counts as obedience to people who were afraid. Faye has grown up under a tied neck of paper. She is tired, and the tiredness is not theoretical. A song now would undo a knot the house kept for fourteen years and then some. A fire would agree with the knot and still be a violence she has to watch.
Names aloud are your ideal, and Faye hears it in the way you lean toward the sack. She tells you your ideal is not her consent.

n_mid_br.letters.sing.text: If she sings, she is used, and I will call that the last honest use. If she refuses, you will not recruit me. My pitch is gone. The instruction was hers to accept.

n_end_br.letters.sing.text: I'll sing them once, in this loft, with the chairs stacked. I won't record it. I won't repeat it at a burial unless the burial is a person who asked. After that the sack is sung and still exists. Don't you clap.

n_mid_br.letters.burn.text: Then I don't have to be used. I also don't get to have been brave. I'll carry the stove wood. You can strike the match. If you want it to mean more than heat, keep it to yourself.

n_end_br.letters.burn.text: Burn them. I paid my life not to send them and I am done being their cupboard. Let the grange smell like paper for an hour and then like a grange again.

branches.summary: Faye sings the roll once, unrecorded, and does not become a choir.
The letters are burned. Faye is not used. The roll ends as heat.
Sylvia burns the letters because Faye cannot consent.
The sack waits for a living voice.

rewards.detail: Ellis has heard a single voice refuse to stand in for a choir.
The sack is either sung-once or ash.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Hannah dies before the choice, Faye does not sing and Sylvia does not burn. The sack waits.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: Neither mercy nor performance happens. Ben inherits a damp sack.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Ash or one unrecorded singing is what the attic year is allowed to call a choir.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Faye is dead, Sylvia will not sing the roll herself and will not let Ellis pretend a dead voice agreed.

n_open.text: Faye isn't here to consent. I will not count her absence as a yes. Burn them, or leave them for a person who is actually alive. I will not be that person. My voice is a memory of a voice.

choices.text: Burn them without borrowing Faye.
Leave them for a living person who is not in this loft.

n_end_br.letters.burn.syl.text: Strike it. I'll watch. That's the last work I do for this sack.

n_end_br.letters.leave.syl.text: Then they wait. Waiting is what they were always doing. Don't congratulate us.

chainStages.endingImplications: Burning is a mercy that ends the roll. Singing makes Faye the instrument of other people's unsent lives. Ben's later question about choir-as-keeping starts here.

chainStages.title: The Keeping or the Singing
chainStages.summary: Ben cannot sing. The loft is an attic. He asks whether a choir is the voices or the not-throwing-away. A college-shaped request, carried by Mina's old petition and not by a campus scene, wants the letters public.
chainStages.discovery: Damp has cockled the top envelope. Ben has a pencil behind his ear and no tune. The petition is a photocopy on the stair, weighted with a stone.

steps.playerAction: Read the petition's ask without going anywhere to answer it.
Admit you cannot make Ben into a voice.
Choose public holding or private keeping, and say which word choir means.

n_open.text: I don't have the voice and I don't have the contract. I have damp. Tell me if a choir is the singing or the not-throwing-away. I can only do one of those. The petition wants a reading room. I want to know if handing them over is a delivery Sylvia was paid to prevent.

choices.text: Let them become a public holding. Choir means the words survive.
Keep them private. Choir means not throwing them away.

textVariants.text: The record holding is your temptation, and Ben puts the petition under your hand like a trap made of your own ideal.

n_mid_br.letters.public.text: Then I'm a courier, not a tenor. I'll write the conditions: no one performs them as found poetry without the names attached to the fear that paid for silence. If they won't take conditions, they don't get the sack.

n_end_br.letters.public.text: Public, with the fear attached. If a stranger uses a sentence, they use it knowing someone paid for it not to move. That is the only clean delivery left.

n_mid_br.letters.private.text: Then I am the cupboard. I'll move them out of the damp and I won't learn the tunes. If that's a failure of nerve, it's a specific one. I can live in a specific failure.

n_end_br.letters.private.text: Keep them. A choir that can't sing can still refuse the reading room. Don't call Ben a priest. Call him the person who carried the box upstairs dry.

branches.summary: The letters become a public holding with the paid silence attached as context.
Ben keeps the letters private. The choir is the refusal to discard.
Owen leaves the sack to rot rather than file it.
Owen sends the sack out labeled with its silence.

rewards.detail: Ellis has defined choir as survival of text or as refusal to discard.
The sack's last custody is written as public conditions or as Ben's cupboard.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies on the stair, Ben keeps the sack and the petition both, and decides in a drier month.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The damp continues to be the only editor.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Public or private is the last word on the unsent.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Ben is dead, Owen Perch will not take the sack into the survey office and will not sing.

n_open.text: I'm not a Keene and I'm not a tenor. I came because nobody else would touch a sack that looks like the flood book in a worse mood. I won't take it to the office. Tell me if it rots here or goes to strangers.

choices.text: Let it stay and rot before it becomes the office's.
Send it to strangers with the fear written on the box.

n_end_br.letters.owen_rot.text: Then it rots in Cornwall, not in a drawer I have to defend. I'll tell the grange. I won't tell a story.

n_end_br.letters.owen_public.text: Box labeled with the price of silence. If they treat it as color, that's their dirt. I won't be in the room.

chainStages.endingImplications: Public holding makes the unsent a record strangers can use. Private keeping makes Ben a cupboard. The county's ending can treat unspoken sentences as archive or as a family's unfinished no.

title: The Last Creemee Stand
summary: Lamb's on Route 17 begins as a spelling in an order book, becomes a fight over whether creemee is a place, survives or spends its last summer before the bridge closure, and ends with Ivy deciding what last means.
endingImplications: A rite keeps the pullout as a dated kindness. A book in a kitchen keeps the names without the gravel. A word that left the county cannot be called back by nostalgia. The ending may mention the stand only in the mode this chain earned.

chainStages.title: The Order as Spoken
chainStages.summary: Doris writes the first book of orders at Lamb's. Someone asks for maple-walnut in June, out of season, in a voice that belongs to a dead surveyor and a displaced life. She will not start a legend. She wants a spelling.
chainStages.discovery: The machine is new enough to still smell like the crate it came in. Doris has the book open to a blank line and is not performing nostalgia. A customer has just walked off without repeating the name.

steps.playerAction: Stand at the window and repeat what you heard, slowly, without improving it.
Let Doris refuse both a ghost story and a tidy customer name.
Choose the spelling that goes in the book.

n_open.text: Maple-walnut in June is a silly order. I wrote nothing yet because the person said it like a debt and then left. If I correct the name to something we know, I tidy a stranger. If I don't, I keep a word I can't cash. Speak slower than they did. This is a stand, not a shrine.

choices.text: Enter the name as spoken, even if it was Cress or a miss.
Correct it to a name the stand can say without flinching.

textVariants.text: You are bound to this stand, so Doris does not ask if you care. She turns the book toward you as if your bond already includes her spelling problem.

n_mid_br.creemee.spoken.text: Don't bless the machine while you do it. Write the word and wipe the drip. If the word is wrong, wrong is what the mouth paid for. I'll fix the compressor. I won't fix the customer.

n_end_br.creemee.spoken.text: As spoken. If it was a ghost, the ghost can read. If it was a child mumbling, the child can correct us next June. I won't do either of them the insult of guessing.

n_mid_br.creemee.correct.text: Then we are tidy and we may be liars. I'll take tidy if you say, out loud, that you are choosing the lie. Hugh will pretend he didn't hear. I won't.

n_end_br.creemee.correct.text: Corrected. The machine doesn't care. I care that we can call the order back if they return. A name nobody can pronounce is a lost cone. Write it so a tired person can shout it.

branches.summary: The order book keeps the name as spoken.
The book is corrected into a shoutable name. The debt is smoothed.
Hugh keeps the spoken name.
Hugh corrects the name so it can be yelled.

rewards.detail: Ellis knows the first order was treated as a debt, not a flavor trend.
The order book's first strange line is either literal or corrected.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies at the window, Doris writes 'unreadable' and does not invent a pretty customer.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The line stays blank and the machine still needs wiping.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Spoken or corrected is how Pearl later defends the card.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Doris is dead, Hugh will not found a legend. He will found a line in a book that has to be shouted across a pullout.

n_open.text: She's not here to be delicate about spellings. I need a word I can yell. Give me the messy one or the useful one. Don't give me a eulogy. The drip is real.

choices.text: Give him the messy word.
Give him the shoutable correction.

n_mid_br.creemee.hugh_spoken.text: He writes the messy word the way the mouth paid, pencil blunt, and the drip hits the counter once. He does not bless the machine. He reads the line back wrong, then right, and the right version is still ugly enough to be a person.

n_end_br.creemee.hugh_spoken.text: Messy. I'll learn it by August or I'll hate it by August, and either way the book keeps what was said. Don't come back and sand it into maple-something. The drip is the only memorial this stand is getting today.

n_mid_br.creemee.hugh_corr.text: He prints the shoutable correction in letters a car can hear, and he feels the dirt of it without performing the dirt. The line is short. The machine still knocks. He wipes the drip because wiping is the job, not because the word deserved a ritual.

n_end_br.creemee.hugh_corr.text: Shoutable. I'll feel slightly dirty and the line will be short. That's a machine man's bargain, and I won't dress it up as kindness to the dead. If Doris would have hated it, she can hate it from somewhere that doesn't have to yell across a pullout.

chainStages.endingImplications: The book either keeps the misheard name or corrects it into something the county can digest. Every later fight about the flavor starts from that spelling.

chainStages.title: Place or Product
chainStages.summary: Randy wants the word creemee on a truck that leaves the county. Pearl asks Hannah to write a definition on a card: a creemee is a place, or it is a product. The card is the whole quest.
chainStages.discovery: Randy has a blank card and a truck brochure on the same napkin holder. Pearl has not let him write. The window is open. You are in the way of a cone and a definition.

steps.playerAction: Read the brochure and the blank card before you take the pen.
Write one definition, not a slogan.
Give the card to the person who has to live with the sentence.

n_open.text: Write what a creemee is. If you write product, Randy wins and the word leaves the pullout. If you write place, we stay poor and specific. I don't want a poem. I want a noun I can defend when the dairy man says flavor is portable.

choices.text: Write: a creemee is this place, or it is not the word.
Write: a creemee is a product that can travel.

textVariants.text: The first book still has the messy June line, written as spoken, because Doris refused to tidy a stranger. Pearl puts that line under the blank card. If you write product, you are taking a word she kept ugly on purpose and making it portable. If you write place, you are agreeing with a dead woman's spelling and Randy will say you chose a postcard.

The first line was corrected into something a pullout could shout. Pearl has lived inside that usefulness. She does not pretend it was innocent. The card in front of Hannah is the second correction, the one that decides whether the shouted word can leave the county when the bridge fails. She wants a noun, not a repentance.
You were raised at a pullout, so Pearl does not translate the stakes. She assumes you know a place can be ruined by becoming a flavor on a truck.

n_mid_br.creemee.place.text: Then we die when the bridge does something stupid. A truck is not a betrayal. It's how the flavor doesn't die with the traffic. You're choosing a postcard over a wage. Say that with your whole mouth.

n_end_br.creemee.place.text: Place. I'll tape the card inside the window. If we close, we close as a place that ended, not as a brand that escaped. Randy can be angry and still wipe the machine.

n_mid_br.creemee.product.text: Then say goodbye to the pullout as the owner of the word. I'll keep the window as long as it pays. I won't pretend the card didn't move the soul out of the gravel.

n_end_br.creemee.product.text: Product. I'll still start here. I'm not a villain for wanting October to have a wage if August's bridge fails. Don't frame me. Frame the card.

branches.summary: The word stays a place. The truck does not get it.
The word is allowed to leave the county as a product.
Randy tapes the word as a place against his own plan.
Randy gets the word as a product.

rewards.detail: Ellis has defined creemee as place or product in a sentence Pearl can defend.
The card is taped in the window or carried toward a truck.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Hannah dies before the card is written, Pearl writes 'place' in a small hand and hides it from Randy until morning.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The card stays blank and the brochure stays smug.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Place or product is what Ivy means when she says last.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Pearl is dead, Randy will not forge her noun. He asks for one and agrees to be angry about it in public.

n_open.text: She's not here to make poverty sound like ethics. I still want the word to survive a bridge. Give me the noun. I'll tape whichever you write. I won't pretend I don't have a favorite.

choices.text: Write place, and make him tape it.
Write product.

n_end_br.creemee.randy_place.text: Place. Taped. I'll hate it in August and I'll still have taped it. That's as honest as I get.

n_end_br.creemee.randy_prod.text: Product. I won't gloat in the window. I'll gloat in the truck, later, where you don't have to watch.

chainStages.endingImplications: If the word is a product, it can leave Addison when the bridge fails. If it is a place, the pullout stays poor and specific. Ivy's later meaning of last depends on this card.

chainStages.title: The Wrench and the Summer
chainStages.summary: The last full summer before the bridge's failure. Chris Dobbs's hands hold the wrench the way Christian Dobbs did. Pearl sees it and does not want theology. She wants to know if the machine will be known in October.
chainStages.discovery: The compressor knocks. Pearl says nothing religious. She says the intake is dirty and then she goes still, because the way the brush is held is a dead plan walking around.

steps.playerAction: Clean the intake because the machine asked, before you discuss souls.
Let Pearl name the hands without making you confess a doctrine.
Choose whether October is planned for, or August is protected.

n_open.text: Christian Dobbs is how you hold that wrench. Chris is what the license says. I don't need the theology. I need to know if the wrench is going to be here in October when the traffic isn't. Warn the summer and we become a book. Don't warn it and the till is full and the book is one copy in a drawer that can burn.

choices.text: Copy the order book and plan October. Let August be spooked.
Keep August full. Leave the book as one copy.

textVariants.text: You spare kind lies, and the kind lie this summer is that the bridge is fine. Pearl watches you almost spend Christian's competence on that comfort.

n_mid_br.creemee.warn.text: You just chose a thin September. I can survive thin. I can't survive being the family that knew and sold cones like a dare. Copy the book. Don't copy a speech.

n_end_br.creemee.warn.text: Copied. If the bridge closes, we still know who ordered what, including the silly June debt. The machine will be tended. That's the stay Christian wanted, done without his mouth.

n_mid_br.creemee.till.text: Then the till wins and the drawer can burn and we will have been busy. I'll hate the busy if the road dies. I'll take your choice. I won't take your comfort about it.

n_end_br.creemee.till.text: Full August. If you wanted to be innocent, you missed it when you recognized the wrench and still said nothing useful. Wipe your hands. Customers.

branches.summary: The book is copied and October is planned. The summer is warned.
The till stays full. The order book is not copied.
Randy copies the book for October.
Randy protects August and the single copy.

rewards.detail: Pearl has named the wrench-hold without being given a religion.
Either a second copy of the order book exists, or only the drawer copy.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Chris dies at the machine, Pearl copies the book herself and does not attribute the decision to a corpse.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The compressor is clean and the future is not.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Warned or full is what Ivy stands in when she says last.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Pearl is dead, Randy sees the hands and will not be tender. He still wants a decision about October.

n_open.text: She's gone and the compressor still knocks. You hold the wrench like Christian. I won't cry about that at the window. October or August. Pick. The customers can wait one minute and no more.

choices.text: October. Copy the book.
August. Don't copy it.

n_end_br.creemee.randy_oct.text: Copied. I'll be poor and informed. That's a new personality. Don't get used to it.

n_end_br.creemee.randy_aug.text: August. If we lose the names, we lose them busy. I'll live with the busy.

chainStages.endingImplications: Warning the summer turns the stand toward a book of names. Protecting the till leaves the book uncopied. Christian's displaced want, to stay through October, is either honored or spent.

chainStages.title: What Last Means
chainStages.summary: Ivy is twenty-six at the pullout. Last can mean the order book in her kitchen, or one afternoon with the window open that she will not call a business. She forbids the word brand.
chainStages.discovery: The boards are off one window or they aren't, depending on nothing mystical: on whether she brought a screwdriver. She has the book under her arm. Traffic on the new bridge is a rumor from here, not a view you need.

steps.playerAction: Look at the book and the window before you offer help.
Do not say brand, revival, or content.
Choose the rite or the shut window, and let her keep the noun.

n_open.text: Last can mean the book is in my kitchen, or it can mean I open this window one afternoon and refuse to call it a business. Don't say brand. The word I have is enough or it isn't. Pearl is alive and she told me not to let you make a speech. So don't.

choices.text: Open the window one afternoon. Don't call it a business.
Leave it shut. Last means the book in the kitchen.

textVariants.text: Pearl's card says the word is a place, and the truck never got it. Ivy has inherited a poor specific pullout and a definition she did not write. Last, for her, cannot mean a brand that already lost. It can mean one afternoon at a window, or a book in a kitchen. She will not let you reopen Pearl's noun in order to feel generous about commerce.

The word already left on a truck, because the card said product. Ivy is standing in what stayed: gravel, a machine, a book with a messy or corrected first line. Last cannot call the word back.
