She is deciding what to do with a place after its name has traveled, and she wants that said without the word brand, which she has heard enough of from people who do not wipe the counter.
You want names aloud, so Ivy opens the book to the strange June line and waits to see if you will read it into a ceremony. She will shut the book if you do.

n_mid_br.creemee.rite.text: One afternoon. I'll make the walnut if the cream is honest. I won't pose. If three cars come, three cars come. If none come, Ivy eats the nobody cones and we go home.

n_end_br.creemee.rite.text: Then last means a rite with a limit. I'll write the date in the book and I won't do it next year unless I want to. Wanting is the whole license.

n_mid_br.creemee.shut.text: Then I don't owe the pullout a performance of continuity. The book comes home. If a name in it was a debt, the debt is mine to not collect. That's quieter than you wanted. Good.

n_end_br.creemee.shut.text: Shut. I'm relieved and a little bereaved and I won't mix those up for a photograph. Go on. The new bridge doesn't need us.

branches.summary: The window opens once as a rite. It is not a reopened business.
The stand stays shut. The order book is kept at home.
Pearl holds one rite without Ivy.
Pearl takes the book home.

rewards.detail: Ivy has defined last without a brand.
Either a single dated rite is written in the book, or the book leaves the pullout.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies in the pullout, Ivy takes the book home and does not invent the rite in your name.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The boards stay a question, and Ivy does not let the next season pretend the question was answered by weather.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Rite or kitchen is the last creemee fact the county is allowed.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Ivy is dead, Pearl will not turn her granddaughter into a mascot for reopening. She will still make one choice.

n_open.text: Ivy isn't here to be the young face of a revival. I am old and I still get a vote. One afternoon or the book in the kitchen. Say it plain. I have buried enough Lambs to hate a soft sell.

choices.text: One afternoon.
The book comes home.

n_end_br.creemee.pearl_rite.text: One. I'll do it ugly and correctly. Then I'll stop.

n_end_br.creemee.pearl_book.text: Home. The pullout can grow grass. I'm done feeding it meaning.

chainStages.endingImplications: The chain ends on a definition of last. The county's ending can include a rite, a closed kindness, or a word that already left. It cannot include a franchise montage.

title: The Quarry Workers' Names
summary: Chalk under a Bristol overhang, an unrealized name near powder, a wage for a week Lou did not work, and a closed cut where Gina brings no chalk.
endingImplications: The ending may speak three names, cite a book, or admit the rain. It may not pretend the monument was always the workers.

chainStages.title: Before the Rain
chainStages.summary: Marco chalks cutters' names under the overhang. The village monument lists donors. Rain will take the chalk by evening. Ellis must say whether a mouth or a survey book is the safer place.
chainStages.discovery: You are under the overhang because the first drops hit the road below. The chalk is fresh. Marco does not offer you a tour.

steps.playerAction: Read the chalk before you discuss the monument.
Say whether your mouth or your book will hold the names.
Leave before the rain, having chosen, not having rescued the wall.

n_open.text: Rain takes it by evening. The monument in the village has donors. Donors did not drill. Read now, and then decide if your mouth is safer than your book. I will not clap for either. I will know which one you trust when you're frightened of being wrong.

choices.text: Speak the names at supper. Do not copy them into the book.
Copy them into the survey book before the rain.

textVariants.text: Names aloud are your whole faith, and Marco points at the chalk as if daring your faith to survive a tax man.

n_mid_br.quarry.spoken.text: Then you will say them where the wives can hear, and you will not own them afterward. If you stumble, stumble. A stumbled name is still a wage the monument skipped.

n_end_br.quarry.spoken.text: Mouth, then. I'll sit where I can correct your pronunciation and nothing else. The rain can have the wall. It was always going to.

n_mid_br.quarry.book.text: Then they become a record and a risk. Official names get counted, taxed, argued. You may think you're saving them. You may be hiring them to the county. Write small.

n_end_br.quarry.book.text: If the book lies later, I will say the chalk was first. Remember that you chose durability over privacy. Both are kinds of care. Only one has a clerk.

branches.summary: The names are spoken at supper and not entered in the survey book.
The names enter the survey book and become official.
Elena takes the names to supper and will not let them be prettied into a wage.
Elena allows the book, keeps the blame, and refuses a speech over the soup.

rewards.detail: Ellis has read the overhang before the rain and chosen mouth or book.
Either a supper roll or a survey page holds the cutters.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rennet dies under the overhang, the rain takes the chalk and Marco does not invent the speech.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The chalked names stay on the overhang until weather takes them, and no supper and no book receives them.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Mouth or book is the method Gina later trusts or resents.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Marco is dead, Elena still has the supper and will not let a surveyor sentimentalize the dust.

n_open.text: He's not here to be modest about the chalk. I am here to feed the people who drilled. Speak them at the table or write them where a clerk can hurt them. Don't do both and call it thorough.

choices.text: Speak them at the table.
Write them small in the book.

n_mid_br.quarry.elena_sp.text: She sets spoons as if the spoons were the roll. She will not let you stand to make it a speech. Sit, she says, and say the first name wrong if you must, then let the table correct you. The monument in the village can keep its donors. This room keeps the men who drilled.

n_end_br.quarry.elena_sp.text: Table. I'll correct you if you pretty them. Pretty is not a wage, and a wage is what the chalk was doing before the rain. You don't get to own the names after dessert. You get to have been heard by the people who packed the lunches.

n_mid_br.quarry.elena_bk.text: She watches the letters stay smaller than the donors' names on the village stone. She does not bless the page. She wants the pen visible, so later, if a clerk hurts a cutter with this list, the hand is not a rumor.

n_end_br.quarry.elena_bk.text: Small. If the county misuses them, I'll know who handed them the pen, and I will say it at supper without your poetry to soften it. Durability is a kind of care. It is also how a man becomes a line item. You picked the line item. Eat, and don't explain.

chainStages.endingImplications: Spoken names stay oral and fragile. Names copied into the survey book become official and taxable. The monument year inherits that choice.

chainStages.title: The Name That Never Worked
chainStages.summary: A name on the wall belongs to a man who never drew a wage: an unrealized life chalked as if asleep. Vito wants it scrubbed before it makes a powder man hesitate. Elena wants it left.
chainStages.discovery: The name is lower than the others, in a hand that isn't Marco's. Vito has a wet rag and has not used it. That restraint is the scene.

steps.playerAction: Read the unrealized name without laughing.
Hear Vito's safety sentence and Elena's lesson sentence as different jobs.
Scrub it or leave it, and do not call the choice folklore.

n_open.text: A name that never worked a shift is a story. A story on the wall by the powder is a way for a tired man to hesitate. Hesitation is how you lose a hand. I am not being poetic. Elena wants the lesson of leaving it. I want my hands. Pick a lesson you can bury someone with.

choices.text: Scrub the unrealized name. Safety outranks the lesson.
Leave the name. Move the powder talk farther from the wall.

textVariants.text: The living come first, and Vito is the living man with the rag. He expects your ideal to take his side and is ready to despise you if it does too easily.

n_mid_br.quarry.scrub.text: Then the cut learns that we permit no ghosts except the ones that had timecards. I will set a place at supper anyway. You don't get to forbid a plate by cleaning a wall.

n_end_br.quarry.scrub.text: Scrubbed. I'll sleep. If you tell this as a haunting later, leave my hands out of your tone. They were the point.

n_mid_br.quarry.leave.text: Then I move the briefing, not the chalk. That's a compromise that still risks a glance. I'll take it if you stand there when I tell the men why the rag stayed dry.

n_end_br.quarry.leave.text: Left. A name that never worked still changes how a man stands. That is not nothing. Don't worship it. Don't wipe it.

branches.summary: The unrealized name is scrubbed. Elena keeps a plate anyway.
The name stays. The powder briefing moves.
Elena scrubs the unrealized name in Vito's absence and keeps the clean spot ugly.
The name stays, the briefing moves, and Elena forbids turning the chalk into a tour.

rewards.detail: Ellis has treated an unrealized name as a safety problem and a lesson, not a jump-scare.
The wall is either scrubbed or deliberately left, and the supper plate follows Elena either way.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies before the rag moves, Vito scrubs it. He will not risk hands for an unfinished debate.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The unrealized name remains a damp argument on the wall, and nobody this season scrubbed it or protected it.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Scrubbed or left is how Gina understands chalk that lies.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Vito is dead, Elena will not pretend his fear of hesitation was superstition. She still wants a choice.

n_open.text: He's dead and the rag is still here, which is its own accusation. Leave the name or finish his gesture. Don't make me eulogize a safety rule.

choices.text: Finish his gesture. Scrub it.
Leave it and move the briefing.

n_mid_br.quarry.elena_scrub.text: The rag is his and she uses it like a tool, not like a relic. The unrealized name comes off in three passes. She does not look at you while she does it. The clean spot is uglier than the chalk was.

n_end_br.quarry.elena_scrub.text: Scrubbed. I'll hate the clean spot and I'll eat. Both. A tired man doesn't get to lose a hand so this wall can be a lesson. If you tell it later as a haunting, leave his hands out of your tone. They were the point, and they are gone.

n_mid_br.quarry.elena_leave.text: She takes the powder talk ten yards down the cut, away from the chalk, and makes the men face her instead of the name. The name stays. The briefing becomes a procedure with a distance in it. She will not call the distance grief.

n_end_br.quarry.elena_leave.text: Left. The briefing moves. His fear gets a procedure instead of a eulogy, which is the only honor I can cook. Don't you come back up here to read the chalk to strangers. The men who work this face already know what it costs to look at it.

chainStages.endingImplications: Scrubbing teaches the cut that only jokes are permitted as ghosts. Leaving it teaches hesitation near powder. Both lessons are real.

chainStages.title: The Envelope for a Week Not Worked
chainStages.summary: Louis Pell's body is from this cut. Gina offers an envelope for a week Lou was going to leave and did not work, because Ellis is in the body. Taking it makes the book match a life already gone.
chainStages.discovery: Envelope day. The pot is salted. Gina does not hand you the envelope. She sets it on the rock where Lou would have refused it.

steps.playerAction: Do not pick up the envelope until she has said whose week it is.
Answer as Ellis, not as a man collecting a check he earned.
Leave the envelope on the rock or in your pocket, and say which life it pays.

n_open.text: The envelope has this body's week on it. You didn't drill. The man who would have left on the bus isn't here because you are. I won't pretend that's payroll. I'm asking you not to cash a ghost. Lou's note said the pot needs salt, not a speech. The pot is salted. The speech is your problem.

choices.text: Refuse the envelope. Leave it on the rock.
Take it so the book matches, and say you know it is wrong.

textVariants.text: You sign unread. Gina puts the envelope under your hand and will not let you sign it until you have said Lou's name without flinching into a signature.

n_mid_br.quarry.refuse_wage.text: Then the week shows a hole. I prefer a hole to a haunted wage. I'll tell Paulette's people, when they're old enough to care, that somebody once didn't cash a ghost. That may be the whole monument.

n_end_br.quarry.refuse_wage.text: The hole stays. I won't be paid for a departure I interrupted. If the pot needs salt tomorrow, that's a living task, not a debt to Lou.

n_mid_br.quarry.take_wage.text: Then say the wrongness while you take it. If you take it silently, you're a thief with a local face. If you take it aloud, you're a record that chose neatness. I know which one I can forgive. Barely.

n_end_br.quarry.take_wage.text: I take it and I say it's Lou's week, not mine. The book will look calm. The rock will remember the sentence. Don't ask the book to.

branches.summary: Ellis refuses Lou's unworked wage. The books show a hole.
The wage is taken aloud as a lie the book wants. Gina hears the confession.
Elena leaves the false wage on the rock and salts the pot without turning soup into a verdict.
The false wage is confessed onto the flap, then taken, and Elena refuses to make the pot an accomplice.

rewards.detail: Ellis has faced Lou's unworked week as payroll, not destiny.
The week's envelope is either a hole or a confessed false calm.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Louis dies on envelope day, Gina tears the envelope and does not deposit a dead argument.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The envelope sits until someone practical files it.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Refusal or confession is what the monument list later cannot pretend was simple.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Paulette is a child in 1980 and cannot surrogate. Use Elena, alive until 1984.

n_open.text: Gina isn't here to be precise about ghosts and payroll. I am old and I still know a false wage. Take it and confess, or leave it. Don't eat the soup as if the soup were a verdict.

choices.text: Leave the envelope.
Take it and say the lie.

n_mid_br.quarry.elena_refuse.text: She puts the envelope on the rock where the pay table used to be and weights it with a spoon so the wind doesn't make it look like a decision. Nobody opens it. The pot gets salt. That is the whole ceremony she is willing to run.

n_end_br.quarry.elena_refuse.text: Left. I'll salt the pot. That's a complete day's ethics. You don't get to eat the soup as if the soup agreed with you. Lou's week stays unworked, and the envelope stays a rectangle of paper we were smart enough not to cash.

n_mid_br.quarry.elena_take.text: She makes you say, before the envelope moves, that the week was not drilled. She writes that sentence on the flap in a hand that is not trying to be beautiful. Then she lets you take it. The ugliness is the point of letting you.

n_end_br.quarry.elena_take.text: Said. Now it's ugly and filed. Ugly is better than sweet, and sweet is how a ghost gets a payday. If a clerk asks me, I will not protect you. I will protect the sentence on the flap. Eat if you're hungry. Don't thank the pot.

chainStages.endingImplications: Taking the wage launders a displacement into payroll. Refusing it leaves a hole in the week that the books will call absence. Paulette's later refusal of blanks starts from this honesty.

chainStages.title: No Chalk
chainStages.summary: The cut is closed. Leo has gone. Gina brings Rowan and does not bring chalk. She asks if a name that only works a shift in a mouth still works.
chainStages.discovery: The overhang is darker without fresh chalk. Gina's hands are empty on purpose. You notice the emptiness before she explains it.

steps.playerAction: Notice she brought no chalk before you offer to find some.
Do not offer a monument as a comfort.
Answer whether a spoken name still works a shift.

n_open.text: I didn't bring chalk. Say them or don't. A name that works a shift only in a mouth is still doing something, or it isn't, and I want to know which you believe when nobody is cutting stone. Leo left for a shop. The dust was the reason. Don't make him a symbol on top of this.

choices.text: Say three names. Claim the mouth is a shift.
Say the mouth is not enough. The loss stands.

textVariants.text: In 1952 the names were spoken at supper and kept out of the book, and the rain took the chalk as everyone agreed it would. Gina has had decades of mouths and no clerk. She did not bring chalk because chalk is how that first choice gets counterfeited into a monument. If you say three names, you are continuing a supper. If you say the mouth is not enough, you are admitting the rain won.

The survey book still has the cutters, because you copied them before the rain. Gina has watched that page get cited, taxed, and misread. She did not bring chalk. She wants to know if you still believe a mouth can do a shift, now that the official version has had seventy years to become the wrong list. The book is not in her hand. The doubt is.
Your ideal is being examined in an empty cut. Gina will know if you romance the silence.

n_mid_br.quarry.oral.text: Then say them and stop at three. A flood of names is a performance. Three is a shift. I will not correct you unless you pretty them.

n_end_br.quarry.oral.text: Three, and no more. If that's labor, it's the labor I have. The stone doesn't have to agree.

n_mid_br.quarry.not_enough.text: Then we agree the rain won something. I can live in that. I can't live in a speech that says we didn't lose the wall. Thank you for the bleakness. It's accurate.

n_end_br.quarry.not_enough.text: Not enough. I won't decorate the closed cut. The names that were copied, if any, are paper. The rest are weather.

branches.summary: Three names are spoken. Gina accepts a short shift of the mouth.
Ellis admits oral memory is not enough. The loss stays a loss.
Paulette allows three names she chooses, then closes the jar and refuses an encore.
Paulette leaves the jar shut and lets the loss stay unnamed.

rewards.detail: Gina and Ellis have tested whether speech replaces stone.
The closed cut is either a short oral shift or an admitted loss.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies in the cut, Gina says three names once and goes home. She does not found a rite.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The overhang stays empty of a decision, and the closed cut does not grow a monument by silence.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Oral or admitted loss is the quarry's last method.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Gina is dead, Paulette will not chalk and will not let a blank envelope sneak back as mourning.

n_open.text: I kept the jar. I didn't keep the job. If you need a witness that we stopped pretending blanks were kindness, I'm the witness. I won't sing. Say if the mouth is enough.

choices.text: The mouth is enough for three names.
The mouth is not enough.

n_mid_br.quarry.paulette_oral.text: She opens the jar and does not pass it around. Three names, she says, and you will not pick the ones that sound best in the wind. She picks the ones whose envelopes she refused to counterfeit. Then she closes the jar on the rest.

n_end_br.quarry.paulette_oral.text: Three. Then we stop. I don't do encores for the dead, and I don't do a soft list for the state. The mouth did a shift. The jar stays closed. If you wanted a monument, you should have brought a chisel and a worse conscience.

n_mid_br.quarry.paulette_loss.text: She does not open the jar at all. The closed cut gets the weather and nothing else. She says the loss out loud once, without names, so nobody can steal a syllable for a plaque.

n_end_br.quarry.paulette_loss.text: Good. Accuracy. I'll keep the jar closed, and I will not let a pretty failure count as remembering. The names that were copied, if any, are paper. The rest are weather. I can live in that. I could not live in a song.

chainStages.endingImplications: If oral names are enough, the ending can speak the cutters without stone. If they are not, the ending has to admit a loss the rain finished.

title: The Animal That Remembers
summary: Queen, a snapping turtle notched by Ivo, forces choices about hay, hurt, numbers, and whether her story is county or family. She is never a judge.
endingImplications: The ending may mention Queen only at the scale chosen: a plain public note or a shrinking kitchen story. It may not make her the Vein's priest.

chainStages.title: The Log and the Mower
chainStages.summary: Hada shows Ellis the log where Queen suns. The body may know Ivo's whistle. Earl wants the turtle moved before hay equipment. Queen is an animal, not a magistrate.
chainStages.discovery: The log is warm. Queen is on it, ugly and specific. Hada does not call you over with wonder. She says the mower is coming at noon.

steps.playerAction: Stand where Hada tells you, not closer.
Decide whether the whistle is allowed to happen.
Move Queen or stand the mower off, and say which loss you take.

n_open.text: She comes for the grease smell and a whistle I will not do, because it isn't mine. If your mouth knows it, that tells me something I don't want. It doesn't make her yours. Earl will lose a cutting or lose a turtle. Tell me if those are equal to you, then help me move the mower or the animal.

choices.text: Move her. Accept she may not find this log again.
Stand the mower off. Lose the cutting. Do not whistle.

textVariants.text: You put the living first. Hada waits to see if you mean the turtle, the hay crew, or only the people you already like.

n_mid_br.animal.move.text: Then we do it slow and we don't pretend it's a parade. If she comes back, she comes back. If she doesn't, I still have a cutting and you still have a story you should be careful with.

n_end_br.animal.move.text: Moved. I won't whistle. If your mouth did it anyway, I heard. We'll both live with what the marsh does next, which is not a judgment.

n_mid_br.animal.mower.text: A cutting is money. I'm not holy about money and I'm not holy about turtles. I'll stand the mower off because you asked in a sentence, not a poem. Don't make it a habit.

n_end_br.animal.mower.text: The log stays hers for today. You didn't whistle. That's the kinder data. I still don't know why your eyes knew the grease.

branches.summary: Queen is moved. The whistle happens and Hada hears it.
The mower stands off. Ellis refuses the whistle. A cutting is lost.
Earl moves Queen without the whistle and refuses to wait for a recognition.
Earl stands the mower off, resents the bill, and forbids a whistle on the way out.

rewards.detail: Hada has shown Queen as a specific animal with a log, not a spirit.
Either the turtle was moved or a cutting was refused.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rennet dies at the marsh, Earl mows and Hada does not forgive the unfinished choice by inventing a gentler one.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The mower comes at noon without a decision.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Moved or spared, the log's story reaches Hada's later hurt.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Hada is dead, Earl will not perform tenderness. He will still not pretend the turtle is a god.

n_open.text: She's not here to love it properly. I have a mower and a log. Move the animal or stand the machine off. I don't do whistles. Don't ask me to.

choices.text: Move the turtle.
Stand the mower off.

n_mid_br.animal.earl_move.text: He lifts her the way you lift a thing that can take a finger, not the way you lift a symbol. The log is left for the mower. He does not whistle. He walks her to the grass and sets her down facing the water she already knew.

n_end_br.animal.earl_move.text: Moved. If she doesn't come back, that's a fact, not a curse, and I won't let you rewrite the fact if the hay comes in clean. You helped. That's all. Don't stand there waiting to be recognized by an animal that has work to do.

n_mid_br.animal.earl_mower.text: He kills the engine and the marsh gets loud in the way machines pretend it isn't. The log stays hers. He looks at the uncut strip and already hears the bill. He does not ask you to feel the bill with him.

n_end_br.animal.earl_mower.text: Off. I'll feel the cutting in the bill and I won't write a poem about it. You can go. If you whistle at her on your way out, I'll know the help was for you and not for the hay. Don't.

chainStages.endingImplications: Moving Queen may lose her the log. Standing the mower off loses a cutting. Whistling tells Hada something she does not want.

chainStages.title: She Walks Past the Boot
chainStages.summary: Queen comes to Ada's new body and not to Hada. A man wants the turtle for a fair display in Middlebury. The scene is Hada's hurt, not a reunion.
chainStages.discovery: Hada is already at the log with her boot turned out, the way you stand when you expect an animal to come to you. Queen is on the bank, pointed wrong.

steps.playerAction: Do not step between Hada and the turtle to prove anything.
Hear her say she will be decent and not cheerful.
Refuse the fair display, or allow it and stay to carry the consequence.

n_open.text: I have fed this marsh attention for thirty years. She walked past my boot toward you. I am going to be decent about it. I am not going to be cheerful. There is also a man who wants her in a tank at a fair so people can say old. I want you to be useful about the tank, since you have been so magnetic about the rest.

choices.text: Refuse the fair. Let Hada be the one who says no.
Allow the display. Stay and say what it costs her.

textVariants.text: You arrived unbound, and Hada says that figures: even the turtle picked a person who doesn't stay attached to a house.

n_mid_br.animal.no_fair.text: Then I say no, and you don't get to be the mercy. You can stand there and be the reason she walked wrong, and I will still be decent. Decency is not friendship.

n_end_br.animal.no_fair.text: No tank. If she comes to me, I won't call it recognition out loud in front of you. You had the years. I had a whistle I didn't earn.

n_mid_br.animal.fair.text: Then you say, in front of me, that you are taking her attention and then lending her to a crowd. I want the sentence. I don't want your guilt face. Guilt faces are how people leave early.

n_end_br.animal.fair.text: I'm allowing the tank and I'm saying it takes her off your log and puts her in a story that isn't yours. If that's theft, it's theft. I won't do it prettily.

branches.summary: The fair is refused. Hada keeps her hurt and her decency.
Queen may be shown. Ellis states the cost to Hada instead of sneaking off.
Earl refuses the fair in public and will not let the refusal be softened.
Earl allows the display, assigns the shame, and bans the ribbon from the barn.

rewards.detail: Hada's hurt is on the record as decency without cheer.
The fair tank is refused or explicitly allowed.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies at the bank, Hada tells the fair man no herself and does not mention you.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The fair's tank remains an offer nobody accepted or refused, and Queen is not displayed by default.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Refused or allowed, Hada's uncheerfulness persists into Lula's science.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Hada is dead, Earl will refuse wonder and still have an opinion about a tank.

n_open.text: She's dead and the turtle still has bad manners. A man wants a tank. I want the marsh not to become a booth. Say no or say yes and pay the embarrassment yourself.

choices.text: No tank.
Yes, and you carry the embarrassment.

n_mid_br.animal.earl_no.text: He says no to the man with the tank before you have finished being delicate about it. The man leaves the offer on the grass like a insult and Earl does not pick it up. Queen stays where she is, which is not a performance.

n_end_br.animal.earl_no.text: No. I'll be rude if I have to. Rudeness is cheaper than a booth, and a booth is how a marsh becomes a story people visit instead of a place that floods. You don't get to soften it on the way back to the road.

n_mid_br.animal.earl_yes.text: He doesn't help load anything. He tells the man the hours, the shade, and the fact that she bites. Then he looks at you until you understand the ribbon, if there is one, comes back to your hands and not to his barn.

n_end_br.animal.earl_yes.text: Then it's your embarrassment. Don't bring the ribbon back here, and don't bring a story about how educational it was. I still live next to the log. You get to live next to the tank for a weekend. That was the trade. Honor it by leaving.

chainStages.endingImplications: Hada's hurt is a second-life fact about attention, not about Ellis being chosen by magic. The display is refused or allowed as a separate harm.

chainStages.title: Notch or Number
chainStages.summary: Lula is eighteen and already arguing with a permit. Vernon hunts to the log. A notch is a family story. A band is a story a stranger can read. Queen arrives because Ellis is there, and that is inconvenient for everyone.
chainStages.discovery: Lula has the pamphlet folded too many times. Vernon has a blind in mind. Queen is half in the water, not performing arrival.

steps.playerAction: Let Lula speak before Vernon does, or notice that you didn't.
Do not whistle to settle the argument.
Choose notch or band, and say who the story is for.

n_open.text: A notch is a story only your family can read. A band is a story the next stranger can read. I want the stranger to be careful. I know what careful has cost this creek. Vernon wants a blind up to the log. I want you not to whistle just to win.

choices.text: Leave the notch. No band. Vernon moves the blind.
Band her. Let the next stranger read the care.

textVariants.text: You were raised at a desk, so Lula assumes you love numbers and asks you to disappoint her assumption on purpose.

n_mid_br.animal.notch.text: Then the blind moves and I mutter for a season. A number would have made me hesitate, and hesitation isn't always holy. I'll hesitate anyway if she looks at me. Don't count on it.

n_end_br.animal.notch.text: No band. I'll be called superstitious by people who like their care in metal. I can stand that better than I can stand fitting her to a form before I know what the form is for.

n_mid_br.animal.band.text: Then I do it myself, small, and I tell Vernon the number is not an invitation. If the band becomes a brochure later, that's on me. You don't get to be shocked.

n_end_br.animal.band.text: Numbered. I'll still hunt the legal side. I won't pretend a tag makes her a pet or a prohibition. Tags are how men avoid thinking. I'll try to think anyway.

branches.summary: Queen stays unbanded. The blind moves. Lula accepts the superstition charge.
Queen is banded by Lula, with the risk of management stated.
Vernon keeps Queen unnumbered and moves his blind without making it wisdom.
Vernon allows a band, hates the pamphlet, and makes Ellis keep the responsibility for the number.

rewards.detail: Lula has separated family legibility from state legibility.
Queen is either notched only or also numbered.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Louis dies at the creek, Lula does not band Queen that day and Vernon does not get a speech.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The banding pamphlet stays folded in a pocket, and Queen is neither numbered nor explicitly spared.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Band or notch is what the permit year argues with.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Lula is dead, Vernon will not become a biologist. He will still refuse a brochure.

n_open.text: She's not here to want the stranger careful. I hunt. I don't want a brochure with my family's turtle on it. Band or don't. I'll hate both a little.

choices.text: No band.
Band her anyway.

n_mid_br.animal.vernon_notch.text: He moves the blind back from the log without announcing it as a virtue. The notch stays a family mark. He complains about the lost angle the whole time he works, which is how he keeps the choice from becoming holy.

n_end_br.animal.vernon_notch.text: No band. Good. I'll move the blind and complain in private, and the private is part of the decision. A stranger doesn't get a number. You don't get a story about how wise the creek is. She's a turtle. I'm a man who hunts and just gave up a shot.

n_mid_br.animal.vernon_band.text: He holds her while the band goes on and he hates the efficiency of it. The number is readable. He will not pose. When it's done he sets her down harder than kindness would, and gentler than spite.

n_end_br.animal.vernon_band.text: Then it's a number. Don't hand me the pamphlet like a prize, and don't tell me the next stranger will be careful just because careful has a form. I hunt here. If the form makes a man hesitate, hesitation is not always holy. Remember that you asked for the form.

chainStages.endingImplications: A band makes Queen manageable later. A notch keeps her illegible to the state. The not-coming year depends on whether she was already numbered.

chainStages.title: County Fact or Family Fact
chainStages.summary: Sim does not hunt. If Queen was moved, there is a shell with Ivo's notch at the wrong pond. If she stayed, she is old and does not need Ellis. Sim asks whether the story is county or family.
chainStages.discovery: Sim is at the log or at the wrong pond, not at a sign. There is no brochure yet. That is what they are refusing in advance.

steps.playerAction: Go where Sim actually is, log or wrong pond, and look before you tell the story.
Do not whistle to improve the evidence.
Choose county fact or family fact.

n_open.text: I don't want her on a sign. I also don't want her only in our kitchen, where she shrinks every winter. Tell me which shrinking you can live with. If you moved her in some earlier life, the shell is at the wrong pond and the notch is still a notch. If you didn't, she doesn't need you. Both are allowed to be the end.

choices.text: Tell it as county fact. Accept the sign's risk.
Keep it a family fact. Accept the winter shrinking.

textVariants.text: Someone in your will let a band stay on her, so a stranger could read the care. Sim has seen the pamphlet drafts that grew from that number. She does not want Queen on a sign, and she is angry that the number already made the sign easy. A family telling now is a retreat. A plain county note is the band kept honest. She wants you to pick the shrinking without pretending the band was never a door.

You moved her off the log in 1952, and the shell people mean is at the wrong pond. The notch is still a notch. Sim will not call that a pilgrimage she led. If the story becomes county fact, it has to include the hay decision and not a myth of guidance. If it stays in the kitchen, the wrong pond gets smaller every winter until it is only a sentence about a grandfather's mower.
You want a record. Sim asks if a record that strangers can read is still a record of an animal or already a sign.

n_mid_br.animal.county.text: Then I'll write it plain: a turtle, a notch, a log, a marsh. No whistle miracles. If someone makes a sign, I'll fight the adjectives and lose some. That's the tax on being public.

n_end_br.animal.county.text: County. No miracle. If the shell is at the wrong pond, say the move was a hay decision. Don't say she led us.

n_mid_br.animal.family.text: Then it shrinks in our kitchen and nowhere else. I'll miss the part a stranger might have protected. I'll also not watch her become a mascot. Kitchens are smaller than signs and sometimes kinder.

n_end_br.animal.family.text: Family. If I knew a whistle, it stays out of the minutes. You can tell it until it gets smaller. That's a way of keeping.

branches.summary: Queen's story is told as county fact, stripped of miracle.
The story stays Pike family fact and will shrink in the telling.
Lula files a plain county note and reserves the right to tear a sign that grows from it.
Lula keeps Queen in the kitchen, starts the shrinking on purpose, and refuses a better paragraph.

rewards.detail: Sim has forced a choice of scale without a mascot.
Queen is either a plain county note or a kitchen story.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies at the marsh, Sim tells it in the kitchen once and does not call that a decision you made.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: No scale is chosen. The sign remains possible.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: County or family is the only scale the ending may use for Queen.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Sim is dead, Lula, older, will not let the story become either a brochure or a private myth without a fight she names.

n_open.text: Sim isn't here to be gentle about shrinking. I still know the difference between a sign and a kitchen. Pick the harm you can proofread.

choices.text: County, plain.
Keep Queen as a family fact.

n_mid_br.animal.lula_county.text: She strikes adjectives while you watch, including the ones that would make Queen sound led. What remains is a notch, a log, a mower, and a refusal to manage her into a brochure. She will file that. She will not read it at a supper.

n_end_br.animal.lula_county.text: Plain. I'll strike every adjective that squeaks. What's left can be public, and public is not the same as loved. If a sign grows out of this note, I will come back and tear the sign, not the note. You picked the scale. I pick the editing.

n_mid_br.animal.lula_family.text: She puts nothing in the county book. She tells the kitchen version once, shorter than Sim would have, and then she stops. The shrinking starts immediately, on purpose, so it is a choice and not a drift.

n_end_br.animal.lula_family.text: Family. I'll hate the shrinking and allow it. No sign on the creek, and no brochure in the barn. If the story gets smaller than the animal, that is the price of not handing her to strangers. I can pay it. Don't you pay it for me with a better paragraph.

chainStages.endingImplications: A county fact puts Queen on a sign and shrinks her into public property. A family fact shrinks her every winter in a kitchen. The ending may use only the scale this choice allows.

title: The Flood Book
summary: The flood book's two sentences are kept, cleaned, or carded, then wetted down to one surviving ink, offered or refused as precedent for a smaller gate, stored or not as a spare, and finally signed or left unfinished while both voices speak.
endingImplications: A single signature lets an ending feel clean. Both or neither keeps the wound as one event with two true sentences. A spare in Salisbury and a citation in 1980 change what a stranger can quote. The ending should not add a third mercy the book was denied.

chainStages.title: The Page That Hurts
chainStages.summary: In 1952 the flood book lies open in the rented survey room because a thaw drip reached the cabinet. The certification says the gate stayed shut. Ivo's margin says it was opened late. Norma wants a fair copy. Gordon wants the mess called a fraud or left ugly. Rennet does not get to be Ivo.
chainStages.discovery: You are in the Court Street room because the door is propped with a brick and the page is already drying on a towel. Nobody sent a rodman. Norma is ashamed of the towel. Gordon is ashamed of you. The two sentences are visible without a request.

steps.playerAction: Read both sentences on the towel before agreeing with either person in the room.
Hear Norma defend neatness as mercy and Gordon defend mess as the only procedure he trusts.
Leave both sentences in the book, make the fair copy, or move the margin onto a private card.

n_open.text: Don't tell me your name yet. The certification says the gate remained shut and the lower works were preserved. The pencil in the margin says opened, late, both mercies missed. One of those makes the other look like panic or like a lie. A fair copy could let this county stop bleeding on a single page. I am not ashamed of wanting that. I am ashamed of the towel. Gordon thinks shame is a method. It isn't. Choose the page strangers will be allowed to see.

choices.text: Keep the certification and the margin in the official book.
Make the fair copy. Leave the margin out of the official book.
Copy the margin onto a private card and leave the book looking settled.

textVariants.text: You want the written thing to be the thing that happened, and Norma sees the hunger. She will not let you call both sentences a record until you say which strangers may hold them. Gordon will call any answer a confidence game. The towel under the flood book is not a metaphor. It is wet.

n_mid_br.flood.margin.text: Gordon laughs without pleasure. Then every clerk in Middlebury gets to feel haunted, which you will enjoy, and every cellar gets a proverb instead of a gate. Fine. Leave it ugly. Ugliness at least has a procedure: you read it and you don't get to feel finished. Don't thank me. I wanted you to be a fraud I could file.

n_end_br.flood.margin.text: Both, then. I will hate the fights this page starts and I will not sand them down after you leave. If a later deputy fair-copies it, she will be undoing you, not me. Gordon, you don't get to tell the selectboard I lost my nerve. I lost an argument. The book keeps the hurt. That is a decision, not a stain I forgot.

n_mid_br.flood.fair.text: Norma already has the clean sheet in the drawer, which is its own confession. She does not pretend she decided this morning. The shut gate can be what the county quotes. The pencil can live in a folder marked private, where panic goes when a deputy is kind. She asks you to watch her copy the attestation and stop her if your mouth can't stand the omission.

n_end_br.flood.fair.text: There. A clean lie with good handwriting. When a cellar floods, they'll read Norma and feel governed. I hope the folder burns. I won't burn it. Burning would make me the kind of man who believes in relics. Rennet, or whoever you are, you helped her sand my uncle into a public servant. Enjoy the quiet. It won't last in the basements.

n_mid_br.flood.card.text: A card is a relic you can lose in a coat. Gordon hates it more than the fair copy, because a card lets you feel honest without letting the town argue. He says so. He also does not take the card. Taking it would mean he agrees to be its priest. He won't.

n_end_br.flood.card.text: The book looks settled. The card does not. I will not file the card, and I will not pretend I don't know which coat it's in. If you die, Rennet, that card is not a will. It is a panic someone might mistake for instructions. Gordon won't carry it. I won't index it. You are inventing a third problem because two sentences were too loud.

branches.summary: The official flood book keeps both the certification and Ivo's margin. Norma accepts the fights. Gordon refuses to call it holiness.
A fair copy becomes the book the county may quote. The margin leaves the official page. Gordon names it a clean lie and does not burn the folder.
The official book looks settled. The margin lives on a private card nobody will index. Norma calls it a third problem.
Gordon keeps both sentences after Norma's death and refuses to explain them into a church.
Gordon witnesses the fair copy after Norma's death and files his disgust as ordinary, not sacred.
Helen refuses to stay as commentary. Both lines remain for strangers, and she leaves the doorway.
Helen accepts the private card so she is not read aloud, and she calls the omission a lie she will live with.

rewards.detail: The 1952 flood book is either a double sentence, a fair copy, or a settled book with a card in a coat.
Ellis knows Norma thinks neatness prevents fights and Gordon thinks neatness is how a cellar gets a proverb.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Rennet dies in the survey room before the page is chosen. Norma blots the towel and does not fair-copy a dead visitor's silence. Gordon tells the selectboard nothing useful.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season turns with both sentences still on the damp page and no copy made. Later readers inherit an accident, not a decision, and Norma will not pretend the towel was policy.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Margin, fair copy, or card remains the form of the book. A later body does not get to call the 1952 choice unfinished if it was finished over the towel.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Norma is already dead, Gordon has the book and no deputy to make neatness sound like care. He still demands a choice, because a dead woman's drawer is not a decision.

n_open.text: Norma's dead and the page is still wet enough to smear. I won't fair-copy it to honor her. I also won't leave it to mildew and call mildew honesty. Keep both sentences, make the clean page she wanted, or put the pencil on a card and feel secretly good. I hate all three. Pick, so I can hate a specific one.

choices.text: Keep both sentences in the book Norma isn't here to sand.
Make the fair copy even though Gordon is the only witness.

n_end_br.flood.margin_gordon.text: Ugly, then. I'll put it back in the cabinet and I won't write a note that explains you. Explanation is how this office becomes a church. The hurt stays on the page. That's the whole favor.

n_end_br.flood.fair_gordon.text: Clean. I'll hate you in a specific way now, which is restful. The county gets a shut gate and a dead deputy's wish. Don't ask me to be moved. I'm filing my disgust under ordinary mail.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Gordon is already dead, Helen comes as far as the survey-room door and will not be made to sermonize. She still knows the margin names a shut gate she once wanted.

n_open.text: Gordon isn't here to make a sermon, and I won't supply one. I told Ivo to keep the gate shut. The pencil says he didn't, or says he did it late. Norma wants the public page kind. I want to leave this doorway. Tell her whether strangers read both lines or one. Then I'm going home.

choices.text: Let strangers read both lines. Helen may leave.
Put the margin on a card so Helen is not read in public.

n_end_br.flood.margin_helen.text: Both, then. I won't stand here while they call me the mercy or the panic. The page can hurt without my commentary. Norma, blot it. I'm finished being a margin.

n_end_br.flood.card_helen.text: A card. Cowardly, and I'll take it. I don't want my sentence in a clerk's mouth. If that makes the book look settled, the book can lie by omission. I am going home before anyone asks me to feel noble about it.

chainStages.endingImplications: Keeping both sentences in the official book forces every later reader to hurt. A fair copy lets the county quote a shut gate. A private card hides the margin and makes the book look settled. The 2022 signing speaks into whichever page this choice left.

chainStages.title: Which Ink Dries
chainStages.summary: In 1966 the cabinet leaks again. Clark says a hearing will read whatever dries. Norma has one blotter and two inks. Ada's face will move if the margin is the survivor. The choice is which sentence the room will be able to say aloud.
chainStages.discovery: The smell of wet paper is in the stair before anyone speaks. Clark has the blotter in his hand and has not used it. The hearing is an hour off, which is why he is sweating and why Norma has not yet performed calm. You walked in because the brick was in the door again.

steps.playerAction: Look at which sentence the water is taking before you touch the blotter.
Let Clark admit he wants a face that will not flinch in the hearing.
Save the margin or save the certification, and do not pretend the blotter can save both.

n_open.text: One blotter. Two inks. If you hesitate, the page chooses by gravity and I won't let gravity be my policy. The hearing will read whatever we save. If your face moves on the pencil, the room will see it, Ada. Decide whether we are walking in with a shut gate or with a late opening. Mother wants both and the water doesn't.

choices.text: Blot so the margin dries and the certification smears.
Blot so the certification dries and the margin smears.

textVariants.text: You kept both sentences in the official book, and the wet is now choosing between them with gravity. Clark is furious that a policy you already made can be undone by a leak. Saving the margin continues 1952. Saving the certification lets the hearing walk out with the shut gate and lets your earlier courage smear into a stain. He will not call either of those an accident.

A fair copy already cleaned the margin, and the official page is the kind one. The wet is threatening the only public sentence the county has agreed to trust. Clark wants that sentence to survive because culverts and hearings need it. The pencil, if it still exists, is on a private card and is not what the room will read. He is asking you whether to spend the blotter on the page strangers actually hold.

The margin lives on a card in a drawer, and the book on the table looks settled. Water is about to make the settled look true by destroying the argument. Clark knows the card is not the hearing's page. If you save the certification, the card becomes the only dissent and it can be lost in a pocket. If you somehow save a pencil that isn't on this sheet, you are performing a rescue the blotter cannot do. He wants you to admit which object is actually wet.

Your hands want a second sheet before the blotter commits. Clark sees it and puts his palm on the dry drawer. A second copy is how this office starts to feel innocent. There is one wet page and one hour. Ada does not get to duplicate her way out of which ink dies.

n_mid_br.flood.wet_margin.text: Norma does not grab the blotter. She says the hearing will call it panic and they will not be entirely wrong. Panic is still a report. A shut gate that didn't stay shut is not a kindness she can hear read aloud without wanting to correct the reader. She will sit in the hearing and not correct. That is the cost she is naming, not a blessing.

n_end_br.flood.wet_margin.text: Pencil, then. I'll walk in with a page that makes my mother look indulgent and my office look late. If your face moves, Ada, I'll say you have a draft in the room and I'll be lying. Don't make me invent a draft. The margin is what dried. We will be hated for a sentence that at least happened.

n_mid_br.flood.wet_cert.text: Norma exhales like someone who has been holding a broom over a spill for fourteen years. The shut gate will be readable. The pencil will be a gray thumb. She does not call the thumb an accident. She calls it the choice you just made with a blotter, so that later nobody can say the water was the deputy.

n_end_br.flood.wet_cert.text: Readable mercy. I'll take it into the hearing and I won't wink. If someone asks about the gray thumb, I'll say the cabinet leaked and a person chose. I won't say the person was a ghost. Ada, keep your face still or don't come in. Stillness is the rest of this decision.

branches.summary: The margin is the ink that dries. Clark takes lateness into the hearing and refuses to invent a draft to explain Ada's face.
The certification dries. Clark will tell the hearing a person chose, and he will not wink the margin back into existence.
Clark carries the dried margin into the hearing after Norma's death and refuses to frame it as revenge.
Clark saves the certification alone and keeps the smear as his decision, not the room's rumor.
Gordon stays out of the hearing. The margin dries, and he refuses the minutes that would neaten it.
Gordon lets the certification dry and leaves for lunch rather than staging a protest.

rewards.detail: The 1966 hearing received either the dried margin or the dried certification, and the other ink is a smear a person chose.
Ellis knows Clark will not invent a draft to cover a flinch, and that the blotter could not save both sentences.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Ada dies before the blotter is used. Clark blots the certification because he will not let a corpse's silence choose the pencil, and he writes that the choice was his.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The water takes both inks unevenly and nobody claims the smear. The hearing reads a wreck. Norma will not testify that wreck into a policy after the season turns.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Whichever sentence dried remains the sentence Clark is willing to read. The smear is not restored by a later, drier conscience.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Norma is already dead, Clark still has one blotter and a hearing. He will not perform her kindness. He asks Ada which ink the room is allowed to say.

n_open.text: Mother's dead and the cabinet still leaks, which is the least poetic fact in Middlebury. One blotter. The hearing is today. Save the pencil or save the attestation. I won't do both with a speech. Ada, your face is not evidence. The ink is. Choose the ink.

choices.text: Save the margin, with only Clark to carry it.
Save the certification and leave the pencil as a smear.

n_end_br.flood.wet_margin_clark.text: Pencil. I'll be the one they call indulgent, not her. If that feels like revenge on a dead deputy, it isn't. It's a wet page and a clock. Come in only if you can keep still.

n_end_br.flood.wet_cert_clark.text: Attestation. I'll say a person chose. I won't say which person, if you stay in the hall. The gray thumb can be weather to them and a decision to me. That's as split as I'm willing to be.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Clark is already dead, Gordon is old enough to still be angry in the doorway. He will not attend the hearing. He will say which ink he is willing to watch dry.

n_open.text: Clark's dead and I'm not becoming the son of the office to replace him. Norma can blot. I'll only say this from the door: save the pencil and the hearing hates you honestly, or save the shut gate and the hearing feels governed. I won't walk in. Pick the hate you can stand to hear about later.

choices.text: Save the margin while Gordon stays in the doorway.
Save the certification. Let Gordon leave without the minutes.

n_end_br.flood.wet_margin_gordon.text: Honest hate. Good. I'll hear about it from a clerk and I'll say I told you the door was as far as I go. Don't send me the minutes. Minutes are how hate gets neat.

n_end_br.flood.wet_cert_gordon.text: Governed. They'll feel better and the cellars won't. I said my piece from the door. Norma, blot your mercy. I'm going to lunch, which is not a protest. It's lunch.

chainStages.endingImplications: If the margin dries, the hearing must hear lateness. If the certification dries, the hearing gets a shut gate and the pencil becomes a smear. Clark's later requests for precedent grow from whichever sentence survived the blotter.

chainStages.title: A Smaller Gate
chainStages.summary: In 1980 Clark wants the flood book to justify a smaller gate: predictable water, a fundable culvert, a precedent that loves the town by repeating the wound at a reduced scale. Ruth counts what the extra water would do to the race. Louis is asked to let the book be used or to refuse it.
chainStages.discovery: Clark has the book open to the dry sentence and a culvert sketch beside it, unasked. Ruth is in the room because she followed the sketch, not because anyone called a meeting. The brick is in the door. The sketch is the discovery.

steps.playerAction: Read the culvert sketch beside the flood book before you touch either.
Hear Ruth's count of the race, and do not translate it into a proverb.
Let the book justify the gate, or refuse the precedent and leave the sketch unfunded by this page.

n_open.text: This is a smaller gate and a louder selectboard. I am not Ivo and I am not asking you to be him, Louis. I am asking the dry sentence to do work: a culvert, a predictable hour of water, fewer cellars. If you stop me, don't offer a proverb. Offer what the flooded cellar gets instead. Ruth thinks the race pays. She came up the hill with the sketch in her head. Let her count, then let the book work or don't.

choices.text: Refuse. The flood book does not justify this gate.
Let the dry sentence justify the smaller gate.

textVariants.text: In the thaw you saved the pencil and let the certification smear. Clark has been carrying a page that makes him look like a man who prefers panic to policy. He wants this smaller gate to rehabilitate the book by putting it to work. If you refuse, the margin you rescued stays a mood. If you allow the precedent, you spend the rescued pencil on a culvert and Ruth will say which hour of water that costs.

You let the margin drown and kept the shut-gate sentence. Clark treats that as the adult book, finally. The sketch in his hand is just the sentence doing the job it was cleaned for. Ruth did not come to admire adulthood. She came to count. Louis, the precedent is easy today because you already chose the easy ink. Clark should not get to pretend this is the first time.

You don't argue with where water wants to go, and Clark is hoping that sounds like agreement. It isn't. Ruth is the one who will say which bank takes the extra hour. The book can be a precedent or it can stay a page. Water will not read it either way. People will.

n_mid_br.flood.refused.text: Ruth nods like a count coming out even. Then the race doesn't inherit his uncle's hour. I'll tell Ansel's memory, or the wheel, nothing romantic. I'll say the book stayed a book. Clark can find another sentence to fund a culvert. He won't like how ordinary the next sentence is. Ordinary is what I trust.

n_end_br.flood.refused.text: Refused. I'll tell the selectboard the page is not a tool, and they will hear superstition. I'll correct them once: it is a decision to not repeat a wound at a smaller scale. The cellar still needs a pipe. I'll go find a pipe that doesn't wear Ivo's name. Ruth, your count stands. I won't forge a proverb over it.

n_mid_br.flood.used.text: Then the race takes an hour it didn't agree to, and I'll write the hour in the mill book as theft with a citation. I won't shout. Shouting is how men turn a count into weather. Louis, if you think a funded culvert loves a town, love it down here where the boards are. I'll still be counting after your meeting adjourns.

n_end_br.flood.used.text: Used. I'll cite the page and I'll cite Ruth's objection in the same paragraph, so nobody later can say the race was a surprise. Precedent is how I love a place: water that arrives when I said it would. You can call that a smaller wound. I'll call it a culvert. Both can be true without becoming friends.

branches.summary: The flood book is refused as precedent. Clark must fund the culvert without Ivo's sentence. Ruth's count stands.
The flood book is cited to justify a smaller gate. Clark records Ruth's objection in the same paragraph and does not call the race a surprise.
Ruth removes the sketch after Clark's death. The flood book is not allowed to become haunted plumbing.
Ruth records the citation and the hour in the mill book, small, and will not host a complicated visit.
Norma shuts the book rather than watch it become a tool, and she accepts being called precious.
Norma lets the book be used and insists her objection sit in the minutes beside the citation.

rewards.detail: The flood book either stayed a page or became a citation for a smaller gate, and Ruth's count is attached either way.
Ellis knows Clark will not cover a refusal with a proverb, and knows the race's hour was the objection.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Louis dies between the sketch and the choice. Clark does not cite a dead man's silence as precedent. Ruth takes the sketch back down the hill and writes nothing romantic.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The sketch stays beside the book and neither use nor refusal is spoken. Clark will not tell the selectboard that hesitation was a yes. Ruth's count remains oral until someone chooses.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Refusal or citation remains what the 1980 book was for. A later gate cannot be called the first time anyone thought to use the page.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Clark is already dead, Ruth still has the sketch and will not let the book volunteer itself. She asks Louis to refuse the precedent or to admit the citation, without Clark's smoothness.

n_open.text: Clark's dead and his sketch isn't. I won't read it in his voice. The book is on the table. If you let it justify a gate, say so, and I'll write the hour as a citation. If you refuse, say so, and I'll take the sketch off this desk. I don't do proverbs. Louis, the race is not a metaphor. Pick.

choices.text: Refuse the precedent. Let Ruth take the sketch.
Admit the citation. Let Ruth write the hour down.

n_end_br.flood.refused_ruth.text: Off the desk. Good. The book stays a book. I'll tell the wheel nothing poetic. If the selectboard wants a culvert they can want it in sentences that aren't a dead surveyor's panic. I can live with unfunded. I can't live with haunted plumbing.

n_end_br.flood.used_ruth.text: Cited. I'll write the hour and your name in the mill book, small, so it doesn't become a speech. The race pays. You said it could. Don't visit the wheel to feel complicated about it. Complicated is not a measurement.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Ruth is already dead, Norma will not pretend to count the race. She will say whether she can bear the book being used as a tool, which is a different pain from neatness.

n_open.text: Ruth isn't here to count, and I won't fake her numbers. Clark wants the dry sentence to fund a culvert. I have spent my life making pages that prevent fights. A tool is not a fair copy. Louis, tell me if I am supposed to watch this book go to work, or if I am supposed to shut it and be called precious.

choices.text: Shut the book. Do not let Norma watch it go to work.
Let the book work, and let Norma say she hates the use.

n_end_br.flood.refused_norma.text: Shut. I'll be called precious by men who own dry shoes. I have been called worse by basements. The page stays a page. Clark can find a culvert sentence that didn't fail anyone in 1938. I won't lend him this one.

n_end_br.flood.used_norma.text: Then it works, and I hate it in the minutes so the hate is not a mood. Write that the deputy objected and the page was used anyway. If a cellar stays dry, I won't spit on the dry. I also won't pretend the citation was kind.

chainStages.endingImplications: Using the book as precedent lets a new gate wear Ivo's sentence. Refusing it leaves the culvert unfunded by this page and leaves Ruth's count as the objection that stood. Later signatures cannot pretend the book was never offered as a tool.

chainStages.title: The Outlet Copy
chainStages.summary: In 2008 Middlebury's basement is wet again and the bridge season is making everyone want a clean story. Willa wants a working copy in the Salisbury outlet shed, high and dry. Clark says a second copy is how his mother's neatness began. Chris has to leave one book or two.
chainStages.discovery: The shed smells like dry cedar and lake outlet, not like a shrine. Willa has the flood book in a waxed cloth on a crate. Clark drove because the Court Street cellar is ankle-wet. Nobody posted a notice. The crate is the whole invitation.

steps.playerAction: Stand in the outlet shed until you know whether the waxed cloth is one book or the start of two.
Hear Clark name his mother's neatness without letting him win by tone.
Leave a working copy on the crate, or refuse the second copy and carry the one book back.

n_open.text: The Court Street cellar is wet and the selectboard wants a story that ends. I want a working copy here, where the outlet stays cooler than a basement and nobody's rug is involved. Father says a second page is how Mother started sanding the hurt. He is not wrong about the method. He is wrong that one book in a wet building is bravery. Chris, bravery isn't the choice. Loss is. Leave a copy on this crate or don't.

choices.text: Leave a working copy in the outlet shed.
Refuse the second copy. Carry the one book.

textVariants.text: You are already relieved by the idea of two, and Willa sees the relief and does not let it count as a reason. A second copy soothes you. It does not answer Clark. The shed will keep whatever you leave, including your habit. Decide as if the habit were the danger, because Clark is not inventing that danger.

n_mid_br.flood.shed.text: Clark sets his keys down so he won't gesture with them. Then a stranger in Salisbury can meet my mother's problem without earning it. Maybe that's democracy. Maybe it's how a panic becomes a handout. I'll write on the cloth that the copy is not the certification. If you won't let me write that, you're not storing a book. You're ordaining one.

n_end_br.flood.shed.text: Leave the note, Father. I want the note. A copy that pretends to be the only page is the neatness you're afraid of. This one is labeled spare. If the cellar takes the original, we are not virtuous, we are merely not stupid. Chris, don't come back to check on it. Checking is how a shed becomes an altar. The crate is enough.

n_mid_br.flood.single.text: He looks older than the argument and not triumphant. One book can still drown, and I will hate the drowning if it comes. I would rather hate a drowning than inherit a drawer of kinder pages. Mother's kindness was real. It was also a solvent. Thank you for not mixing another bottle of it in a shed.

n_end_br.flood.single.text: Then we can lose it. I want that said in this shed, not later as a surprise. Chris, you carry it. Father, you don't get to call the refusal your victory over me. I wanted the spare because I have seen what wet paper does. I am accepting the risk. Acceptance is not agreement, and I won't smile on the drive back to Middlebury.

branches.summary: A labeled spare of the flood book stays in the Salisbury shed. Clark's note says it is not the certification. Willa forbids altar-visits.
No spare is made. Willa accepts the risk of one book and will not smile as if Clark had won a family argument.
Clark leaves a labeled spare after Willa's death and names his own urge to visit the crate as the danger.
Clark carries the single book after Willa's death and refuses to turn the risk into a story about his mother.
Owen lets the spare stay, calls it a fire risk rather than a relic, and returns to the feed store.
Owen carries the single book as far as the truck and refuses to join the office the errand belongs to.

rewards.detail: Either a labeled spare sits in the Salisbury outlet shed, or the flood book remains one object that can still be lost to wet.
Ellis has heard Clark call Norma's kindness a solvent, and has heard Willa separate acceptance from agreement.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Chris dies on the outlet road before the cloth is opened or refused. Willa does not make the spare over a death. Clark drives the book back to the wet cellar and writes nothing triumphant.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The book sits on the crate through the season and then goes back to Middlebury undecided. Willa will not claim a spare was blessed by delay. The shed stays a shed.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Spare or single book remains the 2008 fact. The later signing does not conjure a copy this shed was denied, and does not throw out a spare that was labeled.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Willa is already dead, Clark will not use her absence to win the argument about his mother. He still asks Chris whether the shed gets a spare.

n_open.text: Willa's dead and I don't get to be right in her place. The cellar is wet. A spare in this shed might be prudence. It might be the solvent starting again. I have wanted both, which is not a decision. Chris, leave a copy with a note that it isn't the certification, or carry the one book and let me hate the risk honestly.

choices.text: Leave the labeled spare, without Willa to guard it.
Carry the one book back, and let Clark hate the risk.

n_end_br.flood.shed_clark.text: Labeled. I'll say the word spare until it sticks. If I start visiting this crate, tell whoever you are next to stop me. Visiting is the altar. I can be precise about my own weakness. The book can have a twin. I won't light anything beside it.

n_end_br.flood.single_clark.text: One book. I'll hate the wet in advance so it doesn't get to surprise me into a speech. Willa wanted the spare. I won't call this her defeat. She's dead. It's a risk. Drive. I won't talk about Mother on the way unless the road floods, and then I'll talk about the road.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Clark is already dead, Owen will not take the office and will not take the argument about neatness as his inheritance. He still wants the shed decided so he can go back to feed.

n_open.text: Clark's dead. I'm not the deputy and I'm not the son. Willa wants a spare where it's dry. I want to sell feed before six. A second copy feels like a church to me and like a cellar's insurance to her. Chris, pick. I'll carry whichever you don't leave, and I won't stay to consecrate the crate.

choices.text: Leave the spare. Let Owen go back to the feed store.
Carry the one book. Owen takes it only as far as the truck.

n_end_br.flood.shed_owen.text: Left. I'll tell anyone who asks that it's a spare and a fire risk and not a relic. Then I'm done. Willa can label it. I won't visit. Feed has hours. The book having a twin doesn't make me a surveyor.

n_end_br.flood.single_owen.text: One. I'll put it on the seat and I won't buckle it in like a child. If the cellar eats it, that's a wet fact, not a moral. Chris, don't ask me to feel the moral on the drive. I came to end an errand, not to join an office.

chainStages.endingImplications: A shed copy means a later stranger can meet the page without Middlebury's permission, and Norma's neatness has a spare. A single book means the page can still be lost to a wet cellar, and Willa does not get to feel safe. The 2022 signing happens to whatever this choice preserved.

chainStages.title: Both Accounts
chainStages.summary: After Irene, Owen brings the flood book and asks Ellis to finish Ivo's sentence, sign one account, sign both by signing neither as sole, or leave it unfinished. The Voice and the Other Voice speak. They are one wound.
chainStages.discovery: Owen has the book on the feed-store side of his life, wrapped in a clean cloth he resents. He puts it on the survey table as a refusal, not an inheritance.

steps.playerAction: Let Owen say why he will not take the office before you open the book.
Hear both voices without choosing a favorite in advance.
Sign one, write both, or leave the sentence unfinished.

n_fork.text: This fork is not a past life. It is the two voices in the room. Owen will not let you skip them. The partition is which account you have already favored in the book, if any, or neither.

choices.text: The margin is still in the official book. Let the voices argue over a page that kept both.
A fair copy already cleaned the margin. The voices have less page to stand on.
The book is unresolved. Neither mercy has been made official.

margin_b0.text: The gate remained shut. The record is the mercy. What you feel in the hands is weather. Sign the certification if you want the county to stop hurting itself on a contradiction.

margin_b1.text: Your hands were already on the wheel. Late is still the act. The sentence that says shut is the lie that made the meadow. Sign the margin if you can stand being the person who was late.

margin_b2.text: Write both or write neither. If you write one, you will feel clean, and the meadow will still be wet. I didn't bring this so you could feel clean. The margin surviving this long is not a victory. It's a delay.

choices.text: Write both accounts and sign neither as the sole truth.
Sign the Voice. Let the record be the mercy.

margin_both.text: Good. Unclean. I'll leave the book here and go back to the feed store. Don't follow me for a blessing. Feed is the blessing I chose.

margin_voice.text: Signed. The county can quote a shut gate and go home. You will feel the cleanliness and you will deserve the discomfort of having chosen it.

fair_b0.text: The fair copy is the adult book. Sign it again in a living hand and the precedent is finished. Irene does not need your pencil feelings.

fair_b1.text: The fair copy is how lateness gets laundered. If you sign it, you sign the meadow out of the sentence. Your hands remember the wheel even if the page doesn't.

fair_b2.text: I can still show the private copy. Owen doesn't want it in the office. If you sign the fair one, you join Norma. If you refuse, you join the smear. I have lived in the smear on purpose.

choices.text: Refuse the fair copy. Put the margin back in the margin.
Sign the fair copy. Let the precedent be finished.

fair_refuse_fair.text: Then the smear returns to the official page. I'll be blamed. I'll take the blame in writing. Owen can hate the office and still see it tell the truth.

fair_sign_fair.text: Then you're clean and I'm done. Take the key. I won't. The feed store closes at six. The meadow can argue with your signature without me in the room.

neither_b0.text: Shut. Attested. The lower works preserved. You know the sentence. Finishing it is not a sin. It is the job.

neither_b1.text: Opened. Late. Both mercies missed. The job was the hands. The sentence was the panic. Don't let the job pretend it was only one of them.

neither_b2.text: Leave it unfinished on purpose or don't. Unfinished by death is just death. Unfinished by choice is the only version that isn't a costume. I will watch you choose and then I will go sell feed.

choices.text: Leave the sentence unfinished on purpose.
Sign the late hands, in the margin, in this living hand.

neither_unfinished.text: Then it stays a wound and not a policy. I'll take that. Don't visit me to revisit it. The store has hours.

neither_other.text: Signed late, which is the only tense you have ever had. The meadow will not thank you. The page will at least stop pretending you were on time.

branches.summary: Both accounts are written. Neither is sole. Owen returns to the feed store.
Ellis signs the certification account and feels clean.
The margin is restored against the fair copy. The late hands are signed.
Ellis signs the fair copy. Owen refuses the office and leaves.
The sentence is left unfinished by choice. The office stays refused.
Ellis signs the Other Voice. Lateness becomes the official act.
Willa copies both accounts, labels the page unclean, and refuses to make the copying a cleansing.
Willa records the refusal to finish and will not let the blank become an invitation.

rewards.detail: The flood book's last living hand either signs one account, both, or neither.
Ellis has been refused the feeling of cleanliness.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Rowan dies at the table, Owen closes the book and does not sign it in your stead.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The sentence stays unfinished because a body ended, not because anyone chose unfinished.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The choice of account is what later mouths may quote as Ellis's last survey.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Owen is dead, Willa keeps the contradiction and will not let a clean feeling sign itself.

n_open.text: Owen isn't here to insult your cleanliness. I am. Sign one and feel holy, write both, or leave it. I will copy whatever you do, including the refusal.

choices.text: Write both. Sign neither as sole.
Leave it unfinished on purpose.

n_end_wb.text: Both. I'll copy the unclean page and label it unclean. That's my whole faith, and it is a small faith, and it does not make you clean. Owen would have left for the feed store. I will stay long enough to spell the smear correctly, and then I will also leave.

n_end_wn.text: Unfinished. I'll write the date and the refusal. Refusals are records too, which is the only comfort I will give you, and it is not comfort. Norma does not get this page. Neither do you. The meadow stays wet without a signature to blame.

chainStages.endingImplications: The signed account becomes the sentence the ending is allowed to repeat. Both, or neither, leaves the wound honestly unfinished. One signature makes Ellis feel clean. Owen came to prevent that.

title: The Quiet Household
summary: The Waite house in Orwell keeps plates, a stopped clock, a cloth book, and an east-room bed for lives displaced when Ellis wakes in a body. Across five seasons the house decides whether to feed that fact, write it truly, surrender it to the office, use the bed, and finally dry the plates or keep spending groceries.
endingImplications: A dried rack means the returns no longer get a kitchen. A continued setting means the cost stays edible and local. A book in the office means the names can be cited; a book in the drawer means they stay housekeeping. The bed's use, laundry, or refusal is a 2008 fact Eden can remember without turning it into a vigil. None of these are a romance and none of them crown Ellis. They change what a final account is allowed to do with Orwell.

chainStages.title: The Plate That Is Not a Trick
chainStages.summary: In 1952 the Waite kitchen in Orwell has already set a plate for Cress Moss, the life that stopped the morning Ellis woke in Rennet. Esther offers two kindnesses and will not call either a homecoming. Harold will not let the clock be recruited.
chainStages.discovery: Rennet's feet take the Orwell road without a summons. The Waite door is unlatched because Esther cooks with it open, not because anyone is expected. A plate is served. The hall clock is stopped. No one at the table calls it a welcome.

steps.playerAction: Enter the Orwell kitchen and look at the plate before anyone explains it.
Hear Esther name the two kindnesses, and hear Harold refuse to start the clock as part of the bargain.
Eat Cress's plate or leave it, and stay long enough for the house to say which practice dies.

n_open.text: Cress Moss had a morning. You are standing in what is left of it, and I am not going to guess your name to make the table easier. The plate is onions and a life that did not sit down. Eat, and I stop setting it tomorrow. Leave it, and I set it until I die. Harold has already decided the clock. I am deciding the stove. Neither of us is offering you a homecoming in Orwell.

choices.text: Eat the plate, and let tomorrow's place be empty.
Leave the plate. Let Esther set it until she dies.

textVariants.text: You are bound to this house, so Esther does not ask whether the plate matters. She sets the spoon where your hand will find it and says the kindnesses as house rules, not as news. Eat, and the plate ends tomorrow. Leave it, and she keeps Cress's place until her own death. The clock stays Harold's and stays stopped.

n_mid_br.house.ate.text: Harold Waite does not sit. He watches the first bite as if it were a measurement. The clock stays at the minute he chose. Eating does not wind it. If she stops the plate tomorrow, she is telling the truth about a finished morning. Don't you thank the clock for agreeing. It isn't.

n_end_br.house.ate.text: Tomorrow the place is empty. I will not praise you for finishing Cress Moss's breakfast, and I will not set it again to punish you for having a mouth. You ate.
