The practice ends. Harold can keep his minute. I keep my word. If you call this a homecoming on the Orwell road, you will be lying, and I will correct you in front of whoever is left.

n_mid_br.house.left.text: Harold nods once, which is not approval. The food will go to the hens or the cold, and the clock will not be asked to bless the waste. Leaving is a sentence. It is not a prayer. He will not say Cress's name a second time to decorate it.

n_end_br.house.left.text: Then I set it until I die. That is the kindness you chose, and it is mine to pay for, not yours to visit. Don't stand in the doorway and look fed by the gesture. You are not. The plate stays Cress Moss's until my hands stop. Harold's minute and my place setting are now both refusals. I can live in a house with two of them.

branches.summary: Ellis eats the plate set for Cress. Esther ends the practice the next day and refuses the word homecoming.
The plate is left. Esther will set Cress's place until her own death, and she will not let the gesture feed Ellis.
With Esther dead, Harold lets the plate be eaten and ends the setting without turning it into care.
Harold keeps the uneaten plate as a hard fact after Esther's death and will not rename it her kindness.
Esther, alone because Harold is dead, ends the plate after it is eaten and leaves the clock untouched.
Esther keeps Cress's place until her death without Harold, and she names it a practice rather than grief.

rewards.detail: The Orwell house records whether Cress's plate was eaten or kept as a practice, and Esther will not rename either one a welcome.
Ellis knows the stopped clock and the plate are different refusals, and that only the plate was offered as a choice.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Rennet dies in the Orwell kitchen before the plate is eaten or left. Esther scrapes it into the hens' pail and does not decide the practice on a dead guest's behalf. Harold does not wind the clock to mark the death.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season turns with the plate untouched and uneaten. Esther keeps setting it, but she will not claim Ellis chose the practice. The choice stays unfinished and the clock stays stopped.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The eaten plate or the lasting place setting remains what the house does. The next body is not greeted as if the 1952 kindness were still negotiable.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Esther is already dead, Harold will not inherit her hospitality. He states the plate as her unfinished practice and makes Ellis choose without a warm voice in the room.

n_open.text: Esther is dead. The plate was hers. I stopped the clock and I am not starting it to bury her. Eat, and nobody in this house sets Cress Moss a place tomorrow, because I won't. Leave it, and the cold food is a fact I will look at until I follow her. I don't do kindness. I do the minute and the question she left.

choices.text: Eat, so Harold can stop the place setting.
Leave the plate in the dead woman's kitchen.

n_end_br.house.ate_harold.text: Eaten. Tomorrow the table has one less lie. I will not thank you, and I will not wind the clock because a plate is finished. Cress Moss stays a morning that stopped. That is all the Orwell kitchen is getting from me.

n_end_br.house.left_harold.text: Left. Then it sits until it spoils, and I look at it. Don't call that Esther's kindness continuing. She isn't here to pay it. I'm here to refuse a prettier ending. The clock stays stopped.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Harold is already dead, Esther still offers the plate, and she will not pretend the stopped clock needs his voice to remain stopped. The choice is still eat or leave.

n_open.text: Harold died with the clock already stopped. I am not asking you to wind it in his place. The plate is mine. Cress Moss does not get a eulogy from a man who isn't in the hall. Eat, and I stop setting it tomorrow. Leave it, and I set it until I die. That was the offer before he went, and death didn't improve it.

choices.text: Eat the plate with only Esther left to witness it.
Leave the plate, and let Esther carry the practice alone.

n_end_br.house.ate_esther.text: Tomorrow it is empty. I don't need Harold to ratify an empty place. You ate Cress Moss's breakfast in a house that will not call you home. The clock can stay his, stopped, without an audience.

n_end_br.house.left_esther.text: Then I carry it. No clock-keeper, no chorus. A plate until I die. If that looks like grief from the road, the road is wrong. It is a practice. You chose the long one.

chainStages.endingImplications: Eating ends the plate tomorrow and lets Cress's morning be finished in the house's practice. Leaving the plate makes Esther set it until she dies. Later keepers inherit a stopped kindness or a fed one, and they do not get to pretend the choice was weather.

chainStages.title: One Inconvenient Want
chainStages.summary: In 1966 Esther asks Ada Smollet for one thing Adah wanted that Ellis will not perform. Clara is in the kitchen to catch a pretty want. The house will write a true inconvenience or it will catch Ellis using the ink.
chainStages.discovery: The second plate is already a problem when Ada reaches the Orwell house. Esther has the book open to a blank line and Clara has the pen uncapped, as if they argued about the pen before the door. Nobody sent for a teacher. The damper in the school's story is not yet a sentence.

steps.playerAction: Stand at the kitchen table until Esther asks for a want, and do not offer a speech before she asks.
Say either the damper and the refused thanks, or a want that would look kind in a book.
Let Clara accept the inconvenience or throw the pretty sentence back.

n_open.text: Fourteen years and a new face, and I still don't want your biography. Tell me one thing Adah Smollet wanted that you, in that body, will not do. Not a pretty want. A small, inconvenient, real one. I will write it. Then this house can be rude in the correct direction. Clara is here because she thinks I am too ready to be moved. She is right to watch the ink.

choices.text: Say Adah wanted the school damper fixed, and no thanks in front of the children.
Say Adah wanted to be remembered as the teacher who saved the county's handwriting.

textVariants.text: You ate Cress's plate, and Esther stopped setting it the next day, as she promised. The stove has been ordinary for fourteen years. She is not reopening that kindness. Adah is a different displaced life, and Esther wants one inconvenient want, not a second plate. Clara is watching because a person who will eat a ghost's supper might also invent a pretty future for the next ghost.

You left Cress's plate, and Esther has set it ever since, through her aging and into this second face at her table. She is tired in a way she earned. The want she is asking about Adah is not a new place setting unless you make it one. Clara thinks the kitchen has become a diet of absence. Esther still wants the damper, not a legend, and she will write only what you will not perform.

Esther sees the kindness rising in Ada's mouth and puts her hand on the book. Clara already has the sentence you would spare them. A kind lie about Adah would be easy and inaccurate. Esther wants the damper, or she wants you to admit you are about to decorate a dead plan. The Orwell kitchen will not help you be gentle.

n_mid_br.house.true_want.text: Clara waits for the ornament and does not get it. She caps the pen only after the damper is the whole story. No one thanked. That is usable. A house can fail to thank someone. A house cannot live up to a legend without lying before supper.

n_end_br.house.true_want.text: Written. The damper, and no public thanks. I will not send you to fix it in her place. You said you won't, and I am holding you to the won't. Clara can sneer at me for collecting inconveniences. She can't sneer at this one for being pretty. Adah stays a person who wanted a stove to draw. That is enough line for one life.

n_mid_br.house.pretty.text: Clara laughs once, short, and not kindly. That want is from a book you read, not from a woman who complained about soot. She pushes the book back toward Esther. If you write that, you are feeding us. I live here. I don't eat memorials.

n_end_br.house.pretty.text: I heard the pretty want and I heard my daughter. I will not write it. You offered a legend because a legend is easier than a damper. Clara caught it. The line stays blank, and the blank is now held against you, Ada, not against Adah. Don't try a second, better performance. The kitchen has had its one.

branches.summary: Ellis gives Adah's real want. The household writes the damper and the refused thanks, and does not ask Ellis to perform it.
Clara catches the pretty want. Esther leaves the line blank and the household holds the performance against Ellis.
Clara, keeping the book after Esther's death, writes the damper and refuses Ellis any errand that would perform it.
Clara refuses the pretty want outright and leaves Adah's line blank rather than let a legend into the house book.
Miriam lets the true want into the book and blocks any attempt to turn it into Ada's chore.
Miriam rejects the pretty want after Clara's death and leaves the household line blank.

rewards.detail: The household book either holds Adah's damper and her refusal of thanks, or a blank where a pretty want was refused.
Ellis knows Clara will punish a decorative sentence about the displaced, and that Esther wanted an inconvenience she could aim.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Ada dies at the Orwell table before the want is said. Clara caps the pen. Esther does not invent Adah's sentence to finish a dead visitor's errand. The line stays blank and unblamed.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season turns with the line unwritten. Esther will not fill it from rumor. Clara remembers that Ellis was asked and did not answer, which is not the same as a pretty lie and not the same as a fact.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The damper is in the book, or the pretty want is a known refusal. The next body does not get to re-audition Adah's desire in this kitchen.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Esther is already dead, Clara keeps the book and is less willing to be moved. She still demands one real want or she will throw a pretty one out of the house.

n_open.text: Mother is dead and the book is mine now, which she would hate and which is true. I don't want your biography, Ada. One thing Adah wanted that you will not do. If you give me a legend about handwriting, I will not write it and I will not forgive the attempt just because Esther isn't here to be gentler.

choices.text: Tell Clara about the damper and the refused thanks.
Offer Clara the legend of the saving teacher.

n_end_br.house.true_clara.text: That's a want. Soot and no applause. I'll write it because it can be failed. I will not send you to the school to become Adah for an afternoon. You don't get credit for a stove you won't touch.

n_end_br.house.pretty_clara.text: No. That's a speech for a dead woman who complained about the damper. The line stays blank. You can leave Orwell with the legend still in your mouth. It doesn't get to live in this book.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Clara is already dead, Miriam watches the ink in her sister's place. She is less amused and just as unwilling to let a pretty want become housekeeping.

n_open.text: Clara is dead, so you don't get the laugh. You get me. Mother wants one inconvenient true thing Adah wanted, and she wants it in the book. I want to hear whether you are about to make our dead into a lesson. Speak the want, Ada. I will say if it is food.

choices.text: Say the damper and the private thanks, with Miriam listening.
Say the saving-teacher legend while Miriam holds the book.

n_end_br.house.true_miriam.text: Write it, Mother. A damper and no scene in front of children. That can be true without feeding us. Ada, you don't fix it. You already said you won't. Good. A want is not a chore you inherit with the face.

n_end_br.house.pretty_miriam.text: That's food. Don't write it. Adah is not a county lesson and you don't get to be moved by her in our kitchen. The line stays blank. Clara would have been louder. I am only finished.

chainStages.endingImplications: A true want gives the household one fact about Adah they can be rude toward: the stove, the refusal of public thanks. A pretty want is heard by Clara and stains the book. Later keepers can trust the line or know it was performed.

chainStages.title: Measurements or Housekeeping
chainStages.summary: In 1994 Miriam is failing the argument she has had with herself for decades. The cloth book of displaced names can go to the survey office and become measurements, or stay in the house and make Joel the heir of strange housekeeping. Hannah Greer is not offered a third, cleaner book.
chainStages.discovery: The book is on the kitchen table in Orwell because Miriam took it out of the drawer before Hannah arrived. Joel has not sat down. The office is not in the room. The choice is visible as cloth, names, and two pairs of hands that disagree about what a record is for.

steps.playerAction: Read no farther than Miriam lets the book fall open. The names are not a pile to be taken.
Hear Joel say which inheritance he can stand, without agreeing in order to soothe him.
Leave the book in his hands or carry it toward the office, and let Miriam say which one she can forgive.

n_open.text: Hannah, or whoever is using the year: this is not the flood book and you will not merge them to feel tidy. These are the names this house kept because the office would have kept them wrong. Take it to Middlebury and you make them measurements. Leave it and my son inherits strange housekeeping. I know which one I can forgive. I am asking you which one you can carry without calling yourself kind.

choices.text: Carry the household book to the survey office.
Leave the book in the house, with Joel.

textVariants.text: You want the book where a record lives, and Miriam sees that hunger before you speak. She does not argue that the office is evil. She argues that a measurement is a different act from a plate. Joel will not rescue you from the distinction. The cloth book stays on the Orwell table until you pick a harm.

n_mid_br.house.office.text: Joel does not grab it back. He says, then it's your craft and not my cupboard. I'll hate the citation more than I hate the plates, and I already hate the plates. If a name gets read aloud in a rented room as evidence, don't tell me I consented. I consented to not being the only one who knows.

n_end_br.house.office.text: Take it. I won't forgive it, and I said that before you chose. Joel gets a cleaner cupboard and a worse county. When they measure Cress and Adah and Lou and Nan, they will sound accurate. Accuracy was not the thing I was keeping them from. I was keeping them from being useful. You are useful, Hannah. That is not a compliment tonight.

n_mid_br.house.stays.text: Then it's mine when she's done saying so. I don't want it. I want the wanting to be over. I'll keep it because she asked, and I will not pretend keeping is the same as believing the plates feed anyone but us. Don't you visit to check on my belief.

n_end_br.house.stays.text: Good. Strange housekeeping is the one I can forgive. The office can live without these names. Joel can live with them, angrily, which is a kind of accuracy I trust more than a fair copy. Hannah, you don't get a key to the drawer. You already have a life that wasn't going to be yours.

branches.summary: The household book goes to the survey office. Miriam does not forgive the usefulness. Joel is left with a cleaner cupboard.
The book stays in the house. Joel inherits it as strange housekeeping, not as a belief, and the office does not get the names.
Joel releases the book to the office after Miriam's death and withholds any blessing she would not have given.
Joel keeps the book as an unloved tool after Miriam's death, and forbids Ellis from describing it to the office.
Miriam lets the book go to the office with Eden as witness and names usefulness as the injury.
The book stays, not as Eden's inheritance of sweetness, and Miriam refuses Hannah a copy.

rewards.detail: The cloth book of displaced names is either a survey holding or still a household drawer, and that difference is public inside the family.
Miriam's forgiveness, or the refusal of it, is attached to the book's location and will not be re-litigated as manners.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Hannah dies before the book moves. Miriam puts it back in the drawer herself and tells Joel the choice was interrupted, not inherited. The office does not receive a dead woman's errand.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The book remains on the table through the turn of the season and then goes back to the drawer undecided. Joel does not inherit a verdict. Miriam does not pretend the office won by silence.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The book's place, office or house, remains the 1994 fact. A later body does not get to move it back under the name of kindness.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Miriam is already dead, Joel has the book and the resentment without her forgiveness to aim at. He still asks Hannah to choose office or house, because leaving it unchosen was her last unfinished demand.

n_open.text: She's dead and the book is in my hands, which is not the same as a decision. Take it to the office and the names become measurements. Leave it and I keep a cupboard I resent. I won't perform her speech. I will make you pick, Hannah, so I don't get to say the year decided for me.

choices.text: Take the book to the office now that Miriam cannot forbid it.
Leave the book with Joel and do not make it evidence.

n_end_br.house.office_joel.text: Then go. I won't walk with you. If they cite my mother's handwriting, that's the harm you picked. I'll hate it plainly. Don't come back for a blessing the dead woman already refused you.

n_end_br.house.stays_joel.text: Then it stays. I'll keep it the way I keep tools I don't love. Not as a shrine. If you tell the office we have a secret book, you will be making measurements out of a cupboard. Don't.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Joel is already dead, Eden is old enough in this telling to hear the stakes, and Miriam will not use her granddaughter as a soft reason. The book still moves or stays.

n_open.text: Joel is dead. I will not hand this to Eden as if a child could absolve a record. Hannah, the choice got worse and didn't change. Office, and they become measurements. House, and I keep strange housekeeping with one less son. Say which harm. She can hear it. She is not the judge.

choices.text: Send the book to the office while Eden hears the refusal.
Keep the book in the house, and do not make Eden its reason.

n_end_br.house.office_eden.text: Take it. Eden, remember that I did not forgive this. Remember it as a fact, not as a story you have to repair. The names will be useful now. Usefulness is the injury.

n_end_br.house.stays_eden.text: It stays. Not because she is young and kind. Because the office does not get these names. Eden can hate the drawer later. That is allowed. Hannah, you don't get a copy to feel responsible.

chainStages.endingImplications: If the book goes to the office, the displaced become lines a survey can cite, including this house's private accuracies. If it stays, Joel inherits a practice he resents and the office does not get to measure Cress, Adah, Lou, and Nan. The ending may mention the names only in the form this choice allowed.

chainStages.title: The Bed Made for Someone Else
chainStages.summary: In 2008 the east room is made up for a life that is not going to sleep there. Christian Dobbs was going to stay a mechanic. Chris is in the doorway. Miriam is a year from dying and will not run the night. Eden, twenty-eight, wants the groceries of the thing discussed, not its portion of memory.
chainStages.discovery: The east-room lamp is already lit when Chris comes up from the kitchen. The bed is made with hospital corners that predate the visit. Eden is sitting on the trunk so the bed cannot be casually used. Miriam is in the chair because standing is expensive. Nobody offered a tour.

steps.playerAction: Stop in the doorway of the east room and do not sit until the bed has been spoken about.
Hear Eden separate groceries from memory, and hear Miriam refuse to adjudicate from the chair.
Sleep in the bed, strip it, or sit the night up without using it.

n_open.text: Christian's plate downstairs is too much food. I said portion is groceries. They said portion is memory. This bed is the same argument with sheets. You can sleep in it and make the room a lodging. You can strip it and make the room honest and a little cruel. You can sit up and be useless on purpose. Grandmother is not going to pick. She has spent the year dying on a schedule and she is off duty. Chris, the bed was not made for you. That's the only courtesy I have.

choices.text: Sleep in the bed the house made for the displaced life.
Strip the bed so it cannot host a ghost or a guest.
Sit the night up. Do not use the bed and do not strip it.

textVariants.text: You are inclined to ask what the living in the room need, and Eden is the living one on the trunk. She does not want your sympathy for Christian turned into a night's sleep. Miriam will not choose. The sheets are a decision about use, waste, or refusal, and the east room will show it in the morning.

n_mid_br.house.slept.text: Miriam watches Eden stand up off the trunk and does not stop her or help her. From the chair she says, then it's lodging. I won't call it desecration. I also won't call it care. Christian isn't warmed by it. You are. In the morning the sheets will say someone used the room. That is a true sentence. It isn't a kind one.

n_end_br.house.slept.text: You slept. I'll change the sheets because I live here, not because you earned a turn-down. Don't tell anyone in Orwell you kept a vigil. You kept warm. Grandmother can forgive a truth faster than a vigil. I can forgive neither tonight, and I don't have to. The bed was used. That's the record.

n_mid_br.house.stripped.text: Eden takes the pillow before being asked and stacks it on the trunk. She wanted this and is angry that wanting it feels like a win. Stripping is not an insult she gets to enjoy. It is laundry. Christian doesn't feel the laundry. The room feels less like a dare.

n_end_br.house.stripped.text: Bare mattress. Good. I am too tired to love the gesture and too honest to call it violent. The room can be a room. Eden, don't gloat on the landing. Chris, don't apologize to the sheets. A practice can end in laundry without a hymn. I won't start one from this chair.

n_mid_br.house.sat.text: Miriam almost smiles and doesn't. Sitting up is the choice of a person who cannot leave a gate and cannot bear to close it. She recognizes the type and does not reward it. The bed stays made. The body stays uncomfortable. Nobody is improved.

n_end_br.house.sat.text: Then we all lose a night and the bed stays a dare. I'll allow it. I won't admire it. In the morning the sheets are still smooth and you are useless, which you chose, and Grandmother gets to say she didn't spend her last year commanding guests. Chris, when you leave, leave the lamp. I'll put it out. That's house work, not your symbol.

branches.summary: Chris sleeps in the east-room bed. Eden calls it warmth, not a vigil, and Miriam lets the sheets be a true sentence.
The east-room bed is stripped. Miriam refuses both hymn and apology, and the room becomes a room by laundry.
Chris sits the night without using or stripping the bed. Eden allows the unfinished room and refuses to admire it.
With Miriam dead, Eden lets Chris sleep and names it warmth, then refuses help that would turn the morning into a scene.
Eden strips the bed after Miriam's death and keeps the act from becoming either a victory or a sacrilege.
Joel lets the bed be used and forbids any breakfast poetry about the night.
Joel accepts a night sat up as the house's ugly honesty and refuses to admire it.

rewards.detail: The east room in 2008 records use, laundry, or a night sat up, and Eden will not translate any of the three into a vigil.
Ellis knows Eden separates groceries from memory, and that Miriam has refused to adjudicate the bed.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Chris dies in the east room before the bed is used, stripped, or sat with. Eden strips it in the morning as housework after a death, and she does not record the stripping as Ellis's choice.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The night ends with the bed still made and unused because no one chose. Eden does not upgrade indecision into a vigil. Miriam does not choose from the chair after the season turns.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Use, laundry, or the sat night remains what the room did. A later renter, if one comes, inherits sheets with that history and not a blank rite.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Miriam is already dead, Eden will not borrow her grandmother's chair or her authority. She still makes Chris choose what the made bed is for, and she will not supply a vigil.

n_open.text: Grandmother is dead and the bed is still made, because the house makes it. I am not her. Sleep in it, strip it, or sit up. I won't call any of those a tribute. Christian isn't here and neither is she. Chris, pick a way for the sheets to look in the morning.

choices.text: Sleep in the bed, with only Eden to name it.
Strip the bed with Eden and leave the mattress bare.

n_end_br.house.slept_eden.text: You slept. I'll say warmth if anyone in Orwell asks, and I'll say it without the story. Change is my job in the morning. Don't help. Helping would make it a scene.

n_end_br.house.stripped_eden.text: Bare. Good. I wanted this and I'm not going to enjoy it in the hallway. The room is a room. If I rent it someday, I won't pretend the sheets were sacred first.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Eden is already dead, Joel will not let the bed become his mother's religion or his daughter's. He asks Chris to use it, strip it, or sit, and he will resent all three without forbidding them.

n_open.text: Eden's dead. Don't you look for her on the trunk. Mother is in the chair and off duty, which means I say the practical part. Sleep, strip, or sit. I hated the extra plate my whole life. I won't pretend a mattress is wiser than I am. Choose, Chris. Then live with me hating it quietly.

choices.text: Sleep in the bed while Joel stays in the hall.
Sit the night up, and let Joel call it unfinished.

n_end_br.house.slept_joel.text: Fine. Warmth. I'll hate the poetry if you add any at breakfast. The sheets got used. Mother can call that true. I call it a bed doing a bed's job in a house that over-explains itself.

n_end_br.house.sat_joel.text: Sitting up. Of course. The house specialty. I'll leave the lamp and I won't admire you. In the morning the bed is still a dare and you are tired. That's an honest ugly outcome. I'll take it over a speech.

chainStages.endingImplications: Sleeping in the bed uses the displaced life as lodging. Stripping it ends the hospitality without a speech. Sitting the night up refuses both use and demolition. Eden remembers which one happened when she later decides whether a living person may rent the room.

chainStages.title: Say Them Once and Dry the Plates
chainStages.summary: In 2022 Eden can keep setting places for people the returns push out, or she can say the names once at the water below the pasture and dry the plates. Joel kept the practice because Miriam asked. Rowan is not asked to become Maren. The certificate stays or is spoken.
chainStages.discovery: Eden has the plates in the rack, not on the table, and Joel has said out loud that keeping them was obedience. The drawer is open to Maren Keel's certificate. The pasture below the house runs to a ditch that counts as water in a dry week. No one is invited to a ceremony. The rack is simply not empty yet.

steps.playerAction: Look at the rack and the open drawer before agreeing to walk anywhere.
Walk with them only as far as the ditch below the Waite pasture, still on their land in Orwell.
Say the names once and dry the plates, or leave the places set and Maren's certificate unspoken as a performance.

n_open.text: I can keep setting places for people the returns push out, or I can say the names once at the ditch and dry the plates. I can't stop you coming back, Rowan. I can stop feeding it a house. Father kept this because Grandmother asked. That is not a belief I have to inherit. Maren's certificate is in the drawer. You don't get to do her life. You only get to hear whether this kitchen stays in the business of extra food.

choices.text: Say the names once at the ditch, then dry the plates for good.
Keep setting the places. Do not make Rowan perform the names.

textVariants.text: The cloth book is already in Middlebury, because you made the names measurements. Eden cannot unmeasurement them by drying a plate. She can stop feeding the practice that remained in the kitchen after the book left. If you say the names at the ditch, you are speaking a list the office also holds, and she wants that doubleness admitted. If you keep the plates, you are feeding a house that no longer even has its own book.

The book stayed in the house, strange housekeeping and all, because you would not make the names a survey. Eden has inherited that decision as a weight, not as a romance. Drying the plates does not throw the book away. It stops the food. She will not let you treat the book and the plates as one sacred object. Joel kept both because Miriam asked. Eden is allowed to split them.

You slept in the east-room bed in the closure year, and the sheets have been ordinary ever since, which Joel still resents and Eden does not. The bed being used is not a reason to keep setting extra food. She is asking about plates, not about whether a mattress can be a person. Maren's certificate is paper. The night you slept there does not make you the life the bed was dressed for.

You are bound to the house and you want names said aloud, which Eden already intends to spend carefully. One saying at the ditch is not a life of plates. She will not let your bond turn a single speaking into a permanent supper. Joel is here so obedience can be distinguished from belief.

n_mid_br.house.released.text: Joel says the first names because he is the one who resented them and they should not only be loved out loud. Cress. Adah. Lou. Nan. Christian. He stops before Maren and looks at Rowan, not for permission, for a limit. He will say Maren if Eden says the list includes the life standing in the yard wearing a different plan.

n_end_br.house.released.text: Maren Keel. There. Six names, once, at a ditch that isn't holy. I'm drying the plates. If you come back in some other year, Rowan, you don't get a setting here. Father's obedience is finished because I finished it, not because it aged into wisdom. The certificate goes back in the drawer as paper. The food stops.

n_mid_br.house.kept.text: Joel swears once, tired, and picks up a plate as if it were heavier than ceramic. Then I keep spending groceries on a belief I don't have. Mother asked. Eden is allowed to refuse and she isn't refusing. Don't you thank me. Thank is how this house gets trapped for another generation.

n_end_br.house.kept.text: The places stay set. I am choosing the food, not the sermon. Maren's certificate stays in the drawer and you will not read it out to prove you can be decent. Rowan, if you eat here, you eat a person's portion, not a symbol's. Father, we reassess when the money fails, not when a visitor feels symbolic. That's the rule now.

branches.summary: The names are spoken once at the ditch, including Maren, and Eden dries the plates. The kitchen leaves the business of extra food.
The plates continue. Joel spends groceries without belief, Maren is not performed, and Eden sets a money-rule rather than a rite.
Joel says the six names once after Eden's death and dries the plates, forbidding a return visit to the ditch.
Joel keeps the settings as spending, not doctrine, after Eden's death, and leaves Maren unread.
Eden speaks the names and dries the plates without Joel's witness, and she refuses to quote the dead as blessing.
Eden keeps the plates by her own choice after Joel's death and will not have Maren read for comfort.

rewards.detail: The Quiet Household either leaves the business of extra food or continues it as groceries with a money-rule, not as a sermon.
Rowan hears whether Maren's name was said once at the ditch or left as a certificate, and knows the house will not ask for a performance of her life.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Rowan dies in the yard before the ditch or the rack is decided. Eden dries nothing in tribute. Joel puts the certificate back and will not say the names to an empty body.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season ends with the plates still in the rack and the certificate still in the drawer. Eden does not upgrade delay into a rite. The next keeper, if different, inherits an unfinished rack.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Dried plates or continued settings remain the kitchen's rule. A later telling of Ellis's returns may mention this house only in that mode, and may not add a choir the ditch did not hold.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Eden is already dead, Joel will not let the last question become a eulogy for his child. He can still say the names once and dry the plates, or keep setting them out of the obedience he already resents.

n_open.text: Eden is dead. I won't use her sentence as a haunting. I know it anyway. Say the names once at the ditch and dry the plates, or keep setting them because my mother asked and I never stopped. Rowan, you don't become Maren to help me decide. You stand there and pick a cost I can actually pay.

choices.text: Say the names with Joel and dry the plates.
Keep the settings, and do not make a ditch-speech.

n_end_br.house.released_joel.text: Once. Cress, Adah, Lou, Nan, Christian, Maren. I hated every extra plate and I said them anyway. The rack dries. If that's Eden's line without Eden, it's also just the end of a grocery. Don't visit the ditch again. Once is the whole design.

n_end_br.house.kept_joel.text: Then I keep spending. Obedience outlived the woman I was obeying and the daughter who could have stopped it. I won't dress that up. The certificate stays paper. You stay Rowan. Supper is food. That's the whole remaining doctrine.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Joel is already dead, Eden cannot use his resentment as a witness. She still chooses the ditch or the plates, and she will not invent his blessing.

n_open.text: Father is dead, so you don't get his complaint as a counterweight. I can still say the names once and dry the plates, or I can keep feeding a practice he kept from obedience. I won't pretend he'd bless either. Rowan, Maren stays unperformed either way. Choose the kitchen.

choices.text: Say the names at the ditch and dry the plates without Joel.
Keep setting places, without calling it Joel's obedience.

n_end_br.house.released_eden.text: Said. Dried. I won't quote my father and I won't quote my grandmother. Six names at a ditch, then ordinary plates for the living. If the house feels thinner, good. Thin was the point. Maren's paper goes back in the drawer.

n_end_br.house.kept_eden.text: They stay set, and not because he would have. He's dead. I am choosing groceries for absent lives with my eyes open. You don't read Maren aloud to make me feel accompanied. Accompaniment isn't on the menu.

chainStages.endingImplications: Dried plates end the household's feeding of the returns. The names, spoken once at the ditch, are not a choir and not a filing. Kept plates mean the kitchen continues to spend food on lives that will not sit down. The ending of Ellis's story can mention this house only in the mode the plates were left.

title: The Second Gate
summary: Fourteen years after the night wheel, Ellis comes back in Ada Smollet's body and finds Ansel Demerritt already changed. The gate is either rebuilt against Ellis's hands, still protecting a lie, or unknown to this face.
discovery: The race at the Weybridge pulp mill sounds different if you knew it in 1952. Nobody sends you. The pin is still on the left, and a younger woman is counting boards without looking up.

steps.playerAction: Stand at the lower gate until Ansel speaks first. Do not put a hand on the pin.
Hear which fourteen years he actually lived before you answer.
Leave the race with one clear fact: barred, complicit again, or still a stranger.

n_fork.text: Ada Smollet's shoes are wrong for the race and the race does not care. Ansel Demerritt is fifty-six and the wheel is not the wheel from the first season. What he says depends on whether the meadow was told.

choices.text: The timber is scarred where the old wheel came off. Walk to that scar.
He looks at Ada and uses a dead man's name. Stay for the correction.
No one at this race remembers a confession. Walk up as a stranger, because you are one.

textVariants.text: The latch is half across. Ada's hand moves before Ellis agrees. Ansel sees the movement and his mouth changes before any introduction.

told_b0.text: Don't introduce the schoolteacher. I repinned this after you opened your mouth to March. More water goes by. Henry's milk tastes like morning and my name is on a lawsuit that is at least about the right hours. You don't get to touch the new pin with a new set of hands and call it help.

told_b1.text: I'm in Waltham now. I came up because Ruth said a stranger was standing too near. I'm not your tragedy and I'm not your proof. I fix pumps. I sleep. If you want a tour of the scar, ask him, not me, and then let me go back to a porch.

told_b2.text: Eli left because the truth had a morning. That was the cost. The gate passes water it didn't pass. I am proud and I am not grateful. Stand off the race or ask me something that isn't forgiveness.

choices.text: Step off the race and leave the pin to the man who moved it.
Ask what the downstream meadow sounds like from this bank now.

told_off.text: Good. Watch from the bank if you must watch. The next time a body of yours reaches left out of habit, Ruth has my instructions. She is not sentimental about uncles or about ghosts.

told_ask.text: It sounds like a man who will not drink with me and a dairy that didn't fail. You don't get to taste it for him. If you go to Waltham, go as a person who already spent the apology in 1952. I won't write you a second one.

kept_b0.text: Ivo— damn it. You. The new one. Fourteen years of a lawsuit with my name on it and the farmers' anger and none of the night we kept. If you came to be forgiven, the wheel doesn't do that. Put your left hand in your pocket. I have called you by a dead surveyor's name and I will not do it twice.

kept_b1.text: I'm still here. That's the whole speech. You didn't tell them. I didn't leave. The milk tastes like milk because we say it does. Don't look at me like you're about to become honest at my expense a decade late.

kept_b2.text: I wrote the night as day until the book believed me. If you break it now, you don't rescue my handwriting. You make me a liar in public after I already paid to be a liar in private. Choose knowing that.

choices.text: Keep the left hand in the pocket and leave the counsel where it is.
Tell the truth now, late, and let Clarice hate the timing.

kept_pocket.text: Then we are the same cowards with better knees. Eli stays. Clarice's book stays neat. When you die again, don't send the next one to confess what you wouldn't.

kept_late.text: Late is still a word I can write. I won't thank you. I'll correct the book in the margin and I will not let you call the margin courage. Eli decides for himself whether the wheel still wants him.

none_b0.text: If you're the county, the hours are posted. If you're lost, the bridge is the other way. I don't know your face and I don't owe a schoolteacher a tour of my pin. State the errand in one sentence or get off the boards.

none_b1.text: Father's been waiting fourteen years for a person who never came back to finish a night. He won't say that to you. I'm saying it so you don't mistake his manners for peace. We run when the contract says. The meadow complains. We outlast the complaint.

none_b2.text: You can leave as a stranger. That's a clean outcome. Or you can tell me why your eyes keep finding the left side of the gate. Strangers don't do that. Liars and old hands do.

choices.text: Leave as a stranger. Do not explain the left hand.
Say that the left side is where Ivo's hand went, and that you are late.

none_stranger.text: Good. We stay a family fact. If you were someone we owed, you missed the year for it. I'm still on the wheel. Remember that when you hear otherwise in some later season.

none_left.text: Then you're not a stranger and you're not in time. I won't rebuild my gate for a sentence that missed the lawsuit's birth. Come back when you can stand the meadow's name in your mouth without shaking.

branches.summary: Ellis is barred from the pin. The rebuilt gate stands as Ansel's work, not a reunion.
Ansel allows the knowledge of the meadow and still forbids Ellis's hands on the pin.
Ada keeps the mill's counsel. The lie gets another fourteen years of handwriting.
The counsel breaks in 1966, too late to be the original mercy and early enough to mark the book.
Ellis never finishes the night-wheel sentence. Ansel's life goes on unconfessed.
Ansel hears the old hand in the new body and refuses a late rebuild.
Clarice settles the second gate as a page, not a reunion.
Ellis leaves the dead millwright's gate to his wife and his niece.
Ruth gives the count in Eli's place and refuses comfort.
Ellis declines to spend Eli's death and leaves the race.

rewards.detail: Ansel's stance toward Ellis is fixed by the life he lived, not by a new greeting.
Ellis knows whether the pin was moved to pass more water, and whether Ada is allowed to touch it.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ada dies at the race, Ansel finishes the shift and does not learn the new face. The next body inherits the gate as rumor only.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: An unfinished visit leaves the mill's story as it was. Eli's fate stays on the flag already set in 1952, or on the default if none was.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: The second-gate choice persists. Ruth, counting boards, remembers which side of the race the stranger was sent to.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Ansel is dead, Clarice keeps the wage book and will not let a new body inherit his grudges or his pin. She finishes the accounting without pretending the man is in the room.

n_open.text: Ansel is not here to misname you. I am. The book is what survived him. If you want the pin, the answer is no, because the answer was no when he had lungs. Speak to the page.

choices.text: Ask her which hours she will correct, and accept no tour.
Leave the book with her and do not ask for the pin.

n_end_page.text: I'll correct what I can bear to see in my own hand. I won't correct the night to soothe you. Take that as the whole inheritance.

n_end_leave.text: Then go. Ruth knows the machine. I know the lie. Between us the county is already staffed.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Eli is already dead, Ruth speaks for the wheel he left or died in. She will not let Ellis use his absence as a soft story.

n_open.text: Eli isn't here. If you came to be forgiven by a man the wheel took or the meadow took, you are late twice. I count boards. Tell me if you are here to change the count.

choices.text: Ask Ruth for the count and do not ask for Eli's voice.
Say nothing about Eli and step off the boards.

n_end_count.text: The count is downstream short and upstream proud. I won't average it. That's the only sentence I owe a stranger.

n_end_silence.text: Silence is the first decent thing. Don't come back to spend it. The pin stays a family tool.

endingImplications: The millwright's second meeting decides whether the office is allowed near the pin. Later water choices with Ruth inherit a barred gate, a renewed silence, or a man who was never confessed to.

title: Frost on the Cistern
summary: At dawn Lottie Harrow holds a tin cup over the New Haven cistern and will not drink the frost ring she says is 1927 silt. Maeve Harrow wants no poem. Lottie wants a number. Rennet Moss's hands have to seal it, taste it, or spoon it toward the survey record.
discovery: The frost on the homestead cistern between the New Haven house and the orchard has drawn a ring that is older than this morning. Lottie has the cup ready and Maeve is already impatient with anything that sounds like weather dressed up as feeling.

steps.playerAction: Stand at the New Haven cistern at dawn and look at the frost ring with Lottie Harrow.
Hear Lottie name the ring as 1927 silt while Maeve Harrow refuses a poem about the cup.
Choose at the stone to seal the cistern, drink and name the taste, or take a spoon toward the record.

n_open.text: The frost on this New Haven cistern drew a ring that is not this year's dirt. I am Lottie Harrow. I have the tin cup and I will not drink. Maeve Harrow can stand there and hate a poem. I want the year. Nineteen twenty-seven. Write it or seal it or taste it, Rennet, but do not leave it pretty.

choices.text: Seal the cistern and leave the cup undrunk.
Drink from the cup and name the taste.
Take a spoon of silt toward the record.

textVariants.text: You look at the New Haven cistern as if the frost already belongs in a book. Lottie Harrow sees that and keeps the tin cup off her mouth. Maeve Harrow says a record is not a verse. The ring is still 1927 silt, and the page will be wrong if nobody counts it before the sun takes the proof.

n_mid_br.seal.text: Maeve Harrow puts the cover on the New Haven cistern herself and will not dress it up. The frost ring is 1927 silt. Lottie Harrow still has the tin cup. Maeve says a lid is a fact. A poem would be a way to own the trees without counting them. She does not want the poem.

n_end_br.seal.text: Lottie Harrow sets the tin cup on the stone of the New Haven cistern and says the number out loud so it cannot be smiled off. Sealed. Nineteen twenty-seven. Maeve Harrow has heard it and does not add a line. The cup stays empty. The silt stays under the lid, counted.

n_mid_br.drink.text: Ellis drinks from Lottie Harrow's tin cup at the New Haven cistern and says the taste before anyone can make it lovely. Cold. Iron. Old flood. Not a story. Maeve Harrow watches the mouth, not the sky. The frost ring breaks where the cup disturbed it. The silt is 1927 and now it has been in a living throat.

n_end_br.drink.text: Lottie Harrow takes the cup back at the New Haven cistern and repeats the taste as if it were a figure. Iron, cold, flood year. Maeve Harrow says that is still not a poem, and she will not write one. The drink is done. The number sits beside it. Nineteen twenty-seven has been in Rennet's mouth.

n_mid_br.spoon.text: Lottie Harrow scrapes one spoon of the dark ring from the New Haven cistern and holds it level. She does not hand Ellis a journey. She hands the spoon and the year. Maeve Harrow says if this leaves the stone it is a sample, not a verse. The survey record can have the silt. The cup still does not get drunk.

n_end_br.spoon.text: Maeve Harrow looks at the spoon and not at Rennet's face. The New Haven cistern keeps the rest of its frost. Lottie Harrow has the number she wanted, and the spoon is for the record, not for a story about daughters and floods. Maeve says take it as dirt. She has been here. That is the whole meeting.

branches.summary: The New Haven cistern is sealed with the 1927 silt under the lid. Lottie Harrow has her number. Maeve Harrow has been met and has refused to turn the frost into a poem.
Ellis drank the cistern at New Haven and named the taste in front of Lottie Harrow and Maeve Harrow. The frost ring is no longer an unnamed mark. Maeve still got no poem.
A spoon of 1927 silt leaves the New Haven cistern toward the survey record. Lottie Harrow counted it. Maeve Harrow allowed the sample and refused the poem.
With Lottie Harrow dead, Maeve Harrow seals the New Haven cistern herself. The cup stays empty. The silt is covered, not sung, and Maeve has been met at the stone.
Maeve Harrow, standing in for Lottie, lets the New Haven cistern be drunk and named. She keeps the words plain. The frost ring is tasted, not versed.
With Maeve Harrow gone, Lottie Harrow seals the New Haven cistern and speaks the year as a count. The cup stays empty. The silt is closed under a number.
Lottie Harrow takes a spoon of 1927 silt from the New Haven cistern for the survey record. Maeve is already gone. The sample is a number, not a verse.

rewards.detail: The New Haven cistern's 1927 silt is entered as a seal, a named taste, or a spoon, and not left as unnamed frost.
Ellis knows the dawn ring on the Harrow cistern is flood silt from 1927, whether the cup was drunk or the lid went on.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: The tin cup stays on the stone of the New Haven cistern. Ellis dies in Rennet Moss's body before Lottie Harrow or Maeve Harrow gets a seal, a taste, or a spoon. The next body is not told which choice was unfinished.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The following wearing finds no sentence about the Harrow cistern. The cup may still be on the stone and the 1927 ring has gone back to looking like weather. Nobody wrote which act was left half done.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: If the cistern was already sealed, drunk, or spooned, that fact holds for the next body. The New Haven stone does not reopen the cup so a later mouth can pick a kinder unfinished version.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Lottie Harrow is gone, so the tin cup has no reckoner. Maeve Harrow stands at the New Haven cistern and will close it or taste it without turning 1927 silt into a poem for the orchard.

n_open.text: Lottie is not here to count. I am Maeve Harrow. The tin cup is on the New Haven cistern stone and the frost ring is still the old silt. I will not make a poem so the county can clap. Seal it or drink it and say the taste in plain words. I do not want a third pretty choice.

choices.text: Seal the cistern with Maeve watching.
Drink and name the taste without a poem.

n_end_br.seal.lottie.text: Maeve Harrow sets the lid on the New Haven cistern and leaves Lottie's tin cup empty on the stone. The frost is 1927 silt and it does not need a line of verse. She says the lid is the number. Rennet can remember a cover. Maeve has been met. She will not garnish it.

n_end_br.drink.lottie.text: Maeve Harrow lets the cup reach Rennet's mouth at the New Haven cistern and then takes it back. She repeats only the words that were dirt: cold, iron, flood. She says that is not a poem and she will not add one for Lottie's sake. The taste has been said. The meeting is done.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Maeve Harrow is not at the stone to forbid a poem. Lottie Harrow still wants a number for the New Haven cistern, so the cup is either sealed as a count or spooned toward the survey record.

n_open.text: Maeve is not here to scold the language. I am Lottie Harrow, and the New Haven cistern still has her frost ring of 1927 silt. The tin cup is in my hand. I do not need a mood. I need the year put somewhere a smile cannot erase. Seal it as a count, or spoon it for the record.

choices.text: Seal the cistern and say the year.
Spoon the silt toward the survey record.

n_end_br.seal.maeve.text: Lottie Harrow covers the New Haven cistern and says nineteen twenty-seven once, the way she says a row count. Maeve is not there to call it a poem or to stop her. The tin cup goes on the stone empty. The number is the seal. That is the record Lottie would trust.

n_end_br.spoon.maeve.text: Lottie Harrow lifts one spoon of silt off the New Haven cistern and does not make Ellis walk it anywhere in this hour. The decision is the spoon. It goes toward the survey record with the year attached. Maeve cannot refuse a poem because Maeve is not here. Lottie refuses the poem herself by counting.

endingImplications: The cistern is either closed, tasted and named, or carried as a spoon of silt toward the record. Maeve has been met at the stone either way, and the next argument about the south block cannot pretend this ring was only dirt.

title: Wrong Boots
summary: Ivo Perch's last boots are in the Harrow homestead boot room. Samuel Harrow watched Rennet Moss's hands find the loose peg. The boots can be worn, wrapped for Helen Perch, or burned in the kitchen stove, and the whole decision ends in the house.
discovery: The boot room still smells of wet wool and orchard mud. One pair is not Samuel's and not this year's hire. The left peg is loose in a way Rennet's hand knows before the eye does, and Samuel has already seen that.

steps.playerAction: Step into the Harrow homestead boot room and look at Ivo Perch's last boots on the peg.
Let Samuel Harrow watch Rennet Moss's hands find the loose peg without explaining it away.
Wear the boots, have Samuel wrap them for Helen Perch, or burn them in the kitchen stove.

n_open.text: Those are Ivo Perch's last boots in my boot room, not yours. I am Samuel Harrow. I watched your hands, Rennet Moss, go to the loose peg before you had a reason you would say. Helen Perch is in Middlebury. You can wear them, I can wrap them for her from here, or the kitchen stove can have them. Decide in this house.

choices.text: Wear Ivo Perch's boots in the boot room.
Have Samuel wrap them for Helen Perch.
Burn the boots in the kitchen stove.

textVariants.text: Samuel Harrow sees Rennet Moss already halfway to finishing the peg, the way an unlatched thing gets finished. Ivo Perch's boots are in the New Haven homestead boot room. Samuel says do not tidy a dead man's leather out of nerves. Wear them, wrap them for Helen, or burn them. Do not hover.

n_mid_br.wear.text: Samuel Harrow watches Rennet Moss pull Ivo Perch's boots on in the homestead boot room and does not bless it. The loose peg swings. The leather is dry at the ankle and dark at the toe. Samuel says the feet are Rennet's today and the habit in the hands is older. He will not call that holy. He calls it wearing.

n_end_br.wear.text: The boots are on. Samuel Harrow nods once at the New Haven boot room floor, not at a sermon. Ivo Perch's last pair leaves the peg on a living body and stays in this house for the day's work. Helen Perch is not summoned. The stove is not opened. Samuel has seen the choice and he is finished looking.

n_mid_br.return.text: Samuel Harrow takes Ivo Perch's boots off the loose peg in the New Haven boot room and wraps them in clean feed paper on the bench. He says Helen Perch can have them in Middlebury because that is her dead. He does not hand Rennet a trip. The wrapping is the return. The scene does not grow a road.

n_end_br.return.text: The parcel sits on the boot room bench, tied, with Helen Perch's name said once by Samuel Harrow. Ivo's boots are returned by that decision, here, not by a walk Ellis gets to perform. Rennet's hands stay off the peg. Samuel dusts his palms. The kitchen stove stays shut. The house is done with the leather.

n_mid_br.burn.text: In the Harrow homestead kitchen the stove takes Ivo Perch's boots in two feeds, leather curling, peg-memory gone to smoke. Samuel Harrow stands in the doorway from the boot room and does not look away. Rennet Moss has nothing in the hands that found the loose peg. The house smells of burned hide, not of a rite.

n_end_br.burn.text: Samuel Harrow shuts the stove draft and says the boots are burned, which is a plain result in a New Haven kitchen. Ivo Perch will not be walked around the orchard in someone else's stride, and Helen Perch will not be handed a parcel. The loose peg is empty. Samuel is not grateful. He is finished.
