deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: If the meadow was already told or the counsel already kept, that single mill fact stands. A later body does not set the other truth on top of it and call the pin rinsed.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Ansel Demerritt is dead. Clarice Demerritt is the wage book that remains, but she is not called in to speak a third scene. Eli Demerritt stands at the left pin and will either tell the meadow and pack, or keep a counsel his father can no longer defend.

n_open.text: Father is not here to forbid a third way. I am Eli Demerritt. The pin is still on the left at this Weybridge gate. If we run tonight, Henry March's milk shows it. Clarice will have to write the night or turn neat and false, and I will not put her in the doorway to say it for me. Tell the meadow and I pack. Keep the counsel and I stay. No old speech.

choices.text: Tell the meadow so Eli can leave.
Keep counsel and stay at the wheel.

n_end_br.tell.ansel.text: Eli Demerritt says the meadow gets the truth and he gets to pack like a man. The Weybridge wheel loses him. Clarice Demerritt's book will have a night in it if she is honest, and he has said so without dragging her out as a voice. Ansel is not alive to rage. The downstream telling stands. The left pin is unpreached.

n_end_br.counsel.ansel.text: Eli Demerritt keeps the counsel and stays. Henry March will taste a morning nobody explained. The Weybridge pin remains a family fact. Clarice must still write the night or lie neatly, and Eli says that burden without making her perform it. Ansel cannot call it usefulness. Eli calls it staying. He does not repeat a dead surveyor's mercy.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Eli Demerritt is already gone from the living gate, so he cannot pack. Ansel Demerritt still chooses whether Henry March's meadow hears the night wheel. Clarice is the book in the background, not a speaker brought on to launder it.

n_open.text: Eli is not here to pack or to stay. I am Ansel Demerritt. The left pin at the Weybridge mill is mine to point at, not yours to sermonize. A night run still shows in Henry March's milk. Clarice will write it or she will lie with a tidy hand. I will not call her out here to be my better self. Tell the meadow or keep the counsel.

choices.text: Tell the meadow without Eli to send.
Keep the counsel with Eli already gone.

n_end_br.tell.eli.text: Ansel Demerritt lets the downstream truth go out. There is no Eli in the race to leave like a man, so the telling does not pretend that departure. The Weybridge contract takes the stain anyway. Clarice Demerritt must write a night that happened. Ansel says do not add Ivo Perch's late mercy on top. The meadow is told. That is the whole cut.

n_end_br.counsel.eli.text: Ansel Demerritt keeps the counsel. The Waltham milk will complain without a named cause. Eli cannot be saved by silence because Eli is not in the mill. Clarice still has to write or lie. Ansel puts his left hand near the pin and tells Rennet not to finish an older gate for him. The family fact holds. The meadow stays uninformed.

endingImplications: Either the Waltham meadow is told and Eli leaves because the truth was said, or the mill's counsel is kept and the night stays a family fact. Clarice's book will have to match. Both mill truths are not kept together.

title: Flour and Marble
summary: Agnes Holt lives above a damp room in the Middlebury Marble Works. When the race opens at night her floor sweats and her boy coughs. She wants the damp on the third step surveyed, not the proud wheel. The race hour goes to her floor or stays with the wheel. Ansel is not called in to speak.
discovery: The third step above the race is dark at the edges and damp in the middle of a dry evening. Agnes talks about rent, dust, and a cough. She is not a figure for marble. She is a tenant who can point at a board.

steps.playerAction: Climb to Agnes Holt's third step above the Marble Works race and feel the damp in the board.
Hear that a night opening sweats her floor and starts her boy's cough, and that she wants that surveyed.
Give the race hour to her floor, or keep it with the wheel, without calling Ansel up to argue.

n_open.text: When they open the race at night, this floor sweats and my boy coughs. I am Agnes Holt. You are on the third step of my stair in the Marble Works, not on a proud wheel. Survey the damp. I do not need Ansel Demerritt in the doorway to call it a contract. Give the hour to this floor or keep it with the wheel. Say it here, where the water actually arrives.

choices.text: Give the race hour to Agnes's floor.
Keep the race hour with the wheel.

textVariants.text: Agnes Holt watches Rennet Moss respect the level of the water more than the pride of the machine, and she wants that respect aimed at a step. The Marble Works race will open or it will not. Her floor in Middlebury sweats either way it is told. The boy coughs. Give the hour to the tenant or keep it on the wheel. Do not admire the stone.

n_mid_br.floor.text: Agnes Holt puts her palm on the third step and says this is the survey, then. The Marble Works race does not get the night hour. Her floor stops being a side effect. The boy's cough is not a mood the wheel may outvote. She does not ask Ellis to drag Ansel Demerritt up the stair to be shamed. The hour is given. The damp is the witness.

n_end_br.floor.text: The race hour belongs to the tenant. Agnes Holt says it in the stairwell so the Marble Works cannot rewrite it as a mechanical necessity she failed to understand. Middlebury still has a wheel. It does not have this night. The third step is the place that was surveyed. She will remember who stood on it. She does not offer gratitude as rent.

n_mid_br.wheel.text: Agnes Holt hears the hour stay with the wheel and takes her hand off the step as if the board had lied. The Marble Works race will open at night. Her floor will sweat. The boy will cough. She says she asked for a survey of the damp and got a preference for the machine. Ansel is not summoned to gloat. She will not give him the scene.

n_end_br.wheel.text: The wheel keeps the hour. Agnes Holt states the consequence without a speech about marble's dignity. The third step in the Marble Works stays wet and unofficial. Ellis chose the race. She will pay her rent and hear the cough and know the survey stood on her stair and sided elsewhere. That is the record she is left holding in her own mouth.

branches.summary: The night hour of the Marble Works race is given to Agnes Holt's floor. The third step is surveyed instead of the proud wheel. Her boy's cough is treated as the reason, not the poetry.
The race hour stays with the wheel. Agnes Holt's damp third step in the Marble Works is seen and not given the night. The proud machine keeps the water. Ansel never speaks.
Marie Rouleau assigns the Marble Works night hour to Agnes's floor after Agnes is gone. The damp step outranks the wheel. The decision is a schedule, not a eulogy.
With Agnes dead, Marie still lets the wheel keep the race hour. The Marble Works stair remains wet and unpromoted. She names the cost and does not reverse it.

rewards.detail: Agnes Holt's third step in the Marble Works is a place the race hour can be spoken, not only the wheel below it.
Ellis knows a night opening of the Middlebury race sweats the tenant's floor and starts the boy's cough.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Ellis dies on the third step before the hour is given or kept. Agnes Holt's stair stays wet and unlogged. The Marble Works wheel is not instructed. The boy's cough has no survey attached to it by this death.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The next body finds the damp still unofficial. Nobody recorded whether the race night belonged to the tenant or the wheel. The Marble Works keeps a wet step and an unanswered hour.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: If the hour was already given to the floor or kept with the wheel, that choice stays logged in the living memory of the stair. A later body does not re-survey it into a softer machine.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Agnes Holt is dead and the stair still sweats. Marie Rouleau, who knows a night kitchen's version of other people's hours, stands on the third step and will give the race to the floor or leave it on the wheel.

n_open.text: Agnes is not on this stair. I am Marie Rouleau, and I know what a night hour costs a room that is trying to sleep. The Marble Works floor still sweats when the race opens, and the boy still coughs in a room she paid for. Do not parade the proud wheel in here as a guest. Give the hour to this third step or keep it with the machine.

choices.text: Give the hour to the damp step.
Leave the hour on the wheel.

n_end_br.floor.agnes.text: Marie Rouleau gives the night to the third step and not to the wheel. The Marble Works race can be proud in daylight. Agnes Holt is not alive to hear the cough ease, so Marie says the ease anyway, as a schedule, not as a memorial. The tenant's floor gets the hour. She will not let the stone have the last word.

n_end_br.wheel.agnes.text: Marie Rouleau leaves the hour with the wheel and does not pretend Agnes Holt would have blessed it. The third step in the Marble Works stays wet. The cough keeps its nights. She says a kitchen woman can recognize a theft of sleep without stopping every theft. The machine keeps the water. The stair stays a private dampness.

endingImplications: The night hour of the race is either given to Agnes Holt's floor or kept with the wheel. The third step becomes a surveyed fact or stays a private wetness. No proud machine gets to be the only mouth.

title: The Eel Passage
summary: In 1980 Ruth Demerritt is the millwright at the Weybridge gate, not Ansel. Cutting an eel passage costs her head of water. Keeping the head costs the creek a generation. She is not Ellis's penance. Louis Pell can tell her to cut or to keep. The pin stays hers.
discovery: The gate is pinned the way Ruth pinned it. Eels are a generation in the creek, not a symbol of anyone's grandfather. She talks like a person who inherited a machine and a lawsuit and will not inherit a silence.

steps.playerAction: Meet Ruth Demerritt at the Weybridge pulp mill gate in 1980 and look at the pin she set.
Hear the head of water she would lose to an eel passage and the generation the creek would lose without one.
Tell her to cut the passage or keep the head, and do not offer Louis Pell's hands as penance.

n_open.text: I am Ruth Demerritt, not Ansel, and not your penance. This is the Weybridge gate in 1980, and you are Louis Pell with empty hands. An eel passage costs me head. A kept head costs the creek a generation. I will say the loss out loud either way. Choose the cut or the head. Do not touch the pin and call it inheritance.

choices.text: Cut the eel passage and spend the head.
Keep the head and spend the generation.

textVariants.text: Ruth Demerritt hears Louis Pell lean toward whatever is alive in the creek and she stops it from becoming a sermon. The Weybridge mill still needs head. The eels are a generation, not a moral costume. She says the living are on both sides of the gate, including her. Cut the passage or keep the head. Leave the penance in your pocket.

n_mid_br.cut.text: Ruth Demerritt names the loss before she moves the gate. Head of water, gone to an eel passage, at the Weybridge mill, by her hand and not by Louis Pell's guilt. The creek gets a generation's road. The wheel gets less. She says it out loud so it cannot return later as Ellis's private apology. The pin will sit differently because she says so.

n_end_br.cut.text: The passage is cut. Ruth Demerritt states the new lack of head as a millwright's fact, not as a redemption. Weybridge keeps a wheel that gives something up. The eels are not thanked and not mythologized. Louis does not get to have fixed a grandfather by sponsoring a fish. The loss was said. The gate is hers, altered.

n_mid_br.head.text: Ruth Demerritt keeps the head and does not hide the other price. The creek loses a generation of eels. The Weybridge wheel keeps its water. She says that sentence without asking Louis Pell to look ashamed enough to share it. Ansel is not the author of this refusal. She is. The pin stays where she set it.

n_end_br.head.text: Head kept. Ruth Demerritt repeats it so the mill cannot call the choice weather. The eel passage is not cut. A generation in the creek is the cost she agreed to say at the Weybridge gate. Ellis is not forgiven and not condemned into a role. Louis's hands stay off the pin. The record is her refusal, spoken once and enough.

branches.summary: Ruth Demerritt cuts an eel passage at the Weybridge gate and spends her head of water. She says the loss aloud. The act is not accepted as Ellis's penance for an older pin.
Ruth keeps the head of water at the Weybridge mill. The eel passage is not cut. She names the creek's lost generation herself and does not hand the guilt to Ellis.
Denis Rouleau cuts the eel passage after Ruth is gone, and he spends the head without making it Ellis's penance. The Weybridge gate changes by a spoken loss, not by inheritance.
With Ruth dead, Denis keeps the head of water at the Weybridge gate. The passage is not cut. He states the generational cost and refuses to call the choice penance.

rewards.detail: The 1980 Weybridge gate has a record of either an eel passage cut or a head of water kept, spoken as Ruth's loss or her surrogate's.
Ellis knows the passage spends Ruth Demerritt's head and the closed gate spends a generation of the creek, and neither is a personal absolution.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Ellis dies at the Weybridge gate before the cut or the keep. The pin stays as Ruth Demerritt set it. Louis Pell's hands do not become a penance and do not become a tool. The eel passage is unchosen.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The next body finds Ruth's pin unrevised. No passage was cut and no head was newly justified. The creek's generation and the mill's water remain an argument Ellis did not finish.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: If the passage was already cut or the head already kept, the gate holds that loss. A later wearing does not unpin it to make Ellis feel squared with an older mill.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Ruth Demerritt is dead and the gate is still pinned as she left it. Denis Rouleau will not turn the eel choice into Ellis's penance. He will cut the passage or keep the head as a loss somebody says aloud at Weybridge.

n_open.text: Ruth is not here to refuse being your penance. I am Denis Rouleau, and I will refuse it for the room. The Weybridge gate is pinned the way she pinned it. An eel passage still costs head. Keeping the head still costs the creek a generation. You are Louis Pell. Do not touch that pin to feel historic. Cut, or keep. Say the loss.

choices.text: Cut the passage in Ruth's absence.
Keep the head Ruth pinned in place.

n_end_br.cut.ruth.text: Denis Rouleau says the passage gets cut and the head gets spent. He does not dedicate it to Ruth Demerritt's memory or to Ellis's old hands. The Weybridge creek gets a road for eels. The wheel gets less water. The loss is said on the gate she pinned, by a man who will not let a surveyor wear it home as absolution.

n_end_br.head.ruth.text: Denis Rouleau keeps the head. The eel passage stays uncut. He says the creek loses a generation and that this is not Louis Pell paying a family debt. Ruth Demerritt's pin remains the pin. Weybridge does not get a softer legend. The water stays with the wheel because someone admitted the animal cost and still chose the head.

endingImplications: The Weybridge gate either spends Ruth's head of water on an eel passage or keeps the head and spends the creek's next generation. The loss is said out loud. It is not filed as Ellis's apology for an older gate.

title: Strike Soup
summary: A wage fight in 1966. Upstairs the Vergennes office is writing night hours out of the book. Downstairs Marie Rouleau's kitchen is eating them. Denis Rouleau says if you eat with the crew, stay for the bitter part. Ada Smollet chooses a table from the kitchen, not by running an errand.
discovery: The night kitchen on South Water Street is loud with spoons and quiet about the office above. Marie ladles as an argument. Denis watches who will leave before the soup turns honest. The body in the doorway is Ada's, and the hours are the real wage.

steps.playerAction: Enter Marie Rouleau's Vergennes night kitchen while the wage fight is still in the bowls.
Hear Denis Rouleau say the crew's soup includes the bitter part, and see the office writing night hours out.
Eat in the kitchen, or from the doorway choose the upstairs table, and do not come back down for comfort.

n_open.text: Upstairs they are writing the night hours out of the book. Down here we are eating them. I am Marie Rouleau. This is my kitchen in Vergennes, and you are Ada Smollet if that is the mouth you brought. Denis Rouleau says if you eat with the crew you stay for the bitter part. Take a bowl in the room you are willing to be counted in. The doorway is as far as the other choice needs to travel.

choices.text: Eat in the kitchen and stay for the bitter part.
From the doorway, choose the office table.

textVariants.text: Marie Rouleau sees Ada Smollet ready to sign the office's cleanliness by sitting near it. The Vergennes kitchen is eating the night hours the upstairs book is erasing. Denis Rouleau will not let a signature happen by accident. Eat here and stay bitter, or say the upstairs table from this doorway. Do not drift into a cleaner page.

n_mid_br.kitchen.text: Denis Rouleau puts the bitter part in front of Ada Smollet before the bread can make a conscience. The Vergennes crew is eating hours the office is writing out. He says staying is the point. Marie Rouleau ladles like a count. If Ellis wanted the good feeling without the aftertaste, the kitchen is the wrong room. He watches to see the spoon come back up.

n_end_br.kitchen.text: Marie Rouleau counts Ada in the kitchen. The night hours are eaten where they are lived, not erased upstairs. Denis Rouleau got the bitter part witnessed. The doorway was not used as an exit. Vergennes has one more body on the crew's side of the wage fight, and the bowl is not a souvenir. It is the table Ellis claimed.

n_mid_br.upstairs.text: Denis Rouleau hears the upstairs choice spoken from the kitchen doorway and blocks the sentimental return in advance. Vergennes does not need Ada Smollet to climb as an errand inside this scene. The decision is the sentence. He says do not come down after for the good conscience. Marie Rouleau holds the ladle still. The office is writing the night hours out. That is the table just chosen.

n_end_br.upstairs.text: Marie Rouleau says the office, then, and turns the next bowl away from the doorway. Ellis is counted upstairs with the people erasing the night hours. The kitchen does not keep a chair warm. Denis Rouleau's warning stands. The wage fight has Ada's absence in it, decided without a trip, in the Vergennes doorway, where both rooms could hear.

branches.summary: Ellis eats in Marie Rouleau's Vergennes kitchen and stays for the bitter part Denis required. The night hours are counted with the crew. The office does not get this bowl.
From Marie's kitchen doorway Ellis chooses the upstairs office table. Denis forbids a later return for conscience. The night hours being written out are the side Ada is counted on.
Denis seats Ellis with the Vergennes crew after Marie is gone and keeps the bitter part in the meal. The kitchen table is the wage allegiance. Upstairs does not get the bowl.
With Marie dead, Denis hears Ellis choose the upstairs office from the kitchen doorway. No errand is run. The crew's bitter part is refused, and the return is closed.
Marie counts Ellis at the kitchen table without Denis alive to demand the bitter part. She serves it anyway. The Vergennes crew keeps the night hours in the meal.
Marie hears the upstairs choice from her own doorway after Denis is gone. The bowl is not held. Ellis is counted with the office writing the night hours out.

rewards.detail: Ada Smollet was counted either in Marie Rouleau's kitchen with the crew or with the office upstairs, by a doorway decision.
Ellis knows the 1966 wage fight is night hours written out of the book above and eaten in the Vergennes kitchen below.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Ellis dies in the Vergennes doorway before a table is claimed. Marie Rouleau clears the bowl. Denis Rouleau does not get a witness for the bitter part. No room counts Ada Smollet among its eaters.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The next body is not claimed by the kitchen or the office. The wage fight continues, and the night hours stay a meal or an erasure without Ellis's name attached to either.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: If a table was already chosen, the count holds. A later wearing does not sit the other seat to balance Marie's kitchen against the upstairs book.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Marie Rouleau is dead and the ladle has no owner. Denis Rouleau keeps the Vergennes kitchen open for the bitter part of the wage fight, and he will hear a doorway choice for upstairs without allowing a later rinse.

n_open.text: Marie is not here to ladle the argument. I am Denis Rouleau. The Vergennes kitchen is still eating the night hours the office is writing out. If you sit with the crew, Ada, you stay when it turns bitter. If you want the upstairs table, say it from this doorway. Do not come back down to be forgiven by a dead woman's soup.

choices.text: Sit with the crew for the bitter part.
Choose the office aloud from the doorway.

n_end_br.kitchen.marie.text: Denis Rouleau lets Ada Smollet sit and then he does not sweeten the second half. The Vergennes crew keeps the night hours in their mouths. The office does not get this body. Marie cannot nod. Denis says the staying is the count. The bowl is claimed by the kitchen. He will remember if Ellis tries to narrate it later as a visit.

n_end_br.upstairs.marie.text: Denis Rouleau takes the doorway sentence as final. Ada Smollet is with the office that writes the night hours out. The Vergennes kitchen does not save a bowl. Marie Rouleau is not alive to be disappointed in person, so Denis does the disappointment without theater. He says do not return. The upstairs table is the one that was chosen.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Denis Rouleau is dead and cannot police the aftertaste. Marie Rouleau still makes Ada Smollet pick a table in the Vergennes kitchen: eat the night hours with the crew, or say the office from the doorway and lose the bowl.

n_open.text: Denis is not here to warn you about the bitter part. I am Marie Rouleau, so I will say it shorter. This Vergennes kitchen is eating the hours upstairs is writing out. Sit and be counted with the crew, Ada Smollet, or stand in that doorway and choose the office. I will not hold a bowl for a person who wants both rooms.

choices.text: Take the kitchen bowl and be counted.
Choose upstairs from the kitchen doorway.

n_end_br.kitchen.denis.text: Marie Rouleau puts the bowl down and leaves it bitter on purpose, since Denis is not alive to insist. Ada Smollet is counted in the Vergennes kitchen. The night hours stay in the crew's supper. The office can erase paper. It does not erase this spoon. She says the table is chosen. She means the room, not a mood.

n_end_br.upstairs.denis.text: Marie Rouleau hears the office chosen in the doorway and clears the unused bowl. There is no walk to perform. Ada Smollet is counted upstairs, where the night hours leave the book. Denis cannot forbid the return, so Marie forbids it herself. The Vergennes kitchen does not keep a conscience warm. The wage table is the one above.

endingImplications: Ellis is counted in the kitchen with the crew or counted with the office upstairs. The night hours stay eaten or stay erased, and the doorway decision is the whole allegiance. No second visit repairs the table.

title: Clark's Signature
summary: In 1994 Clark Seaver wants Hannah Greer's living hand to re-sign Ivo Perch's clean certification so a Leicester culvert becomes fundable. He says moods do not move water. Willa is not in the room. This is his promotion and a smaller gate, not the whole flood book.
discovery: The survey room off Court Street has one signature line and a culvert estimate, not a theology. Clark is smooth and specific. The clean certification is a tool he can spend on Leicester if Hannah's hand agrees.

steps.playerAction: Sit at the Middlebury survey table while Clark Seaver lays out Ivo's clean certification and a Leicester culvert.
Hear him say Hannah Greer's living signature would move the funding, and that moods do not move water.
Sign the clean line in Hannah's hand, or refuse it, without preaching the whole flood book.

n_open.text: Re-sign the clean certification in your living hand and the Leicester culvert becomes fundable. I am Clark Seaver. This is the survey office in Middlebury, and you are Hannah Greer today, not a mood from 1938. Ivo Perch's clean line is the one I need. Refuse and you are protecting a feeling. Moods do not move water. Culverts do. This is a smaller gate. Leave the whole flood out of it.

choices.text: Sign the clean certification in Hannah's hand.
Refuse to re-sign the clean line.

textVariants.text: Clark Seaver sees Hannah Greer treat the clean certification as the record that will have to hold. He wants that instinct spent on a Leicester culvert, here in the Middlebury survey office. He says a held record that never signs is just a delay with better posture. Sign, or refuse. Leave the old margin theology in the drawer.

n_mid_br.sign.text: Clark Seaver turns the page so the signature line is the only thing alive on it. Hannah Greer's hand is the promotion's instrument. The Leicester culvert gets a fundable sentence because the clean certification is repeated. He does not ask for a speech about Ivo Perch's mercy or failure. Middlebury's office gets a smaller gate moved by ink. He watches the hand, not the conscience.

n_end_br.sign.text: Signed. Clark Seaver says the culvert can be asked for now, which was the point. The clean certification has a living hand under Ivo's old cleanliness. Hannah Greer will be the name on the ask. He does not call it courage. He calls it water moving because a paper moved. The survey office has its promotion piece. The larger flood is not re-argued.

n_mid_br.refuse.text: Clark Seaver hears the refusal and does not reach for the flood story to punish it. He says the Leicester culvert stays unfunded because Hannah Greer would not put a living hand on a clean line. Moods do not move water. He believes he has just watched a mood. The Middlebury table keeps a blank. He will not supply a kinder interpretation to help the office feel serious.

n_end_br.refuse.text: Refused. Clark Seaver leaves the signature line blank and says he will call it fear if anyone asks, because fear is a mood and moods do not dig a culvert. The promotion does not get its paper. Hannah's hand stays off Ivo's cleanliness. The smaller gate in Leicester is not opened by this room today. He does not require the rest of the book to be angry.

branches.summary: Hannah Greer's living hand re-signs the clean certification. Clark Seaver's Leicester culvert becomes fundable. The Middlebury office gets the smaller gate it asked for, without a flood-book sermon.
Ellis refuses Clark Seaver's re-signature. The Leicester culvert is not fundable by Hannah's hand. Clark keeps the blank and is prepared to call the refusal fear. The flood book stays unpreached.

Hannah signs the clean certification with Willa Seaver watching, after Clark is gone. The Leicester culvert can be funded. Willa names the signature as the office avoiding account, not as plumbing heroism.
Willa Seaver records Hannah's refusal without Clark alive to call it fear. The clean certification stays unsigned. The Leicester culvert is not fundable from this smaller gate.

rewards.detail: The Middlebury survey office has Hannah Greer's signature on the clean certification, or it has a blank Clark can call fear.
Ellis answered a promotion and a Leicester culvert, a smaller gate than the flood, with a living hand or a refusal.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: Ellis dies at the Middlebury table before Hannah Greer's hand signs or refuses. The signature line stays blank. Clark Seaver will call the blank fear. The Leicester culvert is not funded by a death, and the flood book is not given a new sermon.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The next body finds the clean line still unsigned and Clark's word for it already waiting. No promotion was completed. The smaller gate stays a blank that fear is allowed to explain.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: If the certification was already signed or already refused, the survey office keeps that hand's act. A later wearing does not reopen the Leicester culvert to launder Clark's promotion.

ifNpcDead.resolution: Clark Seaver is dead and cannot call a blank fear in person. Willa Seaver puts the same clean line on the Middlebury table and says a clean signature is how the office stays unaccountable. Hannah can still sign or refuse the smaller Leicester gate.

n_open.text: Clark is not here to say moods do not move water. I am Willa Seaver. The clean certification is on this Middlebury table, and he wanted Hannah Greer's living hand on it so a Leicester culvert could be funded. I think a clean signature is how this office stays inherited and unaccountable. Sign it if you mean that. Refuse it if you mean the blank. This is still a smaller gate.

choices.text: Sign the clean line in front of Willa.
Leave the signature line blank.

n_end_br.sign.clark.text: Willa Seaver watches Hannah Greer sign and does not congratulate the culvert. The Leicester paper becomes fundable by a cleanliness she distrusts. The Middlebury office stays able to inherit itself. She says Clark would have called this water moving. She calls it unaccountable ink. The signature is done. She will not enlarge it into the whole flood.

n_end_br.refuse.clark.text: Willa Seaver leaves the line blank with Hannah's refusal and does not let it be renamed fear in Clark Seaver's absence. The Leicester culvert stays unasked by this hand. She says a blank is not yet accountability, but a clean signature would have been the wrong certainty. The Middlebury table keeps the smaller gate shut. She files nothing pretty over the empty line.

endingImplications: The living hand either repeats the clean certification and the Leicester culvert becomes fundable, or the line stays refused. Clark will call a refusal a mood. The office's smaller gate is answered without a full sermon of the flood.

title: The Dust Counts
summary: At the limestone cut above Bristol, Vito Pellegrin holds dust counts the survey office has not posted. Louis Pell's body is known here as the cook's son. Posting lets the wives read the numbers, handing them only to the workers lets the paper be lost on purpose, and Norma Seaver's delay is the third sin.
discovery: Louis Pell is at the overhang because this body comes from the Bristol cut, and Vito Pellegrin stops him under the face with a folded sheet. The counts are not a speech about powder. They are the week's dust, unposted, and Gina Pellegrin is already watching who will be allowed to see them.

steps.playerAction: Stand under the Bristol overhang in Louis Pell's body and hear Vito Pellegrin separate a dust count from a figure of speech.
Choose whether the wives can read the sheet, the workers alone hold it, or Norma Seaver's delay remains the office's answer.
Leave the paper where that choice puts it, and let Gina Pellegrin hear which sin was picked at the cut.

n_open.text: These are counts, Louis, not a poem I am making about powder. The office has not posted them. Nail the sheet at this Bristol cut where the wives can read the dust, or hand it to the men and we can lose it on purpose. Norma Seaver says wait. Those are three different sins, and Gina is standing right there.

choices.text: Post the dust counts where the wives can read them.
Hand the counts to the workers and no one else.
Obey Norma Seaver and leave the delay in place.

textVariants.text: You are the one who thinks a record should hold, Louis Pell, so do not look at me as if this sheet were weather. The Bristol cut has numbers the office has not posted. Gina Pellegrin can watch you choose the board, the pocket, or Norma Seaver's delay. I am not decorating the dust. I am counting it.

n_mid_post.text: Then it goes on the board by the shack door, Louis, where a wife walking up from Bristol can see the week's dust without asking a man to remember it. I will not pretty the nail. Vito Pellegrin means the numbers. Norma Seaver does not get to call this patience.

n_end_post.text: Posted. The wives can see the dust counts, and I will not take the sheet down because the office is shy. Gina watched the nail go in. If Norma Seaver wants a delay, she can come to the Bristol cut and argue with a number that is already in the weather.

n_mid_hand.text: Then it lives in jackets, Louis. Vito Pellegrin already told you the men can lose a paper on purpose, and he was not making a riddle. The wives will not see this week's dust unless a cutter decides to be braver than the Bristol office.

n_end_hand.text: Handed, and not posted. The workers have the counts. We can fold them into a pocket and let the rain at the cut finish the argument. That is the sin you picked, Louis. Gina heard it. Do not tell me later you thought I was speaking in pictures about powder.

n_mid_delay.text: Then Norma's delay is the fact, Louis. The sheet stays off the board and out of the men's hands, and the Bristol cut goes on breathing limestone while the office practices neatness. I chalk names. I cannot chalk a number nobody will hold still for.

n_end_delay.text: Delayed, then. Norma Seaver keeps her wait, and this paper does not meet a wife or a pocket today. I said the counts were counts. You picked the office's silence over either sin I offered. Gina can remember that Louis Pell stood here and let the delay stand.

branches.summary: Ellis has the dust counts posted at the Bristol cut, where the wives can read them. Vito Pellegrin treats the sheet as exposure, not poetry, and Norma Seaver's delay does not cover the nail.
The dust counts are handed only to the workers at the Bristol cut. They are not posted, so they can be lost on purpose, and the wives do not get a look at the week's numbers.
Norma Seaver's delay is obeyed. The dust counts stay unposted and are not handed to the workers, so neither the wives nor the cutters have the week's numbers from the Bristol cut.
With Vito Pellegrin dead, Gina Pellegrin posts the dust counts at the Bristol cut so the wives can read the week's exposure instead of inheriting a silence.
With Vito dead, Gina hands the dust counts only to the workers. The sheet can be lost on purpose, and the wives never get the posted numbers at the Bristol cut.
With Gina Pellegrin dead, Elena Pellegrin posts Vito's dust counts at the Bristol cut so the wives can read the exposure the office delayed.
With Gina dead, Elena leaves Norma Seaver's delay in place. The Bristol dust counts stay unposted, and neither the wives nor a memorial nail gets the week's sheet.

rewards.detail: The week's dust counts at the Bristol cut become a posted sheet, a workers' paper, or an office delay, and that status is the record.
Vito Pellegrin's dust talk is exposure counted in the limestone cut, not a poetic name for powder, and Louis Pell's body already belongs to that work.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ellis dies in Louis Pell's body before the dust sheet is settled, the paper stays in a pocket at the Bristol cut. Vito Pellegrin does not get a witness, and the wives never see the counts Gina was watching.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season turns with the dust counts still pocketed. Norma Seaver's delay becomes the habit, and no one at the Bristol overhang can point to a posting Louis Pell agreed to in the open.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Louis Pell's death does not pull a settled sheet back into a pocket. Whether the Bristol counts were posted, handed to the workers, or left under Norma Seaver's delay, that choice stays after the body.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Vito Pellegrin is dead, Gina Pellegrin holds the unposted dust counts at the Bristol cut. The sheet is still numbers, not a poem about powder, and Louis Pell's body does not get to pretend the office already showed them.

n_open.text: Vito is not here to say it, so I will. These dust counts never got posted, Louis. The wives can read them on the board at the Bristol cut, or the workers can have them and lose them on purpose. I do not have his cough. I have his sheet. Norma Seaver is still waiting, and I will not call that a kindness by myself.

choices.text: Have Gina post the counts on the cut's board.
Have Gina hand the sheet only to the workers.

n_end_vdead_post.text: Then I nail them. The wives coming up to this Bristol face can read the dust without a dead man's permission. Louis Pell, you did not make the numbers prettier by being the cook's son. You only stopped them staying in a pocket Vito cannot lose anymore.

n_end_vdead_hand.text: Then the men get it, and nobody nails it. They can lose it on purpose the way Vito said they might, and the wives of this cut will not see the week's dust. I will not tell Norma Seaver I was braver than I was. Louis, that pocket is a decision, not a draft.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Gina Pellegrin is dead, Elena Pellegrin stands in at the Bristol cut with the unposted counts. She will not let Louis Pell treat the sheet as supper talk, and she will not invent Gina's chalk as a substitute for a number.

n_open.text: Gina is not here to watch your face, Louis, so I will do it without her chalk. Vito Pellegrin's dust counts are still off the board. Post them where the wives can see, hand them to the cutters who can lose them, or bow to Norma Seaver's delay. I kept this shack's grace. I can keep a number honest too.

choices.text: Tell Elena to post the counts for the wives.
Tell Elena to leave Norma Seaver's delay alone.

n_end_gdead_post.text: Posted, then, and Gina does not have to be alive for a wife to read the dust. Vito's numbers go on the Bristol board. I will not mix them with a grace. Louis Pell, if you wanted a poem you came to the wrong woman in the wrong cut.

n_end_gdead_delay.text: Then the delay stands, and I will not steal Norma's sin to make myself kind. The counts stay unposted, Louis, and the wives do not get a surprise board because Gina is dead. Vito can hate me for it. He already knew waiting was a choice with a body.

endingImplications: The Bristol cut either shows its dust to the wives, trusts the workers with a paper they may destroy, or accepts Norma Seaver's delay. Later talk about lungs at this face has a sheet, a pocket, or an office silence behind it, and Louis Pell was standing there when it was chosen.

title: The Powder Key
summary: The key to the powder shack above Bristol was in Rennet Moss's old coat, which came to Ada Smollet through Helen Perch's estate. Helen is dead and silent. Vito Pellegrin calls a key near powder a safety problem. Redmond Mahey has walked up from Shoreham with his tongs and can spoil the bit here.
discovery: Ada Smollet is at the powder shack because the coat from Helen Perch's estate still has a key in it, and Vito Pellegrin will not talk about that key anywhere but here. Redmond Mahey is already on the hill with forge tongs, not waiting in Shoreham for a later errand.

steps.playerAction: Stand at the Bristol powder shack in Ada Smollet's body with Rennet Moss's key and both men in earshot.
Choose whether the key opens the shack, goes back to Vito unused, or is spoiled by Redmond Mahey's tongs on this hill.
Leave the key used, returned, or ruined, and do not carry the argument down to Shoreham to finish it.

n_open.text: A key in a dead coat is a story, Ada, until it is a key beside powder. Helen Perch is not here to explain the estate, and I will not pretend this shack above Bristol is a parlor. Redmond Mahey came up from Shoreham with his tongs. Use it, give it back unused, or let him spoil it. I am talking about hands, not symbols.

choices.text: Use the key and open the powder shack.
Return the key to Vito without using it.
Have Redmond spoil the key here with his tongs.

textVariants.text: I know the look, Ada. An unturned key bothers you the way an open gate does. This is the powder shack, not a proverb. Rennet's coat put it in your hand through Helen's estate, and Redmond Mahey did not climb from Shoreham so you could stand here unfinished. Decide before the bit starts to feel like a duty.

n_mid_use.text: Then turn it while I am standing here, and do not ask me to bless the click. I brought tongs from Shoreham, not a speech. Vito Pellegrin is right that a key near powder is a safety problem. Using it once, in daylight, at this Bristol door, is still using it.

n_end_use.text: Used. The shack is open, Ada, and the key from Rennet Moss's coat has done the thing I did not want a secret to do. Redmond can put his tongs down. I will lock up again with my own bit. Yours is no longer a mystery in Helen's cloth. It is a key that has met powder.

n_mid_ret.text: Unused is a real word if you mean it. Give it to Vito and keep your hand off my tongs. I did not walk up from Shoreham to watch a ceremony. If the key goes back into his palm and never enters the Bristol lock, I will call that restraint. I will not call it my work.

n_end_ret.text: Returned, and unused. I have it, Ada. It will not go back into Rennet's coat, and it will not turn this lock today. Redmond Mahey can take his tongs home to Shoreham. A key near powder was the problem. In my hand, unused, it is not a temptation with your name on it.

n_mid_spoil.text: Say it plain, then. I spoil the bit here, at the shack, with the tongs I carried up. I am not dragging you back to the Shoreham forge to make a journey of it. Vito Pellegrin hears you. The key from that coat will not open anything when I am done, and the reason you were afraid can stay your own.

n_end_spoil.text: Agreed. It is spoiled. The bit is a twist of metal, Ada, and this Bristol door will not know it. Vito can stop imagining a coat pocket beside the powder. I am not sorry. Helen Perch's estate does not get a working key just because the cloth was careful. I came up the hill for this and I am finished.

branches.summary: Ada uses the powder-shack key in daylight at the Bristol door, with Vito Pellegrin and Redmond Mahey present. The key is no longer an unused secret from Helen Perch's estate.
The powder key is returned unused to Vito Pellegrin at the shack. It does not open the lock, and Redmond Mahey does not spoil it. The coat from Helen's estate is empty of that bit.
Redmond Mahey spoils the powder key with his tongs at the Bristol shack, not back in Shoreham. Vito Pellegrin watches the bit die as a working key, and the door stays on Vito's own lock.
With Vito dead, Ada returns the powder key unused to Elena Pellegrin at the shack. The bit is not turned in the lock and not spoiled on the hill.
With Vito dead, Elena watches Redmond Mahey spoil the powder key at the shack. The estate's bit cannot open the Bristol door afterward.
With Redmond Mahey dead, Ada uses the powder key under Vito's eye at the Bristol shack. The door opens, and there is no smith left to unmake the bit.
With Redmond dead, the key is returned unused to Vito at the powder shack. It never opens the Bristol door and is not left in the estate coat.

rewards.detail: The powder-shack key from Rennet Moss's coat is used, returned unused to Vito, or spoiled, and that condition is the token of the hour.
A key beside powder at the Bristol shack is a safety problem Vito will not turn into a symbol, even when the bit arrived through Helen Perch's estate.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ellis dies in Ada Smollet's body before the choice, the key stays in Rennet Moss's coat. Vito Pellegrin finds no decision at the Bristol shack, and Redmond Mahey's tongs go home to Shoreham unused.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season ends with the key still in the coat from Helen Perch's estate. The powder shack above Bristol keeps its own lock, and nobody can say the bit was used, returned, or spoiled.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Ada's death does not put a settled key back into the coat. Used, returned unused, or spoiled by Redmond at the shack, the Bristol door remembers the choice and not the unfinished pocket.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Vito Pellegrin is dead, Elena Pellegrin meets Ada Smollet at the powder shack. She treats the key from Rennet Moss's coat as a safety matter the estate does not get to romanticize, and Redmond Mahey is still on the hill if the bit must die.

n_open.text: Vito is dead and the key is still in Rennet's coat, which is now your problem, Ada. I keep this shack's rules even when I am not the powder man. Helen does not get a vote from the grave. Use it on the Bristol door, put it in my hand unused, or let Redmond Mahey spoil it with those tongs. Pick before I decide you are decorating a danger.

choices.text: Give Elena the key, unused, for the shack.
Let Redmond spoil it while Elena watches.

n_end_vdead_ret.text: Unused, and mine. It does not go back into the coat, Ada, and it does not open this door in your hand. Redmond can walk down to Shoreham with cold tongs. I will not thank Helen's estate for a gift that could have met powder. Vito would have said the same without my manners.

n_end_vdead_spoil.text: Then it is ruined in front of me, and I will not ask Redmond Mahey to pretend the tongs were a prayer. The Bristol shack keeps Vito's lock. Ada, the coat can go back to being cloth. A spoiled key is quieter than a story about Helen Perch, and I prefer quiet near powder.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Redmond Mahey is dead, nobody has come up from Shoreham with tongs. Vito Pellegrin still treats the key as a safety problem at the powder shack, and the ruin of the bit, if it happens, is his decision on this hill rather than a smith's.

n_open.text: Redmond is dead, so do not look down the hill for Shoreham tongs, Ada. The key from Rennet Moss's coat is still next to my powder. Helen's estate is not a reason. Use it in front of me, return it unused, or let me ruin the bit myself on this Bristol sill. I will not make you a trip to a dead man's forge.

choices.text: Use the key once, with Vito watching the door.
Return the unused key to Vito at the sill.

n_end_rdead_use.text: Used, and I saw it. The shack opened, Ada, which is the safety problem arriving on schedule. There is no Redmond to spoil it afterward. I will change my habit around this door. Do not tell me the coat was only memory. A memory did not turn the lock. Your hand did.

n_end_rdead_ret.text: Back in my hand, unused. Redmond's absence does not make the coat braver, Ada. The key stays out of the lock and out of Helen's story. I will keep it where powder is a procedure. You can go down the Bristol hill without a bit in Rennet Moss's pocket.

endingImplications: The powder shack above Bristol either has been opened by the estate key, holds that key unused in Vito Pellegrin's care, or is rid of the bit because Redmond Mahey spoiled it on the hill. Later safety talk at the cut has one of those three facts and not a story about Helen.

title: The Face That Folds
summary: Pauline Ester is a geologist working the limestone cut above Bristol, not a visitor from a campus office. She wants a core from the face that shows the fold. That face has chalked names above it. She will move her bit if shown another face in plain stone language, without a ghost story.
discovery: Louis Pell comes up under the overhang and finds Pauline Ester already set up at the named face, bit still packed until someone answers her. The chalk is Gina Pellegrin's habit even when Gina is not the one holding the drill, and Pauline is asking the cut, not a lecture hall.

steps.playerAction: Meet Pauline Ester at the Bristol face she wants to core and look at the chalked names above the fold.
Tell her a safe face in plain stone words, refuse the core, or allow the name-face, without making her a villain for asking.
Leave her bit either moved, packed, or working under the names, and let the cut keep that answer.

n_open.text: I want the face that shows the fold, Louis, and I want you to hear me as a geologist standing in this Bristol cut, not as a thief from a college. The names in chalk are above the stone I need. Show me a different face that still has the turn in the beds, say it in rock and not in haunting, and I will move my bit. Or refuse me. Or allow this face. I can live with a clear no.

choices.text: Send her to the kinked beds with no chalk on them.
Refuse the core on every face of this cut.
Allow her to core the face under the chalked names.

textVariants.text: You keep looking at the chalk as if a name spoken were a wage, Louis Pell. I am not here to mock that. I am here for the fold in this Bristol limestone. If the names must stay unbored, say so, or show me another face in ordinary stone language. I will not drill through a sentence you are still trying to protect, and I will not pretend the fold is a soul.

n_mid_safe.text: Say it the way you just started to, in stone. If the east rib of this Bristol overhang shows the same fold and the chalk never climbed it, that is a face I can use. I do not need a story about who the names were. I need to know I am not coring a memorial by accident.

n_end_safe.text: Then I move. The east rib, where the beds kink and no chalk is written, is enough fold for my core. I am not insulted, Louis. You told me the difference without a ghost story, and my bit leaves the name-face alone. The limestone is still limestone. The names stay a reason to pick a hole, which is what I asked you for.

n_mid_refuse.text: All right. Hear me answer without sulking. A refusal is cleaner than a mystical warning. If Louis Pell, standing in this cut that knows his body, says no core at all, I pack the bit. I will not sneak a hole on the fold because the chalk offended me, and I will not call you superstitious for a boundary.

n_end_refuse.text: Packed. I am not coring the name-face and I am not coring a substitute. The fold can wait in the Bristol stone without my hole. You refused the work, Louis, and I am leaving the bit in the box so nobody later says the geologist took a silence for permission. The names are untouched because nothing was drilled.

n_mid_allow.text: If you allow it, I will core the fold and I will not pretend the chalk is invisible. The names stay above the hole, Louis. I am not scraping Gina Pellegrin's work to make my sample polite. Say the allowance again if you mean it. I do not want a shrug that Bristol can reinterpret later.

n_end_allow.text: Allowed, then. I core the face that shows the fold, names in chalk above the bit, and I will log it as limestone with a marble temper, not as a haunting. You gave permission, Louis Pell. I am grateful and I am not smug. The hole is a fact under the names, and the names are still the reason this hole needed a witness.

branches.summary: Pauline Ester moves her bit to a Bristol face that shows the fold without chalked names above it. Ellis explains the difference in plain stone language, and the name-face is not cored.
Coring is refused outright. Pauline Ester packs her bit and drills neither the chalked face nor another face at the Bristol cut. She accepts the no without being made a villain.
Ellis allows Pauline Ester to core the name-face at the Bristol cut. The chalked names stay above the hole, and she treats the stone as stone without mocking the names.
With Pauline Ester dead, Gina Pellegrin points any future core to an unchalked face of the Bristol fold and keeps the name-face off the bit.
With Pauline dead, Gina refuses coring at the Bristol cut. No safe-face invitation is made, and the chalked names are left without a hole under them.

rewards.detail: The fold Pauline Ester wants is a limestone fact at the Bristol cut, and it is not the same fact as the chalked names above one face.
Ellis either shows a safe face in plain stone language, refuses the core, or allows the name-face, and Pauline is left a scientist rather than an enemy.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ellis dies in Louis Pell's body before answering, Pauline Ester's bit stays packed. She does not core the name-face on a silence, and the Bristol fold remains unsampled.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season moves on with her bit still packed. No safe face was named and no permission was given, so the chalked names above the Bristol fold never share a hole with a core.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Louis Pell's death does not unpack a refusal or move a bit that was already shifted. The Bristol face Pauline was allowed, or the east rib, or the packed box, stays the answer she heard.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Pauline Ester is dead, no geologist is waiting with a bit. Gina Pellegrin, who chalks the names, decides whether any later core is invited onto a safe face or refused at the Bristol overhang.

n_open.text: Pauline Ester is dead, Louis, so the bit is not hers to aim. I chalked the names above the fold on this Bristol face. If some later hand wants stone, I can point them at beds that kink without my chalk, in plain words, or I can say this cut is not taking cores. I will not invent a ghost story to do either job.

choices.text: Have Gina name a face that is only stone.
Have Gina refuse cores at the named cut.

n_end_pdead_safe.text: Then the safe face is the east rib, beds turned, no names. Anybody who comes after Pauline can core that and leave my chalk alone. I said it in stone, Louis, not in a haunting. The Bristol fold does not need a dead geologist to be real, and the names do not need a hole to stay true.

n_end_pdead_refuse.text: Then no. The bit stays packed and I do not offer a substitute rib. Pauline is not here to be disappointed, Louis, and I will not core the names to feel scientific in her absence. The overhang keeps the fold and the chalk. Bristol can study both with its eyes.

endingImplications: The Bristol cut either loses a core from an unchalked face, loses no core at all, or carries a hole under the names Pauline Ester was shown. She leaves without being the villain of the fold, and later geology of this stone has a witness for which face was touched.

title: The Extra Envelopes
summary: On the Starksboro porch, Céline Boucher keeps envelopes for men the flood took before they could be hired, and a separate pile for a week last month when nobody worked. She will not mix the piles and smile. Marc Boucher's handwriting can make a lie look beautiful. Ada Smollet has to pick memorial or fraud.
discovery: Ada Smollet is asked onto the Starksboro porch where the envelopes come when the Bristol shack is closed. Céline Boucher has two piles on the rail and will not blur them for company. Marc is there with the pen that makes wages look owed.

steps.playerAction: Stand on the Starksboro porch and let Céline Boucher show the two piles without mixing them.
Choose to keep the envelopes as memorial, or stop them as fraud before Marc's hand makes a week of no work look paid.
Leave the piles in the category you defended, and do not ask either Boucher to smile over a blend.

n_open.text: These envelopes on the Starksboro rail are for men the flood took before they could be hired, Ada. This other pile is a week last month when nobody worked. I will not mix them in front of you and smile. Marc can write a name so beautifully it starts to look like a debt. Tell me whether you are here to keep a memorial or to stop a fraud. I will not do both with one face.

choices.text: Keep the unhired dead as memorial, not as pay.
Stop the envelopes before they become a fraud.

textVariants.text: You look ready to spare me a kind lie, Ada Smollet, and I am telling you not to. The Starksboro porch has a memorial pile and a week nobody worked. If you blur them so I can stay gentle, Marc's beautiful hand will finish the job. I would rather you be rude and clear than kind and mixed.

n_mid_memorial.text: Then I do not write the empty week as if it were owed. I can letter a memorial name without making it a wage, Ada, but only if my mother keeps the piles apart. Beautiful handwriting is how a fraud gets dressed. If this is memory, the Starksboro ink stays memory, and the week nobody worked stays blank.

n_end_memorial.text: Memorial, then, and not a smile over a mixture. The flood's unhired men stay envelopes we do not cash, and last month's idle week is not paid in Marc's pretty hand. You picked a category, Ada. I can live in it. The porch will not pretend a memorial is payroll, and payroll will not borrow the dead to look generous.

n_mid_fraud.text: Then the pen stops. I will not write a beautiful lie for a week nobody worked, and I will not let a memorial pile learn how to look like money. Ada, if you are stopping a fraud, say it so my mother hears the category. I am tired of being the hand that makes Starksboro feel generous.

n_end_fraud.text: Stopped. I will not call you cruel for it, Ada, and I will not mix the piles now to soften the stopping. Marc's hand does not get to make the idle week beautiful, and the flood envelopes do not get to masquerade as wages either. Fraud is the word you picked. The drawer can hold paper. It will not hold a trick.

branches.summary: The extra envelopes on the Starksboro porch are kept as memorial for men the flood took before hiring. Marc does not beautify the unworked week into a wage, and the piles stay unmixed.
Ellis stops the extra envelopes as fraud. Marc Boucher does not write the unworked week into a beautiful debt, and Céline does not keep a memorial that behaves like pay on the Starksboro porch.
With Céline dead, Marc keeps the Starksboro envelopes as memorial. His handwriting does not turn the unworked week or the unhired dead into pay.
With Céline dead, Marc stops the envelope practice as fraud. He refuses to beautify either pile on the Starksboro porch into something that looks owed.
With Marc dead, Céline keeps the envelopes as memorial on the Starksboro porch. The piles stay unmixed and unpaid, with no beautiful handwriting to disguise them.
With Marc dead, Céline stops the extra envelopes as fraud. Neither the flood pile nor the unworked week continues as a thing that could be mistaken for wages.

rewards.detail: The Starksboro envelopes are recorded either as memorial for the unhired flood dead or as a fraud that was stopped before it paid an idle week.
Ellis chooses a category Céline will not blur: memory that is not pay, or a stop that refuses Marc Boucher's beautiful lie.

deathTransition.ifEllisDiesMidQuest: If Ellis dies in Ada Smollet's body on the porch, the piles stay mixed in the drawer. Céline Boucher does not get a category, and Marc's hand is left with a beautiful ambiguity.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfUnresolved: The season passes with the Starksboro piles mixed in the drawer. No one can say the flood envelopes were memorial only, and the unworked week is still close enough to a wage to be written pretty.
deathTransition.onEraAdvanceIfResolved: Ada's death does not remix a choice already made. Memorial or fraud-stopped, the Starksboro drawer keeps the category Ellis spoke, and the piles are not blended back into a smile.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Céline Boucher is dead, Marc Boucher is left with both piles and the pen on the Starksboro porch. He knows his own handwriting can counterfeit a wage, and Ada has to choose the category without the widow's hard sorting.

n_open.text: My mother is dead and the piles are still on this Starksboro porch, Ada. One is men the flood took before a hiring. One is a week nobody worked. I can make either look beautiful, which is the danger. Keep them as memorial, unmixed and unpaid, or stop the whole habit as fraud. I will not smile and blend them just because she is gone.

choices.text: Tell Marc to keep the piles as unpaid memorial.
Tell Marc to stop writing the extra envelopes.

n_end_cdead_memorial.text: Memorial, and my hand stays plain. The flood names are not wages, Ada, and the idle week is not a debt I will letter into beauty. Starksboro can remember them without cashing them. I will not mix the piles to feel like her. Céline hated that trick, and her absence does not license it.

n_end_cdead_fraud.text: Then I stop. No beautiful fraud, no memorial that spends like a wage. The piles can sit until someone braver than a pen destroys the habit, but I will not add a name, Ada. Starksboro has had enough of my mother's categories filtered through my handwriting. Fraud is stopped where the ink would have begun.

ifNpcDead.resolution: If Marc Boucher is dead, the beautiful hand is gone. Céline Boucher still will not mix the piles on the Starksboro porch, and Ada's choice is memorial or fraud without a son to make the lie look like craftsmanship.

n_open.text: Marc is dead, so nobody here can write a lie prettier than my bookkeeping, Ada. The Starksboro piles remain what they were: flood dead who were never hired, and a week last month with no work in it. I will not mix them and smile to honor him. Memorial or fraud. Choose the word, and I will keep the drawer as blunt as his absence.

choices.text: Keep Céline's piles as memorial and unpaid.
Have Céline stop the piles as fraud.

n_end_mdead_memorial.text: Memorial, without Marc's hand to decorate it. The unhired dead stay remembered, Ada, and the idle week stays a blank, not a wage. I will not mix the piles because grief is in the house. Starksboro can stand a plain envelope. It does not need a beautiful fraud to feel decent.

n_end_mdead_fraud.text: Stopped, and I will not use my dead son as a reason to keep writing. The fraud was the risk that a memorial would learn to be pay. Ada, both piles come out of the wage habit. The Starksboro drawer can hold old paper. It will not hire a shadow, and it will not pay a week nobody worked.

endingImplications: Starksboro either keeps a memorial that is not payroll, or it stops the extra envelopes as fraud. Marc Boucher's handwriting is not allowed to make the idle week look owed, and later arguments about quarry mercy have to live inside the category that was picked on the porch.

title: The Notch Slide
summary: A slide sits on the Lincoln gap approach where the school-bus road and the quarry lane diverge. Rita Cole has one loader window before the next rain. She does not want the flood book. She wants a minute of Hannah Greer's mouth: bus first, or the lane toward the Bristol cut first.
discovery: Hannah Greer comes up into the Lincoln notch because the road is shut with mud and rock, not because a page sent her. Rita Cole is on the loader with one dry window of work, and the school-bus road and the quarry lane are both waiting on a sentence.

steps.playerAction: Stand in the Lincoln slide with Rita Cole and look at the bus road and the quarry lane without opening the flood book.
Use the minute of mouth to put the school bus first or the quarry lane first.
Leave Rita the order she can drive, and do not stay to revise it into a lesson after the loader moves.

n_open.text: Bus road or quarry lane, Hannah. This is the Lincoln gap, the slide is in both throats, and I have one loader window before the rain comes back. Your flood book is not on the machine. Your mouth is. Give me the order in the next minute. I have heard every speech about who matters. I need a road.

choices.text: Clear the school-bus road before the quarry lane.
Clear the quarry lane before the school-bus road.

textVariants.text: If the living come first with you, Hannah Greer, then say the school-bus road and stop circling the quarry lane as if Bristol stone could stand in the rain and argue. I still only have one loader window on this Lincoln slide. The book stays in your coat. The minute is the whole decision I can spend.

n_mid_bus.text: Bus first. Say it once more so the Lincoln hill hears a person and not a mood. I will take the loader to the school road and leave the quarry lane choked until the window is gone. The cut above Bristol can wait on stone. Children cannot wait on a speech I already refused to hear.

n_end_bus.text: Bus road first. That is the minute, Hannah, and I am spending it. The quarry lane stays closed while I open the way the school bus uses. Do not hand me the flood book as a blessing. Lincoln will remember the order if the rain lets the work stand, and it will remember you said the children before the cut.

n_mid_quarry.text: Quarry lane first, then. I hope you can hear how that sounds on a school morning in Lincoln. I will still do it if it is your minute. The loader window does not have room for both, and the Bristol cut's trucks do not become children because the stone is old. You said the lane. I am not translating it into kindness.

n_end_quarry.text: Quarry lane first. The school-bus road waits behind this slide while I open the way toward the cut. Hannah Greer, that was a mouth's decision, not a chapter. If Lincoln asks me why the bus sat, I will say you chose the lane in the minute you had. I will not invent a better reason after the rain.

branches.summary: Rita Cole clears the school-bus road first at the Lincoln slide. The quarry lane toward the cut waits, and the flood book is not what decided that one opening of the loader.
Rita Cole clears the quarry lane first. The Lincoln school-bus road stays blocked through the loader window, and Ellis owns that order in speech rather than in the flood book.
With Rita Cole dead, Gina carries Hannah's order that the Lincoln school-bus road is cleared before the quarry lane. The flood book stays out of the decision.
With Rita dead, Gina carries the order to clear the quarry lane before the Lincoln school-bus road. She does not rewrite Hannah's minute into something kinder to the children.

Rita Cole has one loader window before the next rain, and the flood book is not a tool that fits on the machine at the Lincoln gap.
